exercises: Exercise 1 – Vocabulary practice: Complete the Quizlet set 'Hobbys & Freizeit A1 Week 9' (20 cards). Study using the 'Learn' mode for at least 15 minutes. Screenshot your score and bring it to the next class.

Exercise 2 – Writing task: Write a short paragraph (6–8 sentences) titled 'Meine Freizeit' describing your real leisure activities. Use at least 3 different verbs, 3 different frequency adverbs, and include one sentence with 'gern' and one with 'nicht gern'. Use the writing frame from class as a scaffold.

Exercise 3 – Listening task: Watch the YouTube video 'Was machst du in deiner Freizeit? – Deutschlernen A1' (teacher provides link or QR code). Answer 3 comprehension questions on the handout: (a) Welche Hobbys nennt Person 1? (b) Geht Person 2 oft ins Kino? (c) Was macht Person 3 am Wochenende?

formative: Observation of pair and mingle activities: teacher uses a simple checklist to note whether learners correctly conjugate verbs in ich- and du-form during spoken interactions
Collected 'Mein Freizeitprofil' writing samples: teacher reviews for correct verb placement, frequency adverb position, and vocabulary range — written feedback provided at next session
Thumbs Up/Down comprehension check during Session 2 warm-up review to identify vocabulary retention gaps

Exit ticket (last 3 minutes of Session 2): learners write 2 sentences on a sticky note — one about what they do in their free time (ich) and one about their partner (er/sie) — assessing third-person conjugation transfer
assessment.summative: End-of-unit speaking and writing mini-assessment (administered in Week 10, first 15 minutes): Learners receive a picture prompt card showing a person engaged in various leisure activities. Task 1 (speaking, 2 minutes): Describe the person's hobbies using at least 4 sentences with frequency adverbs. Task 2 (writing, 10 minutes): Write a 5–7 sentence paragraph about your own Freizeit using vocabulary and grammar from Week 9. Assessment rubric covers: vocabulary accuracy and range (4 points), verb conjugation accuracy (3 points), frequency adverb usage (2 points), overall communicative clarity (1 point). Total: 10 points.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a laminated reference card with the 20 target vocabulary items (with Vietnamese translations and sample sentences) that learners may keep on their desk throughout all activities. Reduce the writing task to 4 sentences with a heavily scaffolded frame (e.g., 'Ich _____ gern _____. Ich _____ manchmal _____.') For the mingle activity, allow struggling learners to work with a stronger peer in a supported triad rather than independently. During conjugation practice, use a color-coded verb chart (ich-form in blue, du-form in red) to visually reinforce patterns. Offer additional pronunciation support for ch/sch sounds using short drill videos with Vietnamese-language explanations if available.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to write 10+ sentences in the Freizeitprofil task, incorporating negation with 'nicht' and 'kein', and experimenting with time expressions like 'am Wochenende', 'jeden Tag', 'einmal pro Woche'. During the mingle activity, encourage them to ask follow-up questions beyond the model (e.g., 'Warum magst du das?' — even if they cannot fully answer yet, productive struggle is encouraged). As an extension, ask them to research one German-speaking hobby club (Verein) online and present 2–3 sentences about it (in German) to the class at the start of the next session. They may also begin exploring the gern/lieber/am liebsten comparison gradient as a preview of Week 11 content.

review_from_previous: Week 5 – Days of the week (Wochentage): reactivated through expressions like 'Am Montag spiele ich Fußball'
Week 4 – Present tense conjugation of regular verbs (spielen, machen, hören): core grammar recycled throughout all activities
Week 6 – Definite and indefinite articles with nouns: recycled when learners use 'das Hobby', 'die Musik', 'ein Buch'
Week 7 – Modal verb mögen (ich mag / ich mag nicht): explicitly contrasted with 'gern' construction to build preference expression repertoire
Week 8 – Negation with 'nicht' and 'kein': briefly recycled in sentence construction exercises
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 10 will focus on 'Tagesablauf & Uhrzeiten' (Daily Routines and Telling the Time). The bridge from Week 9 is natural: learners will extend their Freizeit sentences by adding time expressions — 'Ich spiele um 18 Uhr Fußball' or 'Am Abend höre ich Musik.' The frequency adverbs learned this week will recur in daily routine descriptions. Additionally, separable verbs (aufstehen, aufräumen, fernsehen) will be introduced — learners have already encountered 'fernsehen' as a hobby this week, creating a memorable anchor for the separable verb concept.

learning_objectives: Can describe current weather conditions using simple phrases such as 'Es ist sonnig' or 'Es regnet'
Can name the four seasons in German and associate them with basic weather vocabulary
Can ask and answer simple questions about the weather, e.g., 'Wie ist das Wetter heute?'
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic verb conjugation in present tense (sein, haben)
Numbers 1–31 for dates (introduced in Week 6)
Days of the week and months (introduced in Week 7)
Basic adjective use without declension (e.g., 'Das Wetter ist schön')
Simple question formation with W-Fragewörter (was, wie, wann)

sessions.title: Das Wetter heute – Wetterbeschreibungen einführen

activities.title: Wetter-Bingo
activities.description: Each learner receives a 3x3 bingo card with weather icons (sun, rain, snow, cloud, wind, fog, storm, warm, cold). The teacher calls out German weather words ('sonnig', 'regnerisch', 'schneit', etc.) and learners mark the corresponding icon. The first to complete a row calls 'Bingo!' and must say the three weather words aloud to win. This activates visual association and phonemic awareness from the outset.
materials: Printed 3x3 Bingo cards with weather icons
Teacher call-out list of weather vocabulary

activities.title: Wetterkarte Deutschland – Vokabeln kennenlernen
activities.description: Teacher displays a large weather map of Germany (similar to a TV forecast) on the projector. Introduce 12 core weather vocabulary items with visuals and audio: sonnig, bewölkt, regnerisch, windig, neblig, stürmisch, es schneit, es regnet, heiß, warm, kühl, kalt. For each word, teacher models pronunciation, learners repeat chorally, then individually. Special attention given to vowel sounds 'ü' in 'kühl' and 'ö' in 'bewölkt', which are challenging for Vietnamese speakers. Teacher writes each word on the board with a phonetic Vietnamese-friendly hint (e.g., 'kühl' ≈ 'kuy-l'). Vietnamese contrast: Vietnamese weather vocabulary is often compound nouns; German uses adjectives + 'es ist' structure, which is highlighted explicitly.
materials: Projected weather map of Germany (printed backup available)
Flashcards with weather icons and German labels

activities.title: Satzstruktur: 'Es ist...' und 'Es regnet/schneit'
activities.description: Teacher introduces two key sentence patterns on the board: (1) 'Es ist + Adjektiv' (Es ist sonnig. / Es ist kalt.) and (2) impersonal verb constructions 'Es regnet.' / 'Es schneit.' / 'Es ist bewölkt.' Learners receive a structured gap-fill handout with 10 sentences featuring weather icons as picture prompts. They must choose the correct sentence structure and insert the appropriate weather word. Teacher circulates and monitors. Explicit grammar note: 'es' is an impersonal subject — no direct equivalent in Vietnamese, so this is flagged with a short L1 comparison note on the handout.

activities.title: Wie ist das Wetter? – Partnerdialog
activities.description: Learners work in pairs. Each pair receives a set of 6 weather picture cards (showing different weather scenarios). Partner A picks a card without showing Partner B and says the weather; Partner B must draw or point to the matching icon. Then they swap roles. After two rounds, pairs practice the mini-dialogue: A: 'Wie ist das Wetter heute?' B: 'Es ist [Adjektiv] und [Adjektiv].' or 'Es regnet.' Teacher provides a model dialogue on the board as a scaffold. Encourage use of 'und' to combine two weather descriptors.
materials: Weather picture card sets (6 cards per pair)

activities.title: Wetter-Schnappschuss
activities.description: Teacher shows 5 photos of different weather scenarios in German-speaking cities (Berlin im Schnee, Wien im Regen, Zürich bei Sonne, etc.). Learners call out a sentence describing each photo. Teacher corrects pronunciation and structure in real time. Brief recap: teacher asks 'Was haben wir heute gelernt?' and elicits vocabulary from volunteers. Homework is introduced.
materials: Projected weather photos from DACH cities

sessions.title: Die Jahreszeiten – Seasons, Temperatures & Simple Descriptions

activities.title: Hausaufgaben-Check & Wetter-Kurzbericht
activities.description: Learners pair up for 3 minutes to compare their homework weather diary entries (from Handout 10B). Each learner reads one sentence aloud to their partner. Two volunteers share with the class. Teacher gives brief corrective feedback on 'es ist' vs. verb constructions. This recycles Session 1 vocabulary and builds accountability.

activities.title: Die vier Jahreszeiten – Einführung mit Bildern und Lied
activities.description: Teacher presents the four seasons using a colorful illustrated poster: der Frühling (spring), der Sommer (summer), der Herbst (autumn), der Winter (winter). Key sentence frames introduced: 'Im Frühling ist es warm und sonnig.' 'Im Sommer ist es heiß.' 'Im Herbst ist es kühl und windig.' 'Im Winter ist es kalt und es schneit.' Grammar focus: 'im' = in dem (contracted dative preposition with masculine/neuter nouns). Teacher explicitly explains that all four seasons are masculine (der), so always 'im Frühling/Sommer/Herbst/Winter'. Class listens to a short authentic German children's song about seasons ('Alle meine Jahreszeiten' or similar). Teacher plays once for pleasure, then plays again while learners identify season names they hear.
materials: Jahreszeiten illustrated poster (A3 printed or projected)

activities.title: Jahreszeiten-Zuordnung und Satzbildung
activities.description: Learners receive a worksheet (Handout 10D) with three tasks: (1) Match 8 weather adjectives to the correct season (multiple answers possible, encourages discussion). (2) Unscramble 4 sentences about seasons (e.g., 'kalt / Im / es / Winter / ist' → 'Im Winter ist es kalt.'). (3) Write 2 original sentences about any two seasons using the model. Learners work individually for 7 minutes, then check with a partner. Teacher reviews answers whole-class and addresses common Vietnamese learner errors: omitting 'es', incorrect adjective order.

activities.title: Meine Lieblingsjahreszzeit – Gruppeninterview
activities.description: Groups of 3–4 learners. Each learner prepares 2 sentences: (1) 'Meine Lieblingsjahreszzeit ist der/die/das... [Jahreszeit]' — teacher clarifies grammatically it remains 'der Frühling' etc. even after 'ist'. (2) One reason using 'weil' is previewed passively: 'Ich mag den Sommer. Es ist heiß und sonnig.' (avoid 'weil' clause for A1, use parataxis). Each group member shares their answer; others listen and note which season their partner prefers. Groups report back: 'Jana mag den Winter.' This introduces 3rd person singular conjugation recycling from Week 4. Teacher provides a sentence frame card for support.
materials: Sentence frame support card (one per table)
Simple note-taking grid for group report

activities.title: Exit Ticket: Wetter und Jahreszeiten
activities.description: Each learner receives a half-sheet exit ticket with 3 tasks to complete in 5 minutes: (1) Write the German name for the season shown in a picture. (2) Write a weather sentence for that picture. (3) Answer: 'Welche Jahreszeit magst du?' in one sentence. Teacher collects tickets to assess comprehension before next session. Learners also receive the weekly homework sheet.
materials: Exit ticket half-sheets with seasonal images (Handout 10E)

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Impersonal 'es' constructions (Es ist + Adjektiv; Es regnet / Es schneit) and the preposition 'im' + Jahreszeit (contracted dative: in + dem = im) with masculine nouns; recycling present tense verb conjugation (sein, mögen) in weather context
lesson_plans.cultural_note: Weather is a quintessential small-talk topic in German-speaking countries (DACH region). Germans, Austrians, and Swiss often open conversations with 'Schönes Wetter heute, oder?' In Germany, weather is notoriously unpredictable — especially in the north (Hamburg) — and locals take pride in being prepared with an umbrella ('Regenschirm') year-round. The concept of 'Schmuddelwetter' (grey, drizzly, unpleasant weather) is a culturally recognized and frequently used term. In contrast, Vietnamese learners may be unfamiliar with snow as a daily reality: the first snowfall of winter (especially in Munich or Vienna) is a cultural and emotional event for locals. The 'Aprilwetter' expression ('April weather') refers to unpredictably changeable weather and is widely used as a metaphor. In Switzerland, the 'Föhn' (a warm, dry Alpine wind) is a regionally specific phenomenon that can cause headaches and mood changes — locals even use it as an excuse for feeling unwell.

homework.description: Learners complete a 5-day personal weather diary in German (Handout 10F). Each day, they observe the weather in their Vietnamese city and write 2–3 sentences using the sentence frames learned in class. Additionally, they complete a short online matching exercise (linked via QR code on handout) reviewing weather vocabulary. Finally, they find one photo online of a DACH city in any season and prepare to describe it in 2 sentences in the next class.
exercises: 5-day weather diary: Write 2–3 sentences per day describing the weather in your city using 'Es ist...' and/or 'Es regnet/schneit' (Handout 10F, Section A)
Online vocabulary matching exercise: Match 10 German weather words to their images (QR code on Handout 10F, estimated 10 minutes)
Photo task: Find one photo of a German-speaking city in any season. Write 2 German sentences about the weather visible in the photo and be ready to share it in class

formative: Observation during Wetter-Bingo for phonemic recognition of weather vocabulary
Monitoring of pair dialogue activity in Session 1 for correct 'Es ist...' and 'Es regnet/schneit' usage
Partner check of gap-fill handout (Handout 10A) with peer correction
Exit ticket (Handout 10E) collected at end of Session 2: reviewed by teacher to identify misconceptions before next lesson
Group report-back in Gruppeninterview activity for 3rd person singular accuracy
assessment.summative: End-of-week short quiz (10 minutes, administered at start of Week 11): (1) Label 6 weather icons with the correct German word (6 points). (2) Write a complete sentence for each of the 4 seasons using 'Im [Jahreszeit] ist es...' (8 points). (3) Respond in writing to 'Wie ist das Wetter heute?' and 'Was ist deine Lieblingsjahreszzeit?' with one sentence each (4 points). Total: 18 points. Pass mark: 12/18.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a vocabulary reference card (Handout 10G) with weather words, icons, and phonetic guides using familiar Vietnamese sounds for difficult German phonemes (ü, ö, ä). Allow learners to use the card during all activities except the summative quiz. During pair work, pair struggling learners with a supportive peer rather than isolating them. For the weather diary homework, reduce requirement to 3 days instead of 5. Offer a partially completed diary template with sentence starters ('Heute ist das Wetter ___. Es ist ___.') to scaffold writing. In class, seat these learners closest to the teacher for more immediate support.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to extend their season sentences with a second clause using 'und' or 'aber' (e.g., 'Im Winter ist es kalt, aber ich mag Schnee.'). Introduce the passive vocabulary item 'die Wettervorhersage' (weather forecast) and ask them to write a 3-sentence mini weather forecast for a German city of their choice. Extension task: research and present in 4 sentences (one per season) how the climate in Vietnam differs from Germany, using vocabulary from this week. Advanced learners may also begin exploring comparative structures ('Im Sommer ist es heißer als im Frühling') as a preview of A2 grammar.

review_from_previous: Week 7 – Months and days of the week: recycled by associating seasons with months (e.g., 'Im Dezember ist es Winter.')
Week 6 – Numbers 1–31: temperatures introduced as a passive extension (e.g., 'Es ist 30 Grad.')
Week 4 – Present tense conjugation of 'sein' and 'mögen': activated in 'Es ist kalt' and 'Ich mag den Sommer'
Week 3 – Basic adjectives and 'das ist': extended to impersonal 'es ist' structure in weather context
Week 8 – Everyday routines: revisited briefly by asking 'Was machst du im Sommer?' to bridge weather with activities
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 11 will introduce clothing vocabulary ('die Kleidung') and the modal verb 'müssen' (e.g., 'Im Winter muss ich einen Mantel tragen.'). The weather and seasons vocabulary from Week 10 provides the natural contextual bridge — dressing appropriately for the weather directly links the two topics and gives learners a motivating communicative purpose for learning clothing items.

learning_objectives: Can name at least 15 common professions in German and use correct articles (der/die) for each
Can ask and answer simple questions about jobs using 'Was bist du von Beruf?' and 'Ich bin + profession'
Can describe a job in one or two simple sentences using basic verbs such as arbeiten, helfen, lehren, and verkaufen
prerequisite_knowledge: Definite and indefinite articles: der, die, das, ein, eine (Week 2–3)
Present tense conjugation of sein and haben (Week 4)
Present tense of regular verbs: machen, arbeiten, wohnen (Week 5–6)
Personal pronouns: ich, du, er, sie, wir, ihr, sie/Sie (Week 3)
Basic question words: Was, Wer, Wo, Wie (Week 4–5)
Numbers 1–100 for expressing work hours or salary context (Week 7)
Basic vocabulary for places in the city: Büro, Schule, Krankenhaus (Week 10)

sessions.title: Welche Berufe kennst du? – Introducing Professions

activities.title: Bilder-Rateспiel – Guess the Job
activities.description: The teacher displays 8 flashcard images of people doing recognizable jobs (doctor, teacher, chef, police officer, engineer, nurse, shop assistant, driver) on the board or projector. Learners look at the images and try to write in Vietnamese what they think each person does. Then teacher reveals the German word for each profession, writes it on the board with the article (der Arzt / die Ärztin, der Lehrer / die Lehrerin, etc.), and learners compare with their Vietnamese guesses. This activates prior world knowledge and bridges L1 to L2. Teacher explicitly points out the masculine/feminine distinction in German professions, noting this does not exist in Vietnamese, flagging it as a key learning point.
materials: Flashcard image set (8 profession images, printed or digital slideshow)
Mini whiteboards or scrap paper for learners

activities.title: Vokabelliste – 15 Berufe mit Artikel
activities.description: Teacher distributes a structured vocabulary handout listing 15 professions with masculine and feminine forms, the definite article, a simple Vietnamese translation gloss, and a small picture icon. Teacher models pronunciation of each word using the listen-and-repeat technique. Special phonetic attention is given to sounds difficult for Vietnamese learners: the German 'r' in 'Arzt', the 'ä' in 'Ärztin', the 'sch' in 'Schüler', and the 'z' sound in 'Polizist'. Teacher drills pronunciation using choral repetition, then row repetition, then individual nomination. Teacher then writes on the board the rule: masculine job title → add -in for feminine form (Lehrer → Lehrerin), noting exceptions like Arzt → Ärztin (umlaut change). Learners annotate their handout with the rule.
materials: Vocabulary handout A5 with 15 professions, articles, Vietnamese glosses, and pictures
Audio recording of native speaker pronunciation (optional MP3 file)

activities.title: Artikel-Sortierung – Sorting der / die
activities.description: Learners receive a cut-up card sort activity with 12 profession words (no articles). They must sort the cards into two columns on their desk: 'der (männlich)' and 'die (weiblich)'. After 3 minutes working individually, they compare answers with a partner. Teacher then conducts whole-class feedback using the board. Teacher highlights the important rule that in German, when stating your profession after 'sein', no article is used: 'Ich bin Arzt' (not 'Ich bin ein Arzt'), contrasting this with English and explaining via Vietnamese gloss. This is a common error point for Vietnamese learners influenced by English instruction.
materials: Cut-up card sort sets (one set per learner pair)
Answer key displayed on board or projector

activities.title: Dialog-Modell – Was bist du von Beruf?
activities.description: Teacher presents a short model dialogue on the board and reads it aloud twice while learners follow along on their handout. Dialogue A: 'Hallo! Ich heiße Minh. Was bist du von Beruf?' Dialogue B: 'Ich bin Ingenieur. Und du?' Dialogue A: 'Ich bin Lehrerin.' Teacher then elicits the structure from learners: 'Was bist du von Beruf?' → 'Ich bin + [Beruf ohne Artikel].' Teacher drills the question-answer pattern using substitution: teacher points to a profession image and nominates a learner to answer 'Ich bin…'. After several rounds, learners practice in pairs using their vocabulary handout as a reference. Each pair completes at least 4 exchanges. Teacher circulates to monitor pronunciation and article omission after 'sein'.
materials: Profession flashcard images displayed on board

sessions.title: Wo arbeitet er? Was macht sie? – Jobs in Context

activities.title: Schnelle Wiederholung – Quick Vocabulary Recall Race
activities.description: Teacher shows profession images one by one on the projector. The first learner to call out the correct German profession (with the right article: 'der Arzt!') wins a point for their side of the classroom. This creates a competitive, low-stress review of Session 1 vocabulary while energizing learners at the start of Session 2. Teacher keeps score on the board. After 8 images, teacher switches the task: teacher says a German profession word and learners must hold up a red card (die/feminine) or blue card (der/masculine) to practice article recognition. Vietnamese learners often find grammatical gender abstract; the physical card activity provides a kinesthetic anchor.
materials: Profession flashcard images (same set from Session 1)
Red and blue response cards (one pair per learner, pre-cut from colored paper)

activities.title: Wo arbeitet er/sie? – Workplaces and Job Verbs
activities.description: Teacher introduces 6 key workplace nouns (das Büro, das Krankenhaus, die Schule, das Restaurant, die Fabrik, das Geschäft) connecting them to professions already learned. Teacher builds simple sentences on the board: 'Der Arzt arbeitet im Krankenhaus.' 'Die Lehrerin arbeitet in der Schule.' Teacher draws attention to the contraction 'im' (in + dem, for masculine/neuter dative) using a simple color-coded grammar box on the board, noting this is a preview of dative case which will be covered in detail at A2. Teacher then introduces 5 key job-action verbs: arbeiten (to work), helfen (to help), lehren / unterrichten (to teach), verkaufen (to sell), fahren (to drive). Teacher conjugates 'arbeiten' fully on the board and reminds learners of the -e- insertion rule for verbs with stems ending in -t (arbeit-e-t). Learners copy the grammar box into their notebooks.
materials: Supplementary grammar card with 'im/in der' rule (one per learner)

activities.title: Sätze bauen – Sentence Building with Job Cards
activities.description: Learners receive an envelope containing word cards to build 5 sentences. Each sentence requires them to select the correct subject pronoun, profession, workplace, and verb. Example target sentence: 'Er ist Polizist. Er arbeitet bei der Polizei.' Learners physically arrange the word cards on their desks to form correct sentences, then write them into their notebooks. Teacher circulates and provides corrective feedback. Pairs then check answers against an answer key posted on the board. This activity specifically targets Vietnamese learners' tendency to omit the verb or use incorrect word order (Verb-Second rule in main clauses is reinforced here through physical manipulation before written production).
materials: Word card envelopes (one set per learner pair)
Answer key on board or projector

activities.title: Klassenumfrage – Job Survey
activities.description: Learners receive a survey grid with columns: Name, Beruf, Arbeitsort (workplace). They must stand up and mingle, asking at least 4 classmates (using fictional job identities written on a role card they received at the start): 'Was bist du von Beruf?' and 'Wo arbeitest du?' They record answers in the grid. Teacher monitors for correct question formation and 'Ich bin + Beruf (no article)' structure. After 7 minutes of mingling, learners sit and a volunteer reports back to the class: 'Lan ist Ärztin. Sie arbeitet im Krankenhaus.' This develops third-person present tense use. Teacher provides immediate corrective recasting for errors without halting communication flow. This communicative task simulates real-life workplace small talk which is culturally relevant for adult Vietnamese learners entering professional environments.
materials: Role cards (one per learner with a fictional German job identity)

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Present tense of regular verbs with job vocabulary; zero article after 'sein' with professions (Ich bin Arzt); masculine and feminine forms of profession nouns (Movierung: Lehrer → Lehrerin); Verb-Second (V2) word order in statements; introduction to 'im' (in + dem) for workplace location
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In DACH countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland), it is common to ask about someone's profession in social and professional contexts, though this is less common as an opener with strangers compared to some other cultures. In Germany, the dual Ausbildungssystem (vocational training system) is highly respected — trades like Mechatroniker or Tischler carry equal social prestige to university-educated professions, unlike in many parts of Vietnam where academic degrees are traditionally prioritized. Teachers should note that in Austria the word 'Hausfrau/Hausmann' (homemaker) is used and is considered a valid profession. In Switzerland, learners may encounter Swiss-German dialect words for some jobs (e.g., Coiffeur instead of Friseur). Gender-inclusive language is increasingly important in Germany: forms like 'Lehrer*in' or 'Lehrende' appear in official documents, though for A1 level the standard masculine/feminine pair is sufficient.

homework.description: Learners complete a structured written exercise practicing job vocabulary and sentence construction, then record a short audio self-introduction including their (real or fictional) profession.
exercises: Exercise 1 – Vocabulary gap fill: Complete 10 sentences with the correct profession word (with article where required). Example: 'Maria ist ______. Sie arbeitet im Krankenhaus.' (die Ärztin)
Exercise 2 – Masculine/Feminine pairs: Write the feminine form of 8 given masculine professions. Example: der Lehrer → die ______

Exercise 3 – Sentence writing: Write 5 original sentences about people in your family or neighborhood using the structure '[Name] ist [Beruf]. Er/Sie arbeitet [Ort].' Use at least 3 different professions from the week's vocabulary list.

Exercise 4 – Audio recording (voice memo on phone): Record a 30-second self-introduction in German: 'Ich heiße [Name]. Ich bin [Beruf]. Ich arbeite [Ort].' Submit via class messaging app or bring to next class for teacher feedback.

formative: Observation during the Artikel-Sortierung card sort (Session 1): Teacher notes which learners consistently confuse masculine/feminine forms and provides immediate targeted feedback
Monitoring during pair dialogue practice (Session 1): Teacher checks for correct omission of article after 'sein' (Ich bin Arzt, NOT Ich bin ein Arzt) and records errors on a class tracking sheet
Survey grid completion accuracy (Session 2): Teacher collects survey grids at end of class and scans for correct question formation and third-person conjugation

Exit ticket at end of Session 2: Learners write on a sticky note one thing they learned and one thing they are still unsure about (traffic light self-assessment: green/yellow/red dot sticker indicating confidence level)
assessment.summative: End-of-week speaking quiz (5 minutes per learner pair, conducted during the following class warm-up). Each pair receives a set of 3 profession image cards. Learner A asks 'Was ist er/sie von Beruf?' for each image; Learner B answers and adds a workplace sentence. Roles then switch. Assessment criteria: correct profession vocabulary (2 points each × 3), correct absence of article after 'sein' (2 points), correct verb conjugation (2 points), comprehensible pronunciation (2 points). Maximum 14 points. Pass threshold: 10/14. Results logged on teacher's running A1 progress tracker.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a word bank reference card throughout all activities so learners are not blocked by vocabulary retrieval. Reduce the vocabulary target list to the 8 most common professions (Arzt, Lehrer, Ingenieur, Koch, Polizist, Verkäufer, Fahrer, Kellner) and allow mastery of these before introducing the full list. Use Vietnamese translation glosses on all worksheets for this group. Pair struggling learners with more confident peers during mingle activities. During the sentence-building activity, provide a sentence frame card: 'Er/Sie ist ___. Er/Sie arbeitet ___.' For homework, allow Exercise 4 (audio recording) to be replaced with a written version if technology access is limited. Provide a phonetics guide for the top 5 most mispronounced profession words by Vietnamese speakers.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to use formal 'Sie' register in dialogues: 'Was sind Sie von Beruf?' and respond accordingly. Ask them to write a short paragraph (4–5 sentences) about a family member's job including workplace, typical tasks, and working hours using numbers reviewed from Week 7. Introduce the negation 'Ich bin kein Arzt / keine Ärztin' as an extension. During the survey activity, encourage advanced learners to add a question about working hours: 'Wie viele Stunden arbeitest du pro Woche?' In homework, add an optional extension: find one authentic German job advertisement online (e.g., from Stepstone.de or Indeed.de) and identify 3 German words they recognize from this week's vocabulary, then write 2 sentences about the job.

review_from_previous: Week 10 – Places in the city (Krankenhaus, Schule, Büro, Geschäft): recycled as workplaces in this week's context
Week 5–6 – Present tense conjugation of regular verbs: reactivated with new job-action verbs (arbeiten, verkaufen, fahren)
Week 4 – Verb 'sein': core structure for 'Ich bin + Beruf' reused and extended to third person (er ist, sie ist)
Week 7 – Numbers 1–100: briefly revisited in cultural note context (working hours) and optional advanced homework extension
Week 3 – Personal pronouns (er/sie/es): actively recycled in third-person descriptions during survey reporting phase
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 13 will build directly on Berufe & Arbeit by introducing 'Tagesablauf' (daily routine). Learners will use profession vocabulary as a contextual anchor to discuss what time professionals start work, what they do at different times of day, and how their schedules look. The verb 'arbeiten' will recur alongside new verbs like 'aufstehen', 'frühstücken', and 'schlafen'. Time expressions (um + Uhrzeit) and telling the time (die Uhrzeit) will be the new grammar focus, building on numbers already reviewed. This creates a natural topic progression from 'Who am I professionally?' to 'What does my professional day look like?'

learning_objectives: Can describe childhood memories using simple past tense (Präteritum) of 'sein' and 'haben' in short spoken and written sentences
Can talk about past habits and repeated actions in childhood using 'früher' + simple present or 'als Kind' constructions
Can understand and use at least 20 vocabulary items related to childhood, toys, family activities, and school life
prerequisite_knowledge: Present tense (Präsens) of regular and key irregular verbs (sein, haben, gehen, spielen)
Basic personal pronouns (ich, du, er, sie, wir, ihr, sie/Sie)
Numbers, ages, and basic time expressions (heute, gestern, immer, manchmal)
Basic family vocabulary (Mutter, Vater, Geschwister, Großeltern)
Simple sentence structure: Subject + Verb + Object/Complement

sessions.title: Früher und heute – Meine Kindheit

activities.title: Foto-Impuls: Kindheitsbilder
activities.description: Teacher displays 6–8 photographs on the projector showing typical German childhood scenes (e.g., playing outside, school, birthday party, toys from the 1990s–2000s). Learners look at the images and tell their partner in Vietnamese or simple German what they see and what memories the images remind them of. Teacher then elicits German vocabulary learners already know (e.g., Schule, spielen, Freunde) and writes them on the board. This activates prior knowledge and creates emotional engagement with the topic.
materials: Projector or printed photo cards (6–8 childhood scene images)

activities.title: Wortschatz: Kindheit – Themenfeld aufbauen
activities.description: Teacher introduces a visual mind map on the board with the central node 'Kindheit'. Four branches expand: 'Spiele & Spielzeug' (Puppe, Lego, Fußball, Verstecken spielen), 'Schule & Lernen' (Schulranzen, Hausaufgaben, Pause, Lehrer), 'Familie & Zuhause' (Oma, Opa, Haustier, Garten), 'Gefühle & Erlebnisse' (glücklich, aufgeregt, Abenteuer, Freundschaft). Teacher models pronunciation for each word using the listen-and-repeat method. Learners receive Handout 1 with the mind map skeleton and fill in the German words as they hear them. Vietnamese translations are provided in a glossary column on the right side of the handout to support comprehension without over-relying on L1.
materials: Handout 1: Kindheit Wortschatz Mind Map with glossary (Vietnamese translations)
Audio recording or teacher voice for pronunciation modeling

activities.title: Sortieraufgabe: Was gehört wohin?
activities.description: Learners receive Handout 2 with 16 jumbled childhood vocabulary words and must sort them into four categories (Spiele, Schule, Familie, Gefühle) by writing them into the correct column in a table. They then compare answers with a partner. Teacher conducts whole-class feedback and clarifies any confusion. This consolidates the new vocabulary through meaningful categorization rather than rote memorization.
materials: Handout 2: Vocabulary sorting table with 16 words

activities.title: Grammatik-Spotlight: war und hatte – Präteritum von sein und haben
activities.description: Teacher writes two parallel sentences on the board: 'Ich bin glücklich.' (Präsens) and 'Als Kind war ich glücklich.' (Präteritum). Teacher highlights 'war' in a different color and explains this is how German expresses the past with 'sein'. The same is done for 'haben' → 'hatte'. Teacher distributes Handout 3 which shows a clear conjugation table for 'war' and 'hatte' alongside a short Vietnamese-language grammar note explaining the concept of using Präteritum for 'sein' and 'haben' in narrative/descriptive past contexts (as opposed to Perfekt for other verbs, which will be introduced in Week 2). Learners practice orally in chorus: teacher says a pronoun, learners call out the correct form. Example sentences use childhood vocabulary just learned to create connected context.
materials: Handout 3: Konjugationstabelle war/hatte with Vietnamese grammar note

activities.title: Sätze über die Kindheit schreiben
activities.description: Learners complete 6 sentence starters on Handout 4 using 'war' or 'hatte' and choosing from a word bank. Example prompts: 'Als Kind war ich _____ (glücklich/schüchtern/aktiv).' / 'Mein Lieblingsspielzeug _____ eine Puppe.' / 'Ich _____ einen Hund.' Learners write their own answers making them personally true. After completing the written task, they share two of their sentences aloud with a partner. Teacher circulates and provides corrective feedback on form.
materials: Handout 4: Satzergänzung mit war/hatte (6 sentence starters + word bank)

sessions.title: Früher habe ich immer … – Gewohnheiten in der Kindheit

activities.title: Rückblick-Quiz: Wortschatz-Schnellrunde
activities.description: Teacher uses flashcard images (projected or printed) of 10 vocabulary items from Session 1. Learners call out the German word as quickly as possible. Then teacher says the German word and learners give a Vietnamese translation or mime the word. This spaced retrieval practice reinforces Session 1 vocabulary at the start of Session 2 and primes learners for the lesson.
materials: 10 flashcard images (digital or printed) from Session 1 vocabulary

activities.title: Hörtext: Interview – Kindheitserinnerungen
activities.description: Learners listen to a short, clearly spoken audio dialogue (approximately 90 seconds) in which a German woman named Sabine describes her childhood to a friend. The text is written at A2 level and includes: 'Als Kind war ich sehr aktiv. Ich hatte viele Freunde. Wir haben immer im Park gespielt. Früher hatte ich ein Fahrrad. Meine Oma war sehr nett. Wir haben oft Kuchen gebacken.' Pre-listening: teacher asks learners to predict what topics will come up (pair discussion, 1 minute). First listen: learners note down 3 things they understand (open notes). Second listen: learners complete a true/false comprehension task on Handout 5. Post-listening: whole-class discussion of answers with teacher explaining any misunderstood sections. Teacher draws attention to the expression 'früher' and 'immer' as key temporal markers for past habits.
materials: Audio file: Sabine Interview (teacher-recorded or text-to-speech at A2 pace)

activities.title: Früher … – Gewohnheiten ausdrücken
activities.description: Building on the listening text, teacher introduces the structure 'Früher + Verb (Präsens/Perfekt)' and 'Als Kind habe ich immer … gespielt' as common ways to express childhood habits. Teacher writes on the board: 'Früher habe ich jeden Tag Fußball gespielt.' and explains that Perfekt (haben + Partizip II) is used for most action verbs in spoken German past, while 'war' and 'hatte' stay as Präteritum. A simple reference chart on Handout 6 shows: sein → war, haben → hatte, all other verbs → Perfekt (preview only, full Perfekt treatment in Week 2). Teacher models 3 example sentences using childhood vocabulary. Learners are NOT expected to produce full Perfekt sentences independently yet; the focus remains on recognition and use of 'war', 'hatte', and 'früher' frames.
materials: Handout 6: Grammar reference chart (war/hatte vs. Perfekt overview)

activities.title: Interview: Wie war deine Kindheit?
activities.description: Learners receive Handout 7 containing an interview card with 6 questions about childhood: 1) Wo bist du aufgewachsen? / Wo warst du als Kind? 2) Hattest du Geschwister? 3) Was war dein Lieblingsessen als Kind? 4) Hattest du ein Haustier? 5) Wer war dein bester Freund / deine beste Freundin? 6) Was hast du als Kind am liebsten gemacht? Learner A interviews Learner B, taking notes on a response grid. Then they switch. After both interviews, each learner introduces their partner to another pair using third-person forms (Er/Sie war … Er/Sie hatte …). Teacher monitors for correct use of 'war' and 'hatte' and notes errors for group feedback. This activity is designed to be personally meaningful, encouraging authentic communication.
materials: Handout 7: Interview-Karte mit 6 Fragen und Notizraster
Optional: small recording device or phone for self-monitoring (advanced learners)

activities.title: Schreiben: Meine Kindheit – Ein kurzer Absatz
activities.description: As a consolidation task, learners write a short paragraph (5–7 sentences) about their own childhood using the structures and vocabulary from both sessions. A writing scaffold on Handout 8 provides: sentence starters ('Als Kind war ich …', 'Ich hatte …', 'Mein Lieblingsort war …', 'Früher habe ich oft … gemacht.'), a word bank of adjectives and nouns from the week's vocabulary, and a model paragraph by a fictional Vietnamese student 'Nam' for reference. Learners who finish early add a sentence about what is different now ('Heute bin ich … / Heute habe ich …'). Teacher collects paragraphs at the end for formative assessment.
materials: Handout 8: Schreibgerüst mit Satzanfängen, Wortbank und Modelltext

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Präteritum of 'sein' (war) and 'haben' (hatte) for describing past states and possessions in childhood narratives; use of temporal adverbials 'früher', 'als Kind', 'damals' to frame past context; introductory recognition of Perfekt with action verbs (production expected from Week 2 onward)
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland – DACH), childhood memories are often tied to outdoor play culture: Spielplatz (playground), Fahrradfahren, and seasonal activities like Karneval or Weihnachtsmarkt. Vietnamese learners may find it interesting that German children often start school (Grundschule) at age 6 with a big ceremony called 'Einschulung', where they receive a 'Schultüte' – a large decorated cone filled with sweets and small gifts. This tradition is unique to Germany and parts of Austria and Poland and makes the first day of school a celebrated family event. Discussing this difference with the Lễ Khai Giảng tradition in Vietnam can create meaningful cross-cultural reflection and motivate engagement with the topic.

homework.description: Learners complete two homework tasks to reinforce Session 1 and Session 2 content before the next class meeting. Task 1 is a written vocabulary task. Task 2 is a short personal writing task using the grammar structures from the week.
exercises: Task 1 – Wortschatz üben: Complete 10 fill-in-the-blank sentences using the correct form of 'war' or 'hatte'. Sentences are provided on Handout 9 (take-home). Example: 'Als Kind _____ ich sehr neugierig.' / 'Meine Schwester _____ eine Puppe.'

Task 2 – Schreiben: Write 8–10 sentences in a notebook or on paper about your own childhood. Use at least 5 vocabulary words from the week's list, the words 'früher' and 'als Kind' at least once each, and both 'war' and 'hatte' at least twice. Title: 'Meine Kindheit'
Task 3 (Optional/Advanced): Find one photograph from your childhood and write 3–5 German sentences describing it using the structures learned. Bring the photo or a phone photo to the next session.

formative: Teacher observation during pair interview activity (Session 2): monitor correct use of 'war' and 'hatte' in third-person introductions; note recurring errors for whole-class feedback
Vocabulary sorting task (Session 1, Handout 2): quick peer-check and teacher review to identify learners struggling with core vocabulary categorization
Collected written paragraph (Session 2, Handout 8): teacher reads and provides written feedback using a simple correction code (G = Grammar, W = Wrong word, ? = Unclear) before next session

Exit ticket: at the end of Session 2, each learner writes one sentence on a sticky note – 'Als Kind war ich _____ und ich hatte _____.' – and hands it to the teacher as they leave; teacher scans for accuracy
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (to be administered at the start of Week 2 as a 10-minute task): Learners read a short paragraph (6–8 sentences) about a fictional person's childhood and answer 5 comprehension questions; then write 4 sentences about their own childhood using 'war', 'hatte', and at least 3 vocabulary items from the week. Graded on accuracy of 'war'/'hatte' forms (50%), vocabulary range (25%), and sentence coherence (25%).

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a bilingual word list (German–Vietnamese) for all new vocabulary on every handout. Allow use of the conjugation reference card (Handout 3) during all speaking and writing tasks. During the interview activity, reduce the number of interview questions from 6 to 3 and provide pre-written sentence frames on a support card. For homework, allow Task 1 only (skip Task 2 or reduce to 4 sentences). Pair struggling learners with supportive peers during pair work. Consider pre-teaching the 5 most essential vocabulary words (war, hatte, früher, als Kind, spielen) using picture-word flashcards 10 minutes before the lesson starts.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Encourage use of 3–4 additional adjectives not on the word list during the interview activity. In the writing task, challenge them to include one Perfekt sentence with an action verb (e.g., 'Ich habe Fußball gespielt.') based on the grammar preview. For homework Task 3, ask them to record a 60-second voice memo describing their childhood photo and submit it via a messaging app. Additionally, ask them to research the German 'Schultüte' tradition and write 2–3 sentences in German comparing it to Vietnamese school traditions (Lễ Khai Giảng) as a cross-cultural extension task.

review_from_previous: Present tense verb conjugation (ich, du, er/sie/es forms) – recycled in contrast with new Präteritum forms
Basic family vocabulary (Mutter, Vater, Geschwister, Großeltern) – reactivated and extended with Oma, Opa, Haustier
Time expressions: heute, immer, manchmal – extended with früher, damals, als Kind, jeden Tag
Simple sentence structure Subject + Verb + Object – applied in new past-tense contexts
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 2 will expand past tense production to include the Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip II) for action verbs, allowing learners to tell fuller stories about specific childhood events rather than just states and possessions. The vocabulary of Week 1 will serve as the content basis for Week 2 narrative sentences, ensuring continuity and meaningful recycling.

learning_objectives: Can describe common symptoms and body aches using basic German vocabulary (e.g., Ich habe Kopfschmerzen, Mir ist schlecht)
Can make and respond to a simple doctor's appointment by phone or in person using polite request forms
Can understand and follow simple medical instructions given by a doctor or pharmacist (e.g., Nehmen Sie dreimal täglich eine Tablette)
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic body parts vocabulary (der Kopf, der Bauch, der Arm, das Bein, etc.) from A1
Present tense conjugation of regular and common irregular verbs (haben, sein, fühlen)
Modal verb 'müssen' in basic sentences
Numbers 1–100 for dosage and appointment times
Basic time expressions (heute, morgen, um 10 Uhr) from A1
Polite forms of address: Sie vs. du, bitte, danke

sessions.title: Körper, Beschwerden und Symptome – Mein Körper tut weh!

activities.title: Körperteil-Pantomime
activities.description: Teacher acts out a health problem (e.g., holds head, looks pained) and elicits 'Kopfschmerzen' from students. Then in pairs, Student A mimes a symptom while Student B guesses in German. Encourages retrieval of A1 body part vocabulary and creates a playful, low-anxiety opening. Teacher boards new symptom words as they arise.

activities.title: Beschwerden-Wortschatz: Bildergeschichte
activities.description: Teacher presents a visual story of a Vietnamese character named 'Minh' who wakes up feeling ill. A projected or printed comic strip (6 panels) shows Minh experiencing various symptoms: Halsschmerzen, Fieber, Husten, Schnupfen, Bauchschmerzen, Rückenschmerzen, Schwindel, Übelkeit. Teacher models pronunciation and meaning for each. Students repeat chorally and individually. Vietnamese translation equivalents are provided on a bilingual vocabulary handout to aid comprehension at A2 level. Teacher highlights the key structure: 'Ich habe + [Symptom]' vs. 'Mir ist + [Adjektiv] (schlecht, schwindelig)'.
materials: Projected or printed Minh comic strip (6-panel story)

activities.title: Symptom-Bingo
activities.description: Each student receives a 3x3 bingo card with 9 German symptom words. Teacher reads out symptoms in Vietnamese (or describes them in simple German), and students cross off the matching German word. Winner calls 'Bingo!' and must correctly say all crossed words aloud to win. This reinforces receptive vocabulary and German spelling recognition. Played 2–3 rounds.
materials: Printed Symptom-Bingo cards (unique per student, 5 variants)

activities.title: Wie geht es Minh? – Sätze bilden
activities.description: Students look at 6 images of Minh from the comic strip. In pairs, Student A points to an image and asks 'Was hat Minh?' or 'Wie fühlt sich Minh?'. Student B forms a complete sentence: 'Minh hat Fieber' or 'Ihm ist schlecht.' Then partners switch roles. Teacher monitors, corrects structural errors gently, and notes common errors for whole-class feedback at the end.
materials: Sentence frame poster: 'Ich/Er/Sie hat ___. Mir/Ihm/Ihr ist ___'

activities.title: Exit Ticket: Ich habe…
activities.description: Each student writes 2 sentences on a sticky note or small card: one using 'Ich habe…' and one using 'Mir ist…', using new vocabulary from today. They hand the card to the teacher as they leave. Teacher quickly reviews for Session 2 planning. Students who finish early can write a third sentence about a partner: 'Er/Sie hat…'.
materials: Sticky notes or small index cards

sessions.title: Beim Arzt – Einen Termin machen und das Gespräch führen

activities.title: Schnelle Wiederholung – Symptom-Kette
activities.description: Class stands in a circle. Teacher starts: 'Ich habe Kopfschmerzen.' Student 1 repeats and adds a new symptom: 'Ich habe Kopfschmerzen und Fieber.' Each student adds one symptom. This reviews Session 1 vocabulary through a memory chain game (similar to 'I went to the market'). If a student cannot continue, they sit down. The last 3 standing win. Keeps energy high and reviews previous content.

activities.title: Hörübung: Termin beim Arzt
activities.description: Students listen to a model dialogue (teacher reads aloud or audio recording) in which a patient calls a doctor's office to make an appointment. Dialogue includes: greeting, stating problem, requesting appointment, confirming date/time, thanking and goodbye. Students listen once for gist (What is the problem? When is the appointment?). Second listening: students fill in a simple table with 3 pieces of information: Name des Patienten, Beschwerde, Termin (Datum und Uhrzeit). Vietnamese learners benefit from the structured table as a scaffold. Teacher then reveals the transcript and discusses key phrases.
materials: Printed listening worksheet with gist questions and information table
Audio file or teacher script of phone dialogue

activities.title: Sprachbaukasten: Im Wartezimmer und beim Arzt
activities.description: Teacher presents a structured 'Sprachbaukasten' (language toolkit) handout with three columns of functional phrases: (1) Patient describes symptoms – 'Ich habe seit [zwei Tagen] Schmerzen in…', 'Es tut hier weh.', 'Mir ist seit gestern schlecht.'; (2) Doctor asks questions – 'Seit wann haben Sie die Beschwerden?', 'Haben Sie Fieber?', 'Sind Sie allergisch gegen…?'; (3) Doctor gives instructions – 'Nehmen Sie [zweimal täglich] eine Tablette.', 'Sie müssen im Bett bleiben.', 'Trinken Sie viel Wasser.' Teacher draws attention to 'seit + Dativ' construction (seit zwei Tagen, seit einer Woche) and the imperative for instructions. Vietnamese note: point out that German separates 'pain location' from the verb differently than Vietnamese.
materials: Sprachbaukasten handout (DE/VI glosses for complex phrases)

activities.title: Rollenspiel: Arzt und Patient
activities.description: Students work in pairs. Each pair receives a role card set: one 'Patient' card (with a symptom list, duration, and name) and one 'Arzt/Ärztin' card (with prompt questions and instruction options). Students prepare for 2 minutes, then perform their 3–4 minute dialogue. Teacher circulates and offers correction. After the first round, partners swap roles and use a new scenario card. At least 2 pairs perform in front of the class. Class gives feedback using a simple peer-feedback form (Was war gut? Was kann man verbessern?). Vietnamese learners are reminded to use formal 'Sie' throughout, as the cultural context of speaking to a doctor demands formality—unlike in Vietnam where doctor-patient hierarchy may be expressed differently.
materials: Role cards: Patient (4 variants) and Arzt (2 variants)
Peer feedback form (simple: 2 positive points, 1 suggestion)

activities.title: Reflexion und Hausaufgaben-Einführung
activities.description: Teacher leads a 3-minute whole-class discussion: 'Was war schwierig? Was habt ihr gut gemacht?' Students share one thing they learned and one thing they want to practice more. Teacher introduces homework and previews next week's topic (Apotheke und Medikamente / gesunde Ernährung). Students write the homework in their notebooks.

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: 1. 'Ich habe + Nomen (Akkusativ)' für Symptome vs. 'Mir ist + Adjektiv' (dativische Konstruktion für Befinden). 2. Temporalangabe mit 'seit + Dativ' (seit zwei Tagen, seit einer Woche) – introduction of Dativ with time expressions. 3. Imperativ (2. Person Singular/Plural formal 'Sie') für ärztliche Anweisungen: 'Nehmen Sie…', 'Ruhen Sie sich aus…', 'Trinken Sie…'. 4. Review of modal verb 'müssen' in context: 'Sie müssen im Bett bleiben.'
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In Germany (and Austria/Switzerland), patients must present their Krankenversicherungskarte (health insurance card) at every doctor visit. Most employed people are covered by public health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV). Doctor's appointments (Termine) are typically booked in advance; walk-ins (without appointment) are only for emergencies. Waiting rooms (Wartezimmer) are common, and patients are expected to arrive on time or a few minutes early. In contrast to Vietnam, where it is common to visit a pharmacy first for minor ailments and receive medication without a prescription, in Germany many medications require a prescription (Rezept). The concept of the Hausarzt (general practitioner / family doctor) is central: this is the first point of contact for most health issues, and specialist referrals (Überweisungen) go through the Hausarzt. In Switzerland, this role is called Grundversorger. Learners should also know that German doctors use formal 'Sie' with all adult patients, regardless of age difference.

homework.description: Students complete three written and one audio-based task to consolidate the week's learning on health and doctor visits.
exercises: Exercise 1 – Lückentext (Gap-fill): Complete 8 sentences about symptoms and doctor visits using the correct word from a word box. Includes 'seit + Dativ' forms. (Handout provided or textbook page)

Exercise 2 – Schreiben: Write a short email (50–70 words) in German from the perspective of Minh to a friend, explaining that Minh is sick, describing 2–3 symptoms, and saying that he/she has a doctor's appointment tomorrow. Use 'seit', 'Ich habe…', and 'Mir ist…'
Exercise 3 – Hören: Listen to a 2-minute audio dialogue (link or QR code provided) between a patient and a receptionist booking an appointment. Answer 4 comprehension questions in German.
Exercise 4 – Vokabeln lernen: Review all 30 target vocabulary items using the provided bilingual word list. Write each word 2 times and mark any uncertain ones for class review next week.

formative: Exit ticket at end of Session 1: students write 2 grammatically correct symptom sentences using 'Ich habe…' and 'Mir ist…'; teacher reviews before Session 2
Teacher observation during Symptom-Bingo: notes students who consistently misidentify vocabulary for targeted follow-up
Listening task worksheet (Session 2): spot-check completion of information table to assess comprehension of key details
Peer feedback during role play: teacher collects peer feedback forms and checks for accuracy of observations
Monitoring during pair work and role play: teacher uses a simple checklist to track pronunciation of key medical terms, use of 'seit', and appropriate register (formal 'Sie')
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini role play assessment (conducted in Week 3 final 10 minutes or beginning of Week 4): Each student (in pairs) performs a 3–4 minute doctor-patient dialogue from a new, unseen role card. Assessment criteria (simple rubric, 0–2 points each): (1) correct use of symptom vocabulary, (2) use of 'seit + Dativ' at least once, (3) use of formal 'Sie' register throughout, (4) comprehensibility of communication, (5) appropriate use of at least one imperative instruction. Maximum 10 points. Students receive written feedback within one week.

differentiation.struggling_learners: 1. Provide bilingual (DE/VI) vocabulary cards with pictures for all 30 target words – learners keep these as a physical reference during activities. 2. During role play, allow use of the Sprachbaukasten handout as an open resource (not memorized). 3. Simplify role cards: provide sentence starters and a minimum of 2 exchange turns instead of 4. 4. For 'seit + Dativ', limit practice to fixed phrases (seit zwei Tagen, seit einer Woche) without requiring full Dativ declension analysis. 5. Pair struggling learners with a supportive peer during initial role play practice before performing alone. 6. Offer additional gap-fill exercises with the German word already in base form to reduce cognitive load.
differentiation.advanced_learners: 1. Extension role play: add a complication to the scenario (e.g., patient is allergic to penicillin, or the appointment slot is full), requiring improvisation and negotiation language. 2. Ask advanced learners to write the full transcript of their role play dialogue as a written extension (150+ words). 3. Introduce comparative/superlative in context: 'Die Schmerzen sind heute schlimmer als gestern.' 4. Present Konjunktiv II for polite requests: 'Könnten Sie mir bitte einen Termin geben?' and 'Ich hätte gerne einen Termin für morgen.' 5. Research task: find and summarize (in German, 3–4 sentences) one difference between healthcare systems in Germany and Vietnam to share with the class next week.

review_from_previous: Week 1 topic (Wohnen & Alltag): household routine vocabulary reactivated through context – Minh gets sick at home, connects daily routine to health

Week 2 topic (Einkaufen & Dienstleistungen): making requests and appointments at a service counter – same functional language (telephone etiquette, asking for help politely) reused for booking a doctor's appointment
A1 body parts vocabulary: explicitly reviewed and extended with symptom language
A1 present tense conjugation: reviewed through symptom sentences with haben, sein, fühlen, tun
A1 numbers and time expressions: recycled in appointment booking context (Uhrzeit, Datum)
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 4 will extend the health theme into 'Apotheke und gesunde Ernährung' (Pharmacy and Healthy Diet). Students will need this week's medication vocabulary (Tablette, Rezept, Apotheke) as a foundation. The grammar focus will expand to comparative adjectives (gesünder, besser) and the use of 'sollen' (modal verb for doctor's recommendations: 'Sie sollen mehr Obst essen'). The cultural note will address the German attitude toward preventive health (Vorsorge) and the role of Krankenkassen in covering annual check-ups.

learning_objectives: Can ask for and give information about transport options, departure times, and ticket prices at a ticket office or information desk
Can describe a simple journey using past tense (Perfekt), including means of transport, duration, and destination
Can read and understand basic travel schedules, signs, and short announcements at transport hubs
prerequisite_knowledge: Numbers and times (Uhrzeit) from A1
Basic question words: Wann, Wo, Wie, Wohin, Woher
Present tense of modal verbs: müssen, können, wollen
Basic prepositions with Dativ: mit, nach, von, zu, in
Vocabulary for common places in a city (Bahnhof, Flughafen, Bushaltestelle)
Perfekt formation with haben and sein for regular and common irregular verbs (introduced in Week 5)

sessions.title: Unterwegs – Verkehrsmittel und Reisepläne

activities.title: Bildkarten: Welches Verkehrsmittel nimmst du?
activities.description: Teacher displays 8 flashcard images on the board (Zug, Bus, U-Bahn, Straßenbahn, Flugzeug, Fahrrad, Auto, Schiff). Learners work in pairs and race to name each vehicle in German. Then each learner tells their partner how they travel to class / work every day using 'Ich fahre mit dem/der...' or 'Ich gehe zu Fuß.' Teacher elicits responses whole-class and writes target phrases on the board. This activates prior vocabulary and creates a personal connection to the topic. For Vietnamese learners, teacher notes cultural contrast: motorbike (Motorrad/Moped) is dominant in Vietnam but rare for daily urban commuting in DACH countries.
materials: Flashcard images of 8 transport types (printed or projected)

activities.title: Wortschatz: Am Bahnhof und unterwegs
activities.description: Teacher introduces 20 target vocabulary items using a visual mind-map projected on screen, grouped into three clusters: (1) Verkehrsmittel (der Zug, die U-Bahn, der Bus, das Flugzeug, die Straßenbahn, das Schiff, das Taxi), (2) Am Bahnhof / Flughafen (der Bahnsteig, das Gleis, die Abfahrt, die Ankunft, der Fahrplan, das Ticket/die Fahrkarte, der Schalter, das Gleis, die Verspätung, der Anschluss), (3) Reiseverben (abfahren, ankommen, umsteigen, buchen, reservieren, verpassen). Teacher models pronunciation clearly, paying special attention to vowel length distinctions that are challenging for Vietnamese learners (e.g., Zug vs. Zoo, Bahn vs. Bann). Learners repeat chorally and individually. Teacher then conducts a quick 'point and say' drill using the flashcards. Vietnamese-language glossary handout is distributed for self-study reference.
materials: Projected mind-map slide or whiteboard drawing

activities.title: Am Schalter: Ein Dialog am Bahnhof
activities.description: Learners listen to a short recorded dialogue (approx. 90 seconds) between a traveller and a ticket office clerk at a German train station. The traveller asks about trains to Munich, the price, departure time, and whether a seat reservation is needed. Key phrases include: 'Wann fährt der nächste Zug nach München ab?', 'Muss ich umsteigen?', 'Was kostet eine Fahrkarte?', 'Einmal einfach / hin und zurück, bitte.' Learners first listen for gist (Task 1: multiple choice – Where is the traveller going? When does the train leave?). Second listen focuses on detail (Task 2: fill in a simple form with destination, departure time, price, platform number). Teacher pauses audio after key sections if needed. Answers are checked in pairs then whole-class. Teacher highlights the separable verb 'abfahren' (fährt ab) and 'ankommen' (kommt an) as they appear in context.
materials: Audio file: Bahnhof dialogue (teacher-recorded or from coursebook)
Listening task worksheet with multiple choice and form-fill sections

activities.title: Strukturen: Fragen am Bahnhof – Fragewörter und Modalverben
activities.description: Teacher draws attention to the question structures used in the dialogue and writes a structured table on the board with five key question types: (1) Wann fährt der Zug ab? (2) Wohin fährt dieser Bus? (3) Wie lange dauert die Fahrt? (4) Muss ich umsteigen? (5) Was kostet eine Fahrkarte nach Berlin? Teacher also highlights the modal verb 'müssen' in questions and short answers: 'Müssen Sie umsteigen? – Ja, Sie müssen in Frankfurt umsteigen. / Nein, es ist ein Direktzug.' Learners copy the table and then do a controlled substitution drill in pairs: teacher gives a cue card with a destination, and learners must form the correct question. This controlled practice is especially helpful for Vietnamese learners who benefit from explicit structural patterns before open production.
materials: Cue cards with destination names and travel details (one set per pair)

sessions.title: Eine Reise beschreiben – Perfekt und Kommunikation unterwegs

activities.title: Kurze Wiederholung: Perfekt mit sein und haben
activities.description: Quick 5-minute review bridging from Week 5 grammar. Teacher shows 6 sentences on screen with gaps and learners must choose 'haben' or 'sein' and supply the correct Partizip II. Focus on movement/change-of-state verbs with sein (fahren → ist gefahren, fliegen → ist geflogen, ankommen → ist angekommen, umsteigen → ist umgestiegen) and other verbs with haben (kaufen → hat gekauft, buchen → hat gebucht). Teacher elicits answers, corrects errors, and briefly explains the rule again: Verben der Bewegung / Zustandsveränderung → sein; all others → haben. This recycling is critical for the Perfekt-based speaking activity that follows.

activities.title: Lesen: Eine Reisebeschreibung – Peters Wochenende in Hamburg
activities.description: Learners receive a short text (approx. 120 words, A2 level) in which 'Peter' describes a weekend trip to Hamburg using Perfekt tense. The text includes: departure from Frankfurt by train, arrival time, hotel check-in, sightseeing (Miniatur Wunderland, Speicherstadt), travel by U-Bahn within the city, return journey. Comprehension Task 1 (global): True/False statements (5 items). Comprehension Task 2 (detailed): Answer questions in German using Perfekt (e.g., 'Wie ist Peter nach Hamburg gefahren?', 'Was hat er in Hamburg gemacht?'). Learners work individually, then compare with a partner. Teacher conducts whole-class feedback and writes correct Perfekt forms on the board as a grammar reference bank for the next production activity. Teacher points out authentic language features: booking in advance ('im Voraus buchen'), the Hamburg Card for tourists.
materials: Reading text handout 'Peters Wochenende in Hamburg'

activities.title: Meine letzte Reise – Partnerinterview im Perfekt
activities.description: Guided speaking activity in pairs. Each learner receives a 'Reise-Interviewkarte' with 6 question prompts they must ask their partner about a real or imagined recent trip: (1) Wohin bist du gereist? (2) Wie bist du dorthin gefahren / geflogen? (3) Wie lange hat die Reise gedauert? (4) Wo hast du übernachtet? (5) Was hast du dort gemacht? (6) Hat es dir gefallen? Learner A interviews Learner B (3 minutes), then they swap roles. After the interview, each learner writes 3 sentences summarising their partner's trip using Perfekt. These are then shared with another pair (inner/outer circle or simply across the table). Teacher circulates, noting common errors for later feedback. Vietnamese learners may describe trips to Da Nang, Hoi An etc. – teacher affirms this and ensures German vocabulary is available for Vietnamese destinations (e.g., 'Ich bin nach Da Nang geflogen').
materials: Reise-Interviewkarte (laminated prompt cards, one per learner)
Notebook / writing paper for summary sentences

activities.title: Feedback und Ausblick: Was nehme ich mit?
activities.description: Teacher conducts brief whole-class error correction based on notes taken during the speaking activity, focusing on 2-3 high-frequency errors (e.g., mixing haben/sein in Perfekt, incorrect word order with separable verbs, gender errors with transport nouns). Uses the 'correct the sentence on the board' technique without identifying individual learners. Teacher then previews homework and next week's topic (Übernachten & Hotel). Exit ticket: Each learner writes on a sticky note one sentence about their own travel using Perfekt and sticks it on a wall map poster. Teacher quickly reviews these for formative assessment as learners leave.
materials: Wall map poster of Europe / the world

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Perfekt with movement and change-of-state verbs using sein (fahren→ist gefahren, fliegen→ist geflogen, ankommen→ist angekommen, umsteigen→ist umgestiegen, reisen→ist gereist) contrasted with Perfekt using haben for other travel verbs (buchen→hat gebucht, kaufen→hat gekauft, machen→hat gemacht); word order in Perfekt questions and statements; separable verbs in Perfekt (abfahren→ist abgefahren, ankommen→ist angekommen) with ge- infixed between prefix and stem
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In DACH countries, public transport is highly developed and widely used even in smaller cities. The Deutsche Bahn (DB) in Germany, ÖBB in Austria, and SBB in Switzerland are national rail networks. The 'Deutschlandticket' (49-Euro-Ticket, now Deutschlandticket at 58 Euro from 2025) allows unlimited travel on local and regional public transport throughout Germany, which is culturally significant and a common topic of conversation. Punctuality is highly valued: a train that is more than a few minutes late ('hat Verspätung') is considered noteworthy and is a common source of polite complaint. In Vietnam, long-distance travel often means motorbike or sleeper bus; comparing these cultural travel habits creates engaging discussion and helps learners understand why certain vocabulary and phrases are so central in German daily communication.

homework.description: Learners complete three tasks consolidating vocabulary, grammar, and writing skills from this week's sessions.
exercises: Vocabulary exercise: Match 15 transport and travel vocabulary items to their Vietnamese translations, then write each German word in a sentence of your own (minimum 15 sentences).
Grammar exercise: Rewrite 8 sentences from Präsens into Perfekt, choosing the correct auxiliary verb (haben or sein). Sentences cover a mix of travel verbs practiced in class.

Writing task: Write a short paragraph (60–80 words) in German describing a real or imagined journey you have taken, using at least 5 Perfekt sentences and 3 vocabulary items from this week's list. Post your paragraph in the class WhatsApp/Zalo group or learning platform for peer feedback before the next session.

formative: Observation during pair interview activity: teacher uses a simple checklist to note correct/incorrect use of Perfekt auxiliary (haben/sein) and separable verbs
Exit ticket sticky notes: teacher reads all sentences after class to identify patterns of misunderstanding and adjust next session accordingly
Listening task worksheet collected and reviewed: teacher notes scores on the form-fill task to gauge comprehension of transport dialogue
Oral drill accuracy during substitution practice: teacher notes which question forms learners can produce correctly without support
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini role-play assessment (conducted at start of Week 7): Learner A plays a traveller at a Bahnhof ticket counter, Learner B plays the clerk. The traveller must ask for a ticket to a given destination, enquire about departure time and platform, ask whether they need to change trains, and confirm the price. The conversation should last at least 90 seconds. Assessed using a simple 4-criteria rubric: (1) Task completion – all required information exchanged; (2) Vocabulary accuracy – correct transport and travel terms used; (3) Grammar – Perfekt used correctly in at least one reference to a previous journey; (4) Communication – comprehensible and appropriately structured. Each criterion scored 0–3 for a maximum of 12 points.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a vocabulary scaffold card with all 20 target words, their articles, and a Vietnamese translation for use throughout all activities. During the pair interview, give a sentence frame card: 'Ich bin nach ___ (gefahren / geflogen). Die Reise hat ___ Stunden gedauert. Ich habe ___ gemacht.' Reduce the writing homework to 40 words. Pair struggling learners with supportive peers during speaking tasks. Offer the audio dialogue transcript for a third listen if needed. Allow mother-tongue (Vietnamese) clarification of grammar rules for haben/sein distinction if confusion persists.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to write their travel paragraph as a short travel blog entry (100–120 words) using connectors (zuerst, dann, danach, schließlich) and at least two adjectives. During the role-play preparation, add a complication: the train is cancelled ('Der Zug fällt aus') and the traveller must find an alternative route. Advanced learners can also research and present a 2-minute verbal summary of one interesting fact about DB, ÖBB, or SBB for the next class, practising Perfekt in a real-world context.

review_from_previous: Week 5: Perfekt formation with haben and sein – irregular and regular verbs (directly recycled in this week's reading and speaking activities)
Week 4: Telling the time and expressing duration (Wie lange? / Um wie viel Uhr?) – reactivated in transport timetable contexts
Week 3: Prepositions with Dativ – mit dem Zug, nach München, in der Stadt, vom Bahnhof – drilled implicitly throughout transport vocabulary
Week 2: Modal verbs müssen and können – practised in ticket office dialogue and timetable reading tasks
Week 1: Numbers and prices – reactivated when asking about ticket prices and travel times
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: This week's vocabulary and Perfekt structures provide a direct bridge to Week 7: 'Übernachten & Hotel'. Learners will use Perfekt to describe their accommodation experience ('Ich habe in einem Hotel übernachtet'), build on the booking vocabulary introduced this week ('reservieren', 'buchen'), and extend preposition use to hotel contexts. The role-play format practised at the Bahnhof Schalter will be recycled at the hotel reception desk, lowering the affective barrier for production.

learning_objectives: Can introduce themselves to a neighbour and exchange basic personal information in simple sentences
Can write a short, polite note to a neighbour about everyday issues such as noise or shared spaces
Can understand and use key vocabulary related to apartment buildings, house rules, and neighbourly interactions
prerequisite_knowledge: Present tense of regular and common irregular verbs (sein, haben, wohnen, machen)
Modal verbs: können, müssen, dürfen at basic level
Basic accusative and dative case with common prepositions (in, bei, mit, neben, gegenüber)
Numbers and times for scheduling and describing routines
Polite forms of address: Sie vs. du distinction
Vocabulary for rooms and furniture from Week 5–6

sessions.title: Meine Nachbarn – Wer wohnt nebenan?

activities.title: Bildbeschreibung: Das Mietshaus
activities.description: Display a colourful illustrated cross-section of a German Mietshaus (apartment building) showing 6 different residents in their flats doing typical activities. Learners work in pairs. Partner A describes one resident using 2–3 sentences; Partner B guesses which flat. Teacher models first: 'Im zweiten Stock links wohnt eine alte Frau. Sie hat eine Katze. Sie trinkt Kaffee.' Vietnamese L1 support: key sentence frames are printed on a small card at each desk. Focus on ordinal numbers for floors (Erdgeschoss, erster Stock, zweiter Stock) as these differ from Vietnamese counting conventions.
materials: A3 colour printout of illustrated Mietshaus cross-section (1 per pair)
Sentence frame card: 'Im ___ Stock (links/rechts/Mitte) wohnt ___. Er/Sie ___.'
Vocabulary mini-list: Erdgeschoss, erster Stock, zweiter Stock, links, rechts, gegenüber

activities.title: Wortfeld: Nachbarschaft & Wohnen
activities.description: Teacher presents 18 target vocabulary items using a visual word map on the board. Each word is shown with: (1) a small image, (2) German article/plural, (3) a model sentence, (4) Vietnamese translation equivalent in brackets for reference. Vocabulary is grouped into three clusters: People (der Nachbar/-in, der Mieter/-in, der Vermieter/-in, die Hausgemeinschaft), Places/Objects (der Flur, der Keller, die Mülltonne, der Briefkasten, die Klingel, das Treppenhaus), and Actions/Rules (klingeln, lärmen, beschweren sich, putzen, rücksichtslos sein, ruhig sein, stören). Teacher drills pronunciation chorally then individually, paying special attention to the -er ending (Nachbar, Vermieter) which does not exist in Vietnamese phonology. Learners copy word map into their vocabulary notebooks using the four-quadrant method: word, image sketch, example sentence, Vietnamese meaning.
materials: Whiteboard or digital projector with prepared word map slide
Vocabulary handout with images and Vietnamese translations (1 per learner)

activities.title: Wer bin ich? – Kettenübung mit Rollenkarten
activities.description: Each learner receives a role card describing a fictional resident of the Mietshaus (name, flat number, occupation, one habit). Learners stand up and mingle. They must greet three different classmates using formal Sie, introduce their character, and ask one question. Role card example: 'Sie sind Frau Nguyen, 2. Stock, Köchin. Sie kochen jeden Abend um 19 Uhr.' Greet with 'Guten Tag, ich bin... Ich wohne im zweiten Stock. Und Sie?' A structured feedback slot follows: teacher asks 2–3 pairs to demonstrate for the class. Note for Vietnamese learners: formal Sie address is culturally significant in German contexts; brief explicit comparison to Vietnamese levels of formality (anh/chị vs. em) helps anchor understanding.
materials: Role cards (1 per learner, 15–20 different cards prepared)
Greeting formula reminder strip on each card

activities.title: Die Hausordnung lesen
activities.description: Learners receive a simplified but authentic-style German Hausordnung (house rules document) adapted to A2 level. It contains 8 rules using modal verbs: müssen, dürfen, sollen. Example rules: 'Die Mieter müssen das Treppenhaus sauber halten.', 'Musik darf nur bis 22 Uhr gespielt werden.' (passive avoided; rewritten as 'Sie dürfen nur bis 22 Uhr Musik spielen.'). Task 1 (individual, 3 min): Read and mark each rule as ERLAUBT (allowed) or VERBOTEN (forbidden) using a simple two-column table on the handout. Task 2 (pairs, 3 min): Compare answers and discuss one rule they find surprising. Teacher elicits reactions in a brief whole-class share. Comprehension check questions written on board: 'Was muss man tun? Was darf man nicht tun?'
materials: A2-adapted Hausordnung handout with 8 rules (1 per learner)

sessions.title: Probleme lösen – Höflich schreiben und sprechen

activities.title: Schnellabfrage: Modal-Verb-Karten
activities.description: Quick retrieval practice from Session 1 and previous weeks. Teacher reads 8 situations aloud in simple German (or shows image prompts). Learners hold up a coloured card: GREEN = darf, YELLOW = muss, RED = darf nicht. Example: 'Es ist 23 Uhr. Herr Braun spielt laut Musik.' (RED – darf nicht). After each round, teacher briefly elicits a full sentence from a volunteer: 'Er darf keine laute Musik spielen.' This activates modal verb knowledge and directly connects to the complaint-writing task that follows.
materials: Green / Yellow / Red response cards (1 set per learner, laminated)

activities.title: Hören: Ein Gespräch zwischen Nachbarn
