activities.description: Learners listen to a recorded dialogue (approximately 90 seconds, carefully scripted at A2 level with clear articulation and natural but slow pace) between two neighbours: Frau Müller knocks on Herr Tanaka's door to politely complain about noise late at night. The dialogue models key functions: making a polite complaint ('Es tut mir leid, aber...'), apologising ('Entschuldigung, das wusste ich nicht.'), making a request ('Könnten Sie bitte...?'), and reaching an agreement ('Natürlich, kein Problem.'). Pre-listening (1 min): Learners predict from a still image what the conversation might be about. Listening Task 1 – Global (play once): What is the problem? Learners write one sentence. Listening Task 2 – Detailed (play again): Complete a gapped dialogue transcript – 6 gaps targeting key phrases. Post-listening: Learners check answers with a partner then whole class feedback. Note: The Konjunktiv II form 'Könnten Sie' is presented as a fixed polite formula at this stage, not as a full grammar explanation.
materials: Audio file (teacher-recorded or AI-generated at A2 pace, approx. 90 seconds)
Gapped dialogue transcript handout (1 per learner)
Answer key on reverse side (distributed after task)

activities.title: Höfliche Bitten formulieren – Könnten Sie / Würden Sie
activities.description: Guided inductive grammar discovery. Teacher writes three sentences from the listening on the board: (1) 'Spielen Sie bitte leiser.' (2) 'Können Sie bitte leiser spielen?' (3) 'Könnten Sie bitte leiser spielen?' Learners discuss in pairs: Which sounds most polite? Why? Teacher elicits observations, then explicitly explains that 'Könnten Sie' and 'Würden Sie' are polite request formulas used in formal neighbour situations. A simple transformation drill follows (substitution table on whiteboard): Learners take an imperative from a list and transform it into a polite Könnten-Sie or Würden-Sie request. Example: 'Machen Sie das Licht aus.' → 'Könnten Sie bitte das Licht ausmachen?' Pairs create 3 examples each and share one with the class. Vietnamese pedagogical note: Politeness gradation in German maps onto but is not identical to Vietnamese honorific system; explicit comparison helps transfer.
materials: Grammar reference mini-card: Könnten Sie / Würden Sie + infinitive (1 per learner)
Drill exercise strip with 5 imperatives to transform

activities.title: Schreiben: Ein freundlicher Nachbarn-Zettel
activities.description: Learners write a short note (40–60 words) to a neighbour. Three scenario options are provided so learners choose what is most interesting or relevant: Scenario A – Your neighbour's dog barks every morning at 6am; Scenario B – Someone is leaving rubbish bags in the hallway; Scenario C – A neighbour parks their bicycle blocking the entrance. A writing scaffold is provided on the handout: greeting, problem statement using 'Ich möchte Sie darauf aufmerksam machen, dass...', polite request using 'Könnten Sie bitte...?', closing formula. Teacher circulates and gives targeted feedback using a 'praise-question-polish' method. After writing (8 min), learners swap notes with a partner who reads as the neighbour and writes a 2-sentence reply. Pairs then briefly share their exchange with an adjacent pair.
materials: Writing task handout with three scenarios and writing scaffold (1 per learner)
Sample completed note as model (shown on projector)

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Modal verbs müssen, dürfen, sollen in the context of rules and obligations; introduction of Konjunktiv II forms 'Könnten Sie' and 'Würden Sie' as fixed politeness formulas for requests
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In DACH countries, the relationship between neighbours is often formal even after years of living nearby. It is standard to use 'Sie' with neighbours unless explicitly invited to use 'du'. Ruhezeiten (quiet hours) are strictly observed in Germany: typically 22:00–07:00 on weekdays and throughout Sunday. Many apartment buildings post a Hausordnung in the communal entrance. Recycling and correct use of colour-coded Mülltonnen (bins: gelb for packaging, grün/braun for organic, blau for paper, schwarz for residual waste) is a significant civic responsibility and a common source of neighbour friction. In Vietnam, neighbour relations tend to be warmer and more informal from the outset; German formality and emphasis on written rules may feel distant at first but reflects a cultural value of clear boundaries and mutual respect (Rücksichtnahme).

homework.description: Learners complete a written task and a vocabulary review exercise to consolidate Session 2 grammar and new vocabulary.
exercises: Writing task: Write a second Nachbarn-Zettel (40–60 words) for a new scenario provided on the homework sheet – a neighbour who leaves their laundry in the shared washing machine for two days. Use the writing scaffold from class and include at least one 'Könnten Sie' request.
Vocabulary exercise: Complete a gap-fill text about a typical German Mietshaus using 10 words from the vocabulary target list. Context sentences make the correct answer clear from meaning.

Listening extension (optional, for motivated learners): Watch a 3-minute YouTube clip from the series 'Typisch Deutsch' about Ruhezeiten (link provided on homework sheet) and note down 3 things you learned.

formative: Observation during mingling role-play activity: teacher uses a simple checklist to note whether learners use formal Sie address, correct floor vocabulary, and target vocabulary spontaneously
Colour card responses during modal verb quick-check allow instant identification of learners who confuse müssen/dürfen/dürfen nicht
Circulating during writing task: teacher reads drafts and gives immediate corrective or affirming feedback on use of Könnten Sie and note structure
Exit ticket at end of Session 2 (3 minutes): Learners write one sentence they would say to a noisy neighbour using a polite request form – teacher collects and reviews before next lesson
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (to be conducted at the start of Week 9, first 15 minutes): Learners receive a scenario card describing a neighbour problem and must (a) complete a 50-word written note to the neighbour using target vocabulary and at least one modal verb and one polite request form, and (b) answer 5 vocabulary matching questions from the week's word list. Assessed using a simple 3-level rubric: task completion, language accuracy, and vocabulary range.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a word bank directly on all writing and speaking tasks so learners are not blocked by vocabulary recall. Reduce the number of required vocabulary items in gap-fill to 6 instead of 10. During the mingling activity, pair struggling learners with a more confident peer initially before independent mingling. Offer an L1 (Vietnamese) glossary of all 25 target words as a removable scaffold to be faded from Week 9 onward. For the Hausordnung reading, pre-teach the 3 most difficult modal constructions with a dedicated 2-minute micro-explanation before the reading task.
differentiation.advanced_learners: During the writing task, challenge advanced learners to write without the scaffold and to include a second paragraph offering a compromise or solution. In the role-play, ask them to improvise a longer conversation of at least 8 turns without a script. Extension grammar task: rewrite 5 direct commands from the Hausordnung using all three politeness levels (imperative, können-question, Konjunktiv II) and reflect on the difference in tone. Cultural extension: research and note two differences between German and Vietnamese neighbour etiquette for a short 2-minute class presentation in Week 9.

review_from_previous: Week 5–6: Rooms and furniture vocabulary – reactivated through Mietshaus image description warm-up
Week 4: Modal verbs können and müssen – revisited and extended with dürfen and sollen in Hausordnung context
Week 3: Telling the time and daily routine – recycled through Ruhezeiten context and role card descriptions of daily habits
Week 7: Making requests and asking for help – extended into formal written register with Könnten Sie / Würden Sie formulas
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 9 will focus on 'Einkaufen & im Supermarkt' – the written note skills practised this week directly transfer to writing shopping lists and short messages; the formal register practised here contrasts with the informal dialogue register that will be needed for interactions at market stalls and service counters.

learning_objectives: Can describe simple environmental problems and natural phenomena using basic vocabulary (e.g., Umweltverschmutzung, Recycling, Natur)
Can express opinions about environmental topics using modal verbs (sollen, müssen, können) in simple sentences
Can read and understand short informational texts about nature and environmental protection and extract key information
prerequisite_knowledge: Present tense of regular and irregular verbs (A1)
Basic modal verbs: können, müssen (A1 level usage)
Nominative and accusative cases with definite and indefinite articles
Basic adjective usage in predicative position
Vocabulary related to daily routines and household items (Week 6–8 content)
Simple sentence structure: Subject-Verb-Object
Numbers and quantities (for statistics about environment)

sessions.title: Die Natur und Umweltprobleme – Natur und Probleme kennenlernen

activities.title: Bildkarten-Aktivität: Was siehst du?
activities.description: Teacher displays 8–10 vivid images on the projector showing contrasting scenes: a clean forest, polluted river, recycling bins, factory smoke, solar panels, littered beach, green meadow, and a city with smog. Learners work in pairs and describe what they see using simple German sentences they already know (e.g., 'Das ist ein Wald. Das Wasser ist schmutzig.'). Each pair gets a printed set of the same images. Teacher then elicits Vietnamese comparisons: ask learners if they recognize similar environmental issues in Vietnam (e.g., Mekong River pollution, deforestation). This activates prior knowledge and creates emotional connection to the topic.
materials: Printed image cards (8–10 per pair) showing nature and environmental scenes

activities.title: Wortschatz-Puzzle: Umwelt & Natur
activities.description: Teacher introduces 20 target vocabulary items using a structured input method. Each word is presented with: (1) a visual image, (2) the German word with article and plural, (3) a Vietnamese translation gloss on the handout to reduce cognitive load for A2 learners. Vocabulary is grouped thematically on the handout into three categories: 'Die Natur' (der Wald, der Fluss, der Berg, der See, das Meer, die Wiese), 'Umweltprobleme' (die Umweltverschmutzung, der Müll, der Lärm, das Plastik, die Abgase, der Klimawandel), and 'Umweltschutz' (das Recycling, der Strom, die Energie, Energie sparen, Müll trennen, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel). Teacher models pronunciation; class repeats chorally. Learners then individually match German words to images on their handout (matching exercise). Teacher checks answers whole-class.
materials: Vocabulary handout with images, German words, articles, plurals, and Vietnamese glosses

activities.title: Kategorisierungsspiel: Natur, Problem oder Schutz?
activities.description: Learners receive a set of 20 word cards (same vocabulary from previous activity). In groups of 3, they sort cards into three columns on a large sheet of paper: 'Die Natur', 'Umweltprobleme', 'Umweltschutz'. Groups must justify their choices in simple German (e.g., 'Recycling ist Umweltschutz.'). After 5 minutes, groups compare their tables. Teacher facilitates brief discussion of any disagreements (e.g., 'der Strom' could fit in both Natur and Schutz). This activity reinforces semantic categories and encourages spoken production. Note for Vietnamese learners: the concept of 'Müll trennen' (waste separation) may be culturally unfamiliar—teacher briefly explains the German system with visuals of yellow, blue, green, and brown bins.
materials: Word card sets (20 cards per group)
Large A3 paper or table mats with three columns drawn
Visual handout showing German recycling bin colors and categories

activities.title: Modalverben für Umwelttipps: sollen und müssen
activities.description: Teacher builds on learners' A1 knowledge of 'müssen' and introduces 'sollen' in the context of environmental advice. Teacher writes two example sentences on the board: 'Wir müssen Energie sparen.' (We must save energy – personal necessity) and 'Man soll Müll trennen.' (One should separate waste – external obligation/recommendation). Teacher highlights the difference using Vietnamese explanation: 'müssen' = bắt buộc (must/have to), 'sollen' = nên/được yêu cầu (should/is supposed to). A color-coded grammar card is distributed showing conjugation of both verbs in present tense. Learners complete a gap-fill exercise with 8 sentences choosing between müssen/sollen and inserting the correct form. Teacher reviews answers with class, eliciting reasons for choices.
materials: Color-coded grammar reference card (müssen vs. sollen conjugation table with Vietnamese notes)

sessions.title: Umweltschutz im Alltag – Lesen, Sprechen und Schreiben

activities.title: Lesetext: Umweltschutz in Deutschland
activities.description: Learners receive a short, simplified informational text (approx. 150–180 words, A2 level) about everyday environmental protection habits in Germany. The text covers topics like waste separation (Mülltrennung), using public transport (öffentliche Verkehrsmittel benutzen), shopping with reusable bags (Stoffbeutel benutzen), and saving water and electricity. The text uses simple present tense, modal verbs, and target vocabulary from Session 1. Comprehension is checked through two task types: (1) True/False statements (5 items) – learners circle 'Richtig' or 'Falsch', (2) Simple information retrieval questions (3 Wh-questions in German, e.g., 'Was machen viele Deutsche mit Plastikflaschen?'). Teacher reads the text aloud first while learners follow along, supporting pronunciation and prosody. Learners then work individually on tasks before comparing answers with a partner. Whole-class feedback follows. Vietnamese learner note: teacher explicitly pre-teaches the word 'Pfand' (bottle deposit system) as this concept does not exist in Vietnam.
materials: Reading text handout with True/False and comprehension questions
Optional: audio recording of text for listening support

activities.title: Umwelt-Interview: Was machst du für die Umwelt?
activities.description: Learners conduct a structured interview in pairs using a provided question card. Questions are scaffolded at A2 level: 'Trennst du Müll zu Hause?', 'Fährst du oft mit dem Bus oder dem Fahrrad?', 'Kaufst du manchmal Bio-Produkte?', 'Was kannst du für die Umwelt tun?', 'Was soll die Regierung machen?' Each learner interviews their partner and notes key answers in a simple grid. After the interview, each learner reports one interesting thing about their partner to the class using the third person: 'Lan sagt, sie fährt oft mit dem Fahrrad.' This activity practices all three modal verbs and encourages authentic personal expression. Teacher circulates, notes errors for delayed correction. Vietnamese cultural connection: teacher acknowledges that motorbike use is dominant in Vietnam and that framing changes to cycling or public transport may feel abstract—encourage learners to think about what IS possible in their context.
materials: Interview question card (laminated or printed, one per learner)

activities.title: Schreiben: Meine Umwelttipps
activities.description: Learners write a short paragraph (5–7 sentences) giving environmental advice using modal verbs (müssen, sollen, können). A writing frame is provided on the handout to scaffold production: 'Für die Umwelt ______. Man soll ______. Wir müssen ______. Ich kann ______.' Teacher models one example paragraph on the board before learners write independently. Learners may also include a personal statement about what they already do for the environment. After writing, learners exchange papers with a partner for peer review using a simple checklist: (1) Sind 5–7 Sätze da? (2) Gibt es Modalverben? (3) Gibt es Vokabeln zum Thema Umwelt? Teacher collects written work for formative assessment feedback. Vietnamese learner note: encourage use of learned vocabulary rather than direct translation from Vietnamese—provide a 'banned dictionary' challenge where learners try not to look up any new words beyond the target list.
materials: Writing frame handout with sentence starters
Target vocabulary reference list from Session 1

activities.title: Exit Ticket: Drei Dinge
activities.description: As a closing reflection activity, each learner writes three things on a small card: (1) 'Ich habe gelernt: ______' (one new vocabulary item or grammar point), (2) 'Ich finde interessant: ______' (one interesting cultural fact), (3) 'Ich habe eine Frage: ______' (one remaining question or point of confusion). Teacher collects cards and quickly scans them. This informs the teacher about comprehension gaps before homework and feeds into the next lesson's warm-up review. Cards are returned at the start of Week 12 with brief teacher comments where needed.
materials: Small index cards or printed exit ticket slips (one per learner)

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Modal verbs 'müssen' and 'sollen' in present tense for expressing necessity and obligation in environmental contexts; review of 'können' for expressing possibility and personal ability. Sentence structure: Subject + Modal Verb + ... + Infinitive (Verb-bracket / Satzklammer).
lesson_plans.cultural_note: Germany, Austria, and Switzerland (DACH region) are known for strong environmental awareness. Germany introduced one of the world's first bottle deposit (Pfand) systems – learners pay a deposit on plastic and glass bottles, returned when recycling. Germany has a strict four-bin waste separation system (gelbe Tonne for packaging, blaue Tonne for paper, braune Tonne for organic waste, graue/schwarze Tonne for residual waste). The 'Fridays for Future' movement, started globally by Greta Thunberg, was particularly strong in German-speaking countries with large student demonstrations in Berlin, Vienna, and Zurich. Many German cities have extensive cycling infrastructure (Fahrradwege) and heavily subsidized public transport. Switzerland is ranked among the world's top countries for recycling rates. Austrians are known for their love of nature and have a strong tradition of hiking (Wandern) and nature conservation in the Alps.

homework.description: Learners complete three short tasks at home to consolidate vocabulary, grammar, and reading skills from Week 11, and to prepare for continued practice next week.
exercises: Vocabulary flashcard task: Create 10 physical or digital flashcards (e.g., using Quizlet or paper) for 10 new vocabulary items from the target list. Each card should include: German word with article and plural, a small drawing or image, and a Vietnamese translation. Learners self-test by covering the German side.

Grammar exercise: Complete a structured grammar worksheet with 10 sentences. In sentences 1–4, choose the correct modal verb (müssen/sollen/können) and conjugate it correctly. In sentences 5–8, rewrite sentences with the given modal verb (e.g., 'Du trennst Müll.' → 'Du sollst Müll trennen.'). In sentences 9–10, write original sentences about the environment using one modal verb each.

Reading & response task: Read a short adapted text (provided on handout, approx. 120 words) about environmental habits of a fictional German family 'Familie Berger'. Answer 5 comprehension questions in complete German sentences. One question requires a personal opinion: 'Was macht Familie Berger gut? Was kannst du auch machen?'

formative: Observation during categorization game (Session 1, Activity 3): teacher checks correct use of thematic categories and ability to produce simple justification sentences
Gap-fill grammar exercise (Session 1, Activity 4): reviewed whole-class immediately; teacher notes recurring errors with müssen/sollen distinction for reteaching
True/False and comprehension questions from reading task (Session 2, Activity 1): checked in pairs and whole-class; teacher identifies reading comprehension gaps
Peer review checklist during writing task (Session 2, Activity 3): teacher circulates and monitors accuracy of peer feedback and self-correction
Exit ticket collection (Session 2, Activity 4): teacher reads responses and identifies 2–3 most common confusion points to address at the start of Week 12
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-quiz (to be administered at the start of Week 12, 10–12 minutes): Part A – Vocabulary matching (10 items: match German environmental words to images/Vietnamese translations, 10 points). Part B – Grammar: complete 5 sentences with the correct modal verb form (5 points). Part C – Writing: write 3 sentences giving environmental advice using modal verbs (6 points). Total: 21 points. Pass mark: 14/21 (67%). Results used to inform differentiation groupings for Week 12.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a bilingual vocabulary reference sheet (German + Vietnamese) that learners may use during all in-class activities except the summative quiz. Reduce gap-fill exercise to 6 sentences (remove the 2 most complex items). During speaking activities, allow learners to use short phrase cards with sentence starters. Pair struggling learners with supportive peers during categorization and interview tasks. For homework, allow learners to write 3 sentences instead of 5 for the reading response. Provide pre-completed writing frame with more detailed sentence starters. Teacher gives additional explicit pronunciation drilling for multi-syllable words like 'Umweltverschmutzung' and 'öffentliche Verkehrsmittel' using syllable-by-syllable breakdown.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge learners to write 8–10 sentences in the writing production task and to include at least one negative sentence (e.g., 'Man soll nicht so viel Plastik benutzen.'). During the interview activity, encourage learners to ask follow-up questions beyond the provided card. Provide an extension reading text (approx. 200 words, slightly above A2) about the German Energiewende (energy transition) with 3 open-ended questions requiring personal interpretation. For homework, advanced learners write a short email (60–80 words) to a fictional German friend describing one environmental habit they want to change and why, using all three modal verbs. Introduce the Konjunktiv II form 'sollte' as a preview for B1 grammar ('Man sollte mehr recyceln.').

review_from_previous: Week 8 – Daily routines vocabulary: recycle time expressions (täglich, manchmal, oft, nie) now used in environmental habit discussions
Week 9 – Modal verb 'können' (A1 revision): explicitly connected to new modal verbs müssen/sollen in this week's grammar focus
Week 10 – Accusative case with definite articles: revisited when using direct objects in environmental sentences (e.g., 'Ich trenne den Müll.')
Week 6 – Numbers and quantities: reactivated when discussing statistics about plastic use, recycling rates, or CO2 emissions in reading texts
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 12 will introduce the topic 'Reisen & Verkehr' (Travel and Transport). This week's vocabulary of 'öffentliche Verkehrsmittel' and 'Fahrrad fahren' directly bridges to transport vocabulary. The modal verb structures practiced this week (especially 'können' and 'müssen') will be extended in Week 12 to include 'dürfen' and 'wollen' in the context of travel plans. Learners can be told: 'Nächste Woche lernen wir: Wie reist man in Deutschland?' as a motivating preview.

learning_objectives: Can describe basic emotions and feelings using adjectives and simple sentences (e.g., 'Ich bin glücklich, weil...')
Can talk about personal relationships such as family, friends, and colleagues using appropriate vocabulary and possessive pronouns
Can express likes, dislikes, and emotional reactions to everyday situations using modal particles and simple conjunctions like 'weil' and 'aber'
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic present tense conjugation (sein, haben, regular and common irregular verbs)
Nominative and accusative case for articles and pronouns
Family vocabulary (Mutter, Vater, Geschwister, etc.) from A1
Basic adjective usage in predicative position (Das ist schön.)
Personal pronouns (ich, du, er, sie, wir, ihr, sie/Sie)
Simple sentence structure (Subject-Verb-Object)
Numbers and basic time expressions for talking about routines

sessions.title: Wie fühlst du dich? – Gefühle ausdrücken

activities.title: Emoji-Gefühlsrunde
activities.description: The teacher displays 8 large emoji cards on the board (happy, sad, angry, tired, excited, nervous, bored, surprised). Each learner receives a small emoji card matching one emotion. In pairs, learners show their card and say 'Heute bin ich...' or 'Ich fühle mich...' The teacher models pronunciation and models two example sentences. Pairs then share one sentence with the class. This activates prior knowledge and sets the emotional vocabulary context. For Vietnamese learners, the teacher writes Pinyin-style phonetic hints for tricky German vowels (e.g., müde: mü-də) on the board.
materials: Large emoji flashcards (8 emotions) for board display
Small individual emoji cards (one per learner)

activities.title: Gefühle-Wortschatz mit Bildern
activities.description: Teacher presents 16 target emotion words using a visual vocabulary chart with German word, Vietnamese translation, example sentence, and a picture. Words are grouped into positive feelings (glücklich, froh, verliebt, aufgeregt, stolz, entspannt), negative feelings (traurig, wütend, einsam, gestresst, enttäuscht, eifersüchtig), and neutral/physical states (müde, nervös, überrascht, verwirrt). Teacher reads each word aloud, learners repeat chorally and individually. Special attention is given to umlaut sounds (ü, ö) which are challenging for Vietnamese speakers. Teacher drills minimal pairs: müde vs. Mode, fühlen vs. fehlen. Learners mark words they already know with a star in their vocabulary notebooks.
materials: A3 visual vocabulary chart (printed or projected)
Audio pronunciation guide (teacher voice or recording)

activities.title: Gefühle-Bingo
activities.description: Each learner receives a blank 4x4 bingo grid. They write 16 emotion words (from the target vocabulary list) freely into the grid squares. The teacher reads out definitions or Vietnamese translations (e.g., 'Bạn cảm thấy điều này khi nhận được quà bất ngờ' – überrascht), and learners cross off the matching German word. The first learner to complete a row shouts 'Bingo!' and reads the words aloud to check. This is played twice to reinforce recognition. The teacher corrects pronunciation errors gently using the 'repeat after me' technique rather than explicit correction to maintain confidence.
materials: Target vocabulary list (for reference during grid-filling)

activities.title: Weil-Sätze: Gefühle begründen
activities.description: Teacher introduces the subordinating conjunction 'weil' to express reasons for feelings. Using a contrastive approach relevant to Vietnamese learners (Vietnamese 'vì' functions similarly), teacher explains that in German, 'weil' sends the verb to the end of the clause. Teacher writes on board: 'Ich bin glücklich.' → 'Ich bin glücklich, weil meine Familie gesund ist.' A color-coded sentence template is displayed: [Main clause] + WEIL + [Subject + (Object) + VERB(end)]. Teacher demonstrates with 5 example sentences using emotion vocabulary from the lesson. Learners identify the final verb in each example. Teacher explicitly contrasts with Vietnamese word order to address the most common interference error. A short gap-fill of 4 sentences is completed together as a class.
materials: Whiteboard with color markers (red for end-verb position)
Contrastive grammar note card (Vietnamese vs. German word order)

sessions.title: Beziehungen beschreiben – Familie, Freunde, Kollegen

activities.title: Gefühle-Blitzrunde
activities.description: Quick 3-minute review of Session 1 vocabulary. Teacher holds up emoji cards one at a time; learners call out the German word and form one sentence with 'weil' spontaneously. Teacher selects 4–5 learners to share full sentences. Any recurring pronunciation or grammar issues are noted briefly on the board for later correction. This spaced-repetition warm-up reinforces the weil-construction before building on it with relationship vocabulary.

activities.title: Beziehungsvokabular – Wer ist wer in meinem Leben?
activities.description: Teacher presents relationship vocabulary organized in three semantic groups using a mind map on the board. Group 1 – Family: die Verwandten, der/die Verwandte, die Großeltern, der Onkel, die Tante, der Cousin/die Cousine, die Schwiegermutter, der Schwiegervater. Group 2 – Friendship & Social: der/die beste Freund/in, der/die Bekannte, der/die Nachbar/in, die Clique, der/die Mitbewohner/in. Group 3 – Romantic/Professional: der/die Partner/in, der/die Freund/in (girlfriend/boyfriend), der/die Kollege/Kollegin, der/die Chef/in. Teacher highlights the grammatical gender of each noun with color coding (blue=masculine, red=feminine, green=neuter) and provides one model sentence per group. Vietnamese cultural note: Teacher acknowledges that Vietnamese has many specific terms for relatives (anh, chị, em, etc.) but German is more general – this is discussed briefly to contextualize the vocabulary.
materials: Mind map poster or projected slide
Color-coded vocabulary handout with Vietnamese glosses

activities.title: Beziehungskarten – Wer ist das?
activities.description: Learners work in pairs. Each pair receives a set of 12 relationship description cards in German (e.g., 'Das ist die Tochter meiner Tante.' / 'Er arbeitet mit mir zusammen.'). Learners must match each description card to the correct relationship word card. After matching, pairs write two of their own description sentences using 'Das ist mein/e...' or 'Er/Sie ist mein/e...'. Possessive pronouns in nominative (mein/meine/mein) are reviewed through this activity. The teacher circulates, checks work, and provides immediate corrective feedback focusing on gender agreement of possessives.

activities.title: Mein Beziehungsnetz – Eine wichtige Person vorstellen
activities.description: Each learner draws a simple 'relationship web' showing 4–5 important people in their life, writing the relationship word next to each person's name. They then prepare a short 4–6 sentence spoken description of one important person, combining relationship vocabulary with emotion vocabulary and weil-clauses from Session 1. Example target output: 'Das ist meine beste Freundin Lan. Ich kenne sie seit der Schule. Sie ist sehr lustig und freundlich. Ich bin froh, weil sie immer für mich da ist.' Learners practice in pairs, then 3–4 volunteers share with the class. Teacher provides positive feedback and notes 2–3 class-wide language points for brief whole-class correction.
materials: Sentence starter support card: 'Das ist mein/e... Er/Sie ist... Ich fühle mich... weil...'
Vocabulary reference sheet from both sessions

activities.title: Wochenreflexion und Hausaufgabenvorstellung
activities.description: Teacher leads a 10-minute closing that includes: (1) Exit Ticket – each learner writes on a sticky note one new word they learned and one sentence using 'weil' they are confident about, and posts it on the board. Teacher quickly reviews posted notes for formative assessment purposes. (2) The homework task is explained clearly with a model example shown on the board. (3) Teacher previews next week's topic ('Alltag und Termine') and draws a connection: 'Nächste Woche sprechen wir darüber, wie wir uns bei der Arbeit oder in der Schule fühlen.' This creates a content bridge and motivates learners.
materials: Preview slide or sentence on board

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Subordinating conjunction 'weil' with verb-final word order (Nebensatz): 'Ich bin glücklich, weil meine Familie gesund ist.' Review of possessive pronouns in nominative case (mein/meine/mein) for describing relationships.
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In DACH cultures, emotional expression in public is generally more reserved than in Vietnamese culture. Germans, Austrians, and Swiss may appear less effusive with emotions among acquaintances but are typically very open and direct in close relationships. The concept of 'Freund/in' in German has two meanings: a close friend AND a romantic partner – context determines meaning. This is worth highlighting explicitly. Additionally, 'Du' is used freely among friends and young people in DACH countries, while 'Sie' remains important in professional and formal contexts – a cultural nuance directly tied to relationship vocabulary. In Vietnam, relationship hierarchies are embedded in pronouns (anh/chị/em), while German uses 'du/Sie' as a binary. This contrast often surprises Vietnamese learners and is worth a brief class discussion.

homework.description: Learners complete a written task in two parts: Part A – a structured writing exercise using weil-clauses, and Part B – a reflective vocabulary task using their personal relationship web from class.
exercises: Part A – Schreib 6 Sätze mit 'weil': Complete six sentence stems about feelings with appropriate reasons using 'weil' (e.g., 'Ich bin müde, weil...' / 'Meine Mutter ist stolz, weil...'). Learners must use at least 6 different emotion words from the target vocabulary list.

Part B – Mein Beziehungsnetz: Write a short paragraph (5–8 sentences) about one important person in your life using the relationship web from class. Include: who the person is, how you know them, what they are like (2 adjectives), and how they make you feel (using weil-clause). Use the sentence starter card as support if needed.

Part C – Vokabellernkarte: Create vocabulary flashcards for 10 new words from this week. Each card must include: German word with article (for nouns), Vietnamese translation, and one example sentence. Learners are encouraged to use a spaced-repetition app (e.g., Anki) if available.

formative: Emoji Bingo game performance: teacher observes whether learners correctly identify emotion words from Vietnamese/German definitions (Session 1)
Circulating during pair work for relationship card matching: teacher checks possessive pronoun gender agreement and weil-clause verb position

Exit ticket sticky notes: teacher reviews each note to identify learners who have not yet internalized weil-clause structure or key vocabulary – these learners are flagged for additional support at the start of next week
Oral monitoring during 'Mein Beziehungsnetz' presentation: teacher notes fluency, vocabulary use, and accuracy of weil-constructions per learner using a simple ✓/△/✗ checklist
assessment.summative: End-of-week short assessment (to be administered at the start of Week 13): A 15-minute written quiz consisting of (1) matching 10 emotion words to their Vietnamese translations, (2) completing 5 sentences with the correct form of possessive pronouns, (3) rewriting 4 simple sentences by adding a 'weil'-clause with logical content, and (4) one short writing task: describe a person in your life in 4 sentences using vocabulary and grammar from Week 12.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a pre-filled sentence frame card for all speaking and writing tasks (e.g., 'Ich bin ___, weil mein/e ___ ___.'). Allow use of bilingual vocabulary list (German-Vietnamese) during all practice activities. During pair work, pair struggling learners with a supportive peer rather than a high-performing one. For the weil-clause, use a physical 'verb parking' visual: a small red 'parking' sign that learners can physically place at the end of their written clause to remember verb-final position. Reduce homework Part B to 4 sentences minimum. In the Bingo activity, allow struggling learners to keep the vocabulary chart open.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Extension task during controlled practice: after completing the card matching, advanced learners write a short paragraph describing their own family using all three semantic groups of relationship vocabulary without sentence starter support. For the weil-clause activity, introduce the contrast with 'denn' (coordination, no word-order change): 'Ich bin glücklich, denn meine Familie ist gesund.' Ask advanced learners to rewrite 3 of their weil-sentences using 'denn' and explain the word-order difference. Homework extension: write a short dialogue (8 turns) between two friends discussing how they feel about a shared situation (e.g., a party, an exam, moving apartments), using at least 5 emotion words and 3 weil-clauses naturally embedded in conversation.

review_from_previous: Week 10 – Possessive pronouns (mein/dein/sein/ihr) in nominative and accusative: these are directly needed for describing relationships in Week 12
Week 9 – Present tense of reflexive verbs (sich vorstellen, sich fühlen): 'sich fühlen' is a core verb in this week's topic
Week 8 – Basic adjective predicative use (Das ist schön / Er ist nett): expanded in Week 12 to describe people's character in relationships
Week 6 – Family vocabulary (A1 review): foundational for the relationship web activity and semantic extension in Week 12
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 13 topic: 'Alltag und Termine – Verabredungen machen und absagen'. Learners will extend their relationship vocabulary into social planning contexts, using temporal expressions and modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen) to make and decline appointments. The emotional vocabulary from Week 12 will reappear when learners express how they feel about plans (e.g., 'Ich kann leider nicht kommen, weil ich müde bin.'). Introduce the bridge phrase at end of Week 12: 'Was machst du am Wochenende?' to prime the transition.

learning_objectives: Can describe personal future plans using 'werden + Infinitiv' and 'Präsens mit Zeitangabe' in simple sentences
Can express intentions and wishes about work, travel, and daily life using modal verbs 'wollen' and 'möchten'
Can understand and respond to simple questions about future plans in a short conversation or written text
prerequisite_knowledge: Present tense conjugation of regular and common irregular verbs (Week 1–5)
Modal verbs 'können', 'müssen', 'wollen', 'möchten' in present tense (Week 8)
Basic time expressions: heute, morgen, nächste Woche, nächstes Jahr (Week 6)
Vocabulary for professions and daily activities (Week 10–11)
Simple sentence structure: Subject-Verb-Object and verb-second rule (Week 3)

sessions.title: Träume und Pläne – Einführung in Zukunftspläne

activities.title: Traumbilder – Was siehst du in deiner Zukunft?
activities.description: Teacher displays 6–8 images on slides or printed cards depicting common future scenarios relevant to Vietnamese adult learners: a wedding, a new apartment, an airplane, a university diploma, a promotion at work, a trip to Europe, a baby, and a new car. Learners work in pairs and discuss in Vietnamese or simple German which images represent their own dreams. Pairs then share one image with the class using the sentence stem 'Ich möchte ... .' Teacher writes responses on the whiteboard to activate prior modal verb knowledge and create a visual word bank.
materials: Printed image cards or PowerPoint slide with 8 future-scenario images

activities.title: Werden + Infinitiv – Die Zukunft auf Deutsch
activities.description: Teacher introduces 'werden + Infinitiv' as the primary future tense construction using a structured mini-poster displayed on the projector. Full conjugation table of 'werden' (ich werde, du wirst, er/sie/es wird, wir werden, ihr werdet, sie/Sie werden) is presented with colour-coding. Teacher gives 5 example sentences directly relevant to learner lives: 'Ich werde nächstes Jahr Deutsch lernen.', 'Sie wird in Deutschland arbeiten.', 'Wir werden eine Reise machen.', 'Er wird einen neuen Job finden.', 'Du wirst bald heiraten.' Teacher highlights the verb-bracket rule (werden in position 2, Infinitiv at the end) using bracket notation on the board. Contrast with Präsens + Zeitangabe (e.g., 'Morgen lerne ich Deutsch.') is briefly shown to demonstrate both options are natural and correct at A2 level. Vietnamese metalanguage note: teacher briefly explains that 'werden' functions similarly to 'sẽ' in Vietnamese future constructions to aid comprehension.
materials: Whiteboard with colour markers for verb bracket notation
Handout A: 'werden + Infinitiv' reference card with conjugation table and 6 example sentences

activities.title: Satzbausteine – Puzzlesätze mit 'werden'
activities.description: Learners receive Handout B containing 10 scrambled sentences. Each sentence is broken into word/phrase tiles printed in a table that learners must cut or number in the correct order to form grammatically correct future sentences. Examples include: 'nächstes Jahr / werde / ich / nach Deutschland / fliegen', 'wird / meine Schwester / ein Baby / bekommen', 'werden / wir / eine neue Wohnung / kaufen'. After individual work (5 minutes), learners compare answers with a partner. Teacher conducts whole-class check by calling on random learners to read aloud, paying attention to pronunciation of 'werden' forms. Common errors—particularly verb placement—are addressed immediately on the board.
materials: Handout B: Scrambled sentence strips (10 sentences)

activities.title: Mein Zukunftsplan – Lückentextübung
activities.description: Learners receive Handout C: a short paragraph (8–10 sentences) written in the voice of a Vietnamese character named 'Linh' describing her future plans. Key verb forms are blanked out and learners must fill in the correct form of 'werden' or the infinitive as required. The paragraph includes varied content: career plans, travel, family, and study. Example: 'Nächstes Jahr _____ (werden) Linh nach Deutschland _____  (fahren). Sie _____ (werden) dort Deutsch _____ (lernen). Ihr Mann _____ (werden) einen neuen Job _____ (finden)...' Teacher monitors and provides individual feedback. Vietnamese-familiar context reduces cognitive load and increases engagement.

activities.title: Blitzrunde – Ein Satz über meine Zukunft
activities.description: Each learner says one sentence using 'werden + Infinitiv' about their own future. Teacher writes a sentence stem on the board: 'In einem Jahr werde ich ...' Learners go around the room quickly (30 seconds each). Teacher provides immediate positive correction only for 'werden' conjugation errors. This activity serves as informal formative assessment of uptake from the session. Teacher notes recurring errors for Session 2 review.

sessions.title: Über Zukunftspläne sprechen und schreiben

activities.title: Fehlerkorrektur-Karussell – Richtig oder falsch?
activities.description: Teacher projects 6 sentences on the board, some correct and some containing typical errors from Session 1 observation (e.g., wrong 'werden' form, infinitive in wrong position, missing infinitive). Learners work in pairs to identify and correct errors. Each pair writes corrections on a small whiteboard or paper. After 4 minutes, pairs swap papers and compare. Teacher reveals correct answers with explanation. This targets error patterns specific to Vietnamese learners, such as omitting the infinitive at the end or confusing 'wird' and 'werde'.
materials: Projector or whiteboard with 6 example sentences

activities.title: Zukunftswortschatz – Wörternetz und Kollokationen
activities.description: Teacher introduces and drills 15 target vocabulary items using a semantic web drawn on the board, organized into three clusters: (1) Lebensereignisse: heiraten, ein Kind bekommen, umziehen, eine Wohnung kaufen; (2) Beruf und Studium: einen Job finden, studieren, eine Ausbildung machen, Karriere machen; (3) Reisen und Freizeit: reisen, ins Ausland gehen, eine Sprache lernen, Urlaub machen. For each word, teacher models pronunciation and gives a sample sentence. Learners repeat chorally and individually. Flashcard drilling in pairs using printed mini-flashcards (word on one side, Vietnamese translation and example sentence on other side). Teacher emphasizes collocations (e.g., 'eine Ausbildung MACHEN', not 'haben') to prevent typical calque errors from Vietnamese.
materials: Handout D: Mini-flashcards (printed, 15 vocabulary items with Vietnamese translations)

activities.title: Interview: Was sind deine Pläne? – Strukturiertes Partnergespräch
activities.description: Learners receive Handout E: a structured interview guide with 6 questions about future plans. Questions progress from concrete/near-future to more personal/distant future: (1) Was machst du nächste Woche? (2) Was wirst du nächsten Monat machen? (3) Wo wirst du in einem Jahr wohnen? (4) Was für einen Job wirst du haben? (5) Wirst du heiraten oder eine Familie gründen? (6) Was ist dein größter Traum? Learner A interviews Learner B, taking brief notes in the provided grid, then they switch roles. Pairs are then regrouped: Learner A reports one interesting fact about Learner B to a new partner using third-person 'er/sie wird ...'. Teacher circulates and notes interesting or fluent responses to share with class at the end.
materials: Handout E: Interview-Leitfaden with 6 questions and note-taking grid

activities.title: Mein Zukunftsplan – Kurzer schriftlicher Text
activities.description: Learners write a short personal text (6–8 sentences) titled 'Meine Pläne für die Zukunft'. They must use: at least 3 'werden + Infinitiv' sentences, at least 1 'wollen/möchten' sentence, at least 2 different time expressions (nächstes Jahr, in fünf Jahren, bald, etc.), and at least 4 vocabulary items from Handout D. A structured writing frame is provided on Handout F for learners who need support, with sentence starters: 'In einem Jahr werde ich ...', 'Ich möchte ...', 'Vielleicht werde ich ... '. Advanced learners are encouraged to write without the frame and add a reason using 'weil' (preview of B1 content as enrichment). Teacher collects texts at end of session for written feedback before next lesson.
materials: Handout F: Schreibrahmen 'Meine Pläne für die Zukunft'

activities.title: Lernzielcheck – Daumen-Feedback und Zusammenfassung
activities.description: Teacher reads aloud the three can-do statements from the learning objectives. After each statement, learners show a thumbs up (I can do this confidently), thumbs sideways (I can do this with some help), or thumbs down (I need more practice). Teacher notes overall class confidence. Teacher briefly summarizes the two key structures learned ('werden + Infinitiv' and modal verbs for plans) and previews homework. Any urgent questions are addressed in the final minute.

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Futur I: 'werden + Infinitiv' (full conjugation, verb-bracket rule, word order in main and subordinate-ready clauses); contrast with Präsens + Zeitangabe for near future; review of modal verbs 'wollen' and 'möchten' for expressing intentions
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland), discussing future plans openly—such as career ambitions, moving cities, or family planning—is common in casual conversation and is not considered overly personal at the acquaintance level. The concept of 'Lebensplanung' (life planning) is culturally valued, and many Germans create structured timelines for major life goals. Apprenticeship ('Ausbildung') is a highly respected vocational path in Germany and Austria, unlike in Vietnam where university degrees are traditionally prioritized—this cultural difference is worth discussing with learners. In Switzerland, multilingualism affects future planning for language learners, as Swiss residents may need German, French, or Italian depending on the canton. The word 'Zukunft' (future) also appears in political and environmental discourse ('Zukunft der Erde'), which connects to broader DACH cultural literacy.

homework.description: Learners complete two written tasks and one listening task to reinforce 'werden + Infinitiv' and Zukunftspläne vocabulary before the next lesson.
exercises: Exercise 1 – Schreiben: Write a short text (8–10 sentences) about the future plans of a family member or friend. Use 'werden + Infinitiv' at least 4 times and include time expressions. Title: 'Die Pläne von [Name]'.
Exercise 2 – Grammatik: Complete the 15-sentence 'werden' conjugation and word order exercise from the course workbook (page 87, exercises 1–3).

Exercise 3 – Hören: Listen to the DW Learn German A2 podcast episode 'Zukunftspläne' (available free at learngerman.dw.com) and answer 5 comprehension questions on the provided worksheet (Handout G, distributed at end of class).

Exercise 4 – Vokabeln: Review all 20 vocabulary items from Handout D using the flashcard method (cover Vietnamese side, produce German; then reverse). Prepare to use 5 of these words in sentences orally at the start of next session.

formative: Observation of oral production during 'Blitzrunde' activity (Session 1): teacher listens for correct 'werden' conjugation and verb-final infinitive placement
Pair monitoring during structured interview (Session 2): teacher uses a simple checklist to note correct use of target structures and vocabulary
Thumbs feedback at end of Session 2: teacher records overall class self-assessment against three can-do statements
Collection of written texts from Session 2 productive task for teacher written feedback (returned with annotations before Week 16)
Error analysis of scrambled sentence activity (Session 1) to identify persistent word-order issues for Session 2 review
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (10 minutes, administered at start of Week 16 Session 1): Learners receive a short task with three parts: (A) Fill in 5 blanks with the correct form of 'werden' in context; (B) Unscramble 3 future tense sentences; (C) Write 3 sentences about their own future using different time expressions and vocabulary from the week. Scoring: 10 points total (A: 5 points, B: 3 points, C: 2 points for content + accuracy). Pass mark: 7/10. Results used to identify learners needing additional support.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a laminated reference card with the full 'werden' conjugation table and a model text to keep on their desk during all activities. Reduce writing task to 4–5 sentences with mandatory use of the structured writing frame (Handout F). During pair work, strategically pair struggling learners with patient mid-level peers rather than the strongest learners. For homework, allow learners to write in a mix of German and Vietnamese with a note explaining meaning, then revise to full German before submission. Provide pre-taught vocabulary with picture support and audio recordings of all new vocabulary (QR code on handout linking to teacher-recorded audio). During the controlled practice sentence puzzle, pre-cut sentence strips are provided so learners focus on ordering, not cutting.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge extension: After the structured interview, advanced learners write up their partner's responses as a third-person paragraph without using the sentence frame, and add a reason clause using 'weil' or 'denn' (e.g., 'Sie wird Medizin studieren, weil sie Ärztin werden möchte.'). In the productive writing task, require 10 sentences with at least one conditional or reason clause. Provide an additional vocabulary list with 10 higher-level Zukunft-related words: der Ehrgeiz, verwirklichen, planen, das Ziel, erreichen, die Herausforderung, beschließen, der Fortschritt, nachhaltig, investieren. Advanced learners may also be invited to present their future plan to the class as a 60-second informal speech in the next session.

review_from_previous: Week 8 – Modal verbs 'wollen', 'möchten', 'können', 'müssen': revisited in warm-up and vocabulary drilling activities to contrast with 'werden'
Week 6 – Time expressions (morgen, nächste Woche, nächstes Jahr): explicitly recycled in all example sentences and the interview activity
Week 10–11 – Professions and daily activities vocabulary: recycled in future plan contexts (e.g., 'Ich werde Lehrerin werden', 'Er wird im Büro arbeiten')
Week 3 – Verb-second word order rule: reinforced through error correction activity and scrambled sentence task as 'werden' creates a new context for applying this rule
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 16 will introduce 'Wenn-Sätze' (conditional clauses) and Konjunktiv II for hypothetical future scenarios ('Wenn ich viel Geld hätte, würde ich ...'), building directly on the Zukunftspläne vocabulary and 'werden/würden' forms introduced this week. Learners are encouraged to bring their Week 15 writing tasks to Week 16 as a base text for expanding with conditional sentences.

learning_objectives: Can demonstrate readiness for all four Goethe A2 exam modules (Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen) by completing timed practice tasks with at least 60% accuracy
Can produce a short written message (e-mail, note, or form) of 30–40 words using familiar vocabulary and A2 grammar structures within a time limit
Can participate in a guided spoken interaction (Prüfungsgespräch) by asking and answering personal questions about daily life, family, work, and free time with acceptable fluency and intelligibility
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic sentence structure: Subject-Verb-Object and verb-second word order
Present tense of regular and common irregular verbs (haben, sein, werden, modal verbs)
Simple past of sein and haben; Perfekt of common verbs
Definite and indefinite articles in Nominativ, Akkusativ, Dativ
Personal pronouns, possessive pronouns (mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr)
Common A2 vocabulary fields: family, home, food, shopping, health, transport, leisure, work, time expressions
Subordinating conjunctions: weil, dass, wenn; coordinating conjunctions: und, aber, oder, denn
W-questions and yes/no questions
Comparative and superlative of adjectives (basic forms)
Separable and inseparable verbs in present tense and Perfekt
Numbers, dates, times, prices
Familiarity with Goethe A2 exam format from previous lessons

sessions.title: Leseverstehen & Hörverstehen – Prüfungssimulation Teil 1

activities.title: Prüfungsangst abbauen – Blitzrunde
activities.description: Teacher writes 'Prüfung' on the board and elicits feelings in German. Each learner says one sentence: 'Bei einer Prüfung fühle ich mich…' or 'Ich bin nervös/ruhig/aufgeregt, weil…' Teacher acknowledges responses and briefly reminds learners of exam structure (4 modules, total 70 minutes + speaking). Post a simple visual overview of the Goethe A2 exam components on the board for reference throughout the lesson. This activity builds confidence and activates schema.
materials: Poster or slide: Goethe A2 Prüfungsübersicht (Lesen 30 Min, Hören 20 Min, Schreiben 30 Min, Sprechen ~15 Min)

activities.title: Leseverstehen – Timed Practice (Teile 1–3)
activities.description: Distribute a full Goethe A2 Leseverstehen practice paper (authentic or closely modelled). Learners work individually under timed conditions: Teil 1 (Kurztexte, 5 items, 7 min), Teil 2 (Anzeigen zuordnen, 5 items, 7 min), Teil 3 (Lesetext mit Multiple Choice, 5 items, 8 min). Teacher circulates silently, noting common difficulties. Vietnamese learner tip: remind them that key words in options often paraphrase the text – underlining strategy is encouraged. After time is up, learners compare answers in pairs briefly before full class correction.
materials: Goethe A2 Leseverstehen Übungstest (printed or projected)

activities.title: Leseverstehen Auswertung & Strategie-Tipps
activities.description: Teacher goes through answers using a projected answer key. For each wrong answer, teacher models the reading strategy: (1) Read question first, (2) Scan for key words, (3) Eliminate wrong options. Teacher highlights 3 common traps Vietnamese learners face: false cognates with English, German compound nouns, and negation patterns (nicht, kein, nie). Learners self-mark and calculate their score (/15). Teacher records class average on board.

activities.title: Übergang: Hörverstehen ankündigen
activities.description: Teacher briefly explains that in Session 2 the class will practise Hörverstehen and Schreiben. Learners are asked to note one reading strategy they will use again. Quick show of hands: 'Wer hat mehr als 10 Punkte?' This builds momentum and prepares learners for the next session.

sessions.title: Hörverstehen, Schreiben & Sprechen – Prüfungssimulation Teil 2

activities.title: Hörverstehen – Timed Practice (Teile 1–3)
activities.description: Play a Goethe A2 Hörverstehen practice recording. Teil 1: Short conversations, learners tick richtig/falsch (5 items). Teil 2: Telephone messages or announcements, learners choose correct answer (5 items). Teil 3: Interview or conversation, learners match or fill in (5 items). Each part is played twice as per exam conditions. Teacher manages audio from laptop/speaker. Vietnamese learner tip: remind them to read the questions before each audio begins. After the audio, learners self-correct using the answer key. Teacher discusses any phonological challenges: German vowel sounds (ü, ö, ä) and fast speech reduction.
materials: Laptop and speaker or language lab

activities.title: Schreiben – E-Mail oder Kurzmitteilung verfassen
activities.description: Learners receive a Schreiben prompt modelled on Goethe A2 Teil 1 (semi-formal e-mail reply, ~30 words) and Teil 2 (short informal note or message, ~30 words). They have 20 minutes total for both. Teacher writes the assessment criteria on the board: (1) Inhalt – alle Punkte angesprochen? (2) Kommunikative Gestaltung – verständlich? (3) Formale Richtigkeit – Grammatik und Wortschatz. Vietnamese learner tip: remind them to use a greeting (Liebe/r…, Sehr geehrte/r…), body with all required points, and closing (Mit freundlichen Grüßen / Viele Grüße). Warn against copying the prompt verbatim. After writing, pairs exchange texts and give one positive feedback and one suggestion using a peer-checklist.

activities.title: Sprechen – Partnerübung: Aufgabe 1 & 2 simulieren
activities.description: Learners work in pairs to simulate Goethe A2 Sprechen Aufgabe 1 (sich vorstellen – introduce yourself using 6 prompt cards: Name, Wohnort, Familie, Arbeit/Schule, Hobbys, Sprachen) and Aufgabe 2 (Alltagsgespräch – one learner makes a request or suggestion, partner responds and asks a follow-up question, e.g. 'Ich möchte ein Restaurant empfehlen. Was meinst du?'). Teacher assigns roles and circulates, taking brief notes on fluency, accuracy, and interaction. After practice, teacher gives 2–3 pieces of whole-class feedback focused on the most common errors observed (e.g., verb-end in subordinate clauses, missing articles). Learners note corrections in their Prüfungsheft.
materials: Sprechen Aufgabe 2: Situation cards (3 different scenarios)

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Consolidation of A2 grammar for exam accuracy: (1) Verb-second word order and inversion after adverbials (Heute gehe ich…); (2) Perfekt vs. Präteritum of haben/sein; (3) Modal verbs in present tense (müssen, können, dürfen, wollen, sollen, möchten); (4) Dative case with common prepositions (mit, bei, nach, seit, von, zu, aus, gegenüber); (5) Subordinate clause word order with weil, dass, wenn; (6) Negation with nicht and kein/keine.
lesson_plans.cultural_note: The Goethe-Institut is a globally respected German cultural institution headquartered in Munich, Germany, with branches in Vietnam (Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City). The Goethe A2 certificate is internationally recognised and accepted for visa applications (e.g., family reunification to Germany or Austria) and university preparatory programmes in DACH countries. Learners should know that the Sprechen module is conducted face-to-face with an examiner and that polite, direct communication is expected – in contrast to the more indirect communication style common in Vietnamese culture. In DACH contexts, it is normal to make direct requests and to say 'nein' politely but clearly. Practising this directness helps Vietnamese learners feel more comfortable in the exam speaking tasks.

homework.description: Complete a full timed Goethe A2 mock exam at home using the provided practice materials. Simulate real exam conditions: no dictionary, no phone, strict time limits. Then write one short self-reflection in German (4–6 sentences): Was war leicht? Was war schwer? Was muss ich noch üben?
exercises: Leseverstehen: Complete Übungstest 2 (alle drei Teile, 30 Minuten)
Hörverstehen: Listen to Übungstest 2 audio and complete tasks (20 Minuten) – use the Goethe-Institut free online materials or provided USB/download link
Schreiben: Write a 30-word e-mail reply to a prompt about cancelling an appointment with a reason and an alternative suggestion
Sprechen Vorbereitung: Record yourself on your phone doing Aufgabe 1 (sich vorstellen, ~1 minute). Listen back and note 2 things to improve
Vokabeln: Review all vocabulary from Weeks 12–16 using your vocabulary notebook or flashcard app (Anki / Quizlet). Focus on Lernfelder: Alltag, Wohnen, Gesundheit, Freizeit, Arbeit
Grammatik: Complete grammar consolidation worksheet (10 gap-fill sentences covering modal verbs, Dativ prepositions, and Perfekt)

formative: Teacher observation during Sprechen pair practice: note fluency, accuracy, and interaction quality using a simple observation checklist
Leseverstehen self-scoring: learners track their score and identify which part (Teil 1/2/3) was most difficult
Hörverstehen self-scoring: same format – learners flag items they found difficult for discussion
Peer-feedback on Schreiben using the three-criteria checklist (Inhalt, Gestaltung, Sprache)
Exit ticket (last 2 minutes): each learner writes on a sticky note 'Ich kann _____ gut' and 'Ich muss _____ noch üben' – teacher reads these before next lesson
assessment.summative: End-of-week full mock Goethe A2 Prüfung (simulated under exam conditions, 70 minutes written + 15 minutes spoken). All four modules assessed. Written modules scored against Goethe A2 official marking criteria (each module worth 25 points, total 100 points, pass mark 60). Speaking assessed using a simplified rubric based on Goethe descriptors: Kommunikative Gestaltung (0–5), Aussprache und Intonation (0–5), Formale Richtigkeit (0–5). Results returned with written feedback within one week. Learners who score below 60 receive a targeted remediation plan for the following week.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a 'Prüfungshilfe' reference card with key exam phrases, a grammar summary table (verb conjugations, case endings, common prepositions), and a writing template with sentence starters for the Schreiben module. During Sprechen practice, pair struggling learners with a supportive peer and allow them to use prompt cards. Offer an extended practice version of Leseverstehen with 5 additional comprehension questions before timed conditions. In homework, allow struggling learners to use a dictionary for the grammar worksheet only (not for the mock exam). Suggest additional resources: Goethe-Institut free A2 practice tests at goethe.de/pruefungen, DW Deutsch A2 interactive exercises, and the 'Deutsch für dich' app.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to write a longer e-mail (50–60 words) using complex sentence connectors (obwohl, damit, sodass). During Sprechen, introduce Aufgabe 3 (Bitten und Reagieren) with more complex scenarios requiring negotiation or disagreement. Ask them to write brief examiner-style feedback comments on their partner's Schreiben using the Goethe criteria. As extension homework, have them listen to an authentic B1-level Goethe Hörverstehen sample and identify which items would be above A2 level, justifying their reasoning in German.

review_from_previous: Week 12 – Wohnen und Haushalt: vocabulary for rooms, furniture, household tasks (likely tested in Lesen/Hören scenarios)
Week 13 – Gesundheit und Körper: medical vocabulary, making appointments, describing symptoms (common in A2 Schreiben and Sprechen tasks)
Week 14 – Reisen und Verkehr: transport vocabulary, reading timetables and tickets, buying tickets (frequent topic in Goethe A2 Lesen)
Week 15 – Arbeit und Beruf: job titles, work routines, formal e-mail register (directly relevant to Schreiben Teil 1 and Sprechen sich vorstellen)
Weeks 1–10 core grammar: all tenses reviewed at A2 level, article cases, common prepositions
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 17 will focus on post-exam reflection, results analysis, and bridging to A2+ or B1 preparation. Learners will identify their personal grammar and vocabulary gaps from the mock exam results and begin targeted self-study plans. The topic will introduce first B1 concepts: Konjunktiv II für höfliche Bitten (würde + Infinitiv, könnte), Passiv in present tense, and extended spoken interaction (Diskussion, Meinung äußern). This provides a motivating bridge from A2 consolidation towards the B1 learning journey.

learning_objectives: Can describe their current job or desired profession using appropriate B1-level vocabulary and sentence structures
Can understand and respond to questions in a job interview context, including strengths, weaknesses, and career goals
Can read and extract key information from a German job advertisement (Stellenanzeige) and write a short cover letter paragraph
prerequisite_knowledge: A2-level vocabulary related to daily routines and simple work tasks
Basic present tense and perfect tense (Perfekt) conjugation
Modal verbs: können, müssen, wollen, dürfen at A2 level
Simple sentence structure with subordinate clauses using 'weil' and 'dass'
Basic adjective endings in nominative and accusative cases
Numbers, dates, and time expressions for scheduling contexts

sessions.title: Berufe & Stellenanzeigen – Wortschatz und Leseverstehen

activities.title: Berufe-Raten: Was bin ich?
activities.description: Teacher shows 8 images of people in different professions (Arzt, Ingenieur, Buchhalter, Lehrer, Softwareentwickler, Krankenpfleger, Anwalt, Marketingmanager) on flashcards or projected slides. Learners work in pairs: one learner describes the job in simple German sentences (e.g. 'Diese Person arbeitet im Büro. Sie benutzt viel den Computer.'), and the partner guesses the profession. Vietnamese learners are encouraged to use German they already know rather than translating directly. After 5 minutes, pairs share the most surprising or difficult profession with the class.
materials: Berufe-Bildkarten (8 profession image cards, printed or digital)

activities.title: Wortfeld Beruf & Karriere – Strukturiertes Einführen
activities.description: Teacher presents 20 target vocabulary items using a structured mind map on the board divided into four clusters: (1) Berufsbezeichnungen (job titles), (2) Arbeitsplatz & Bedingungen (workplace conditions), (3) Karriereschritte (career steps), (4) Bewerbung (application process). Each word is presented with its article, plural form, and one example sentence. Special attention is given to German compound nouns (e.g., die Stellenanzeige, der Arbeitsvertrag, die Gehaltsvorstellung) which Vietnamese learners often find challenging due to the absence of compounding in Vietnamese. Learners copy the mind map into their vocabulary notebooks using a colour-coding system: nouns in blue, verbs in green, adjectives in red. Teacher models pronunciation of difficult words and learners repeat chorally.
materials: Whiteboard with pre-drawn mind map structure

activities.title: Stellenanzeige lesen und verstehen
activities.description: Learners receive two authentic-style German job advertisements: one for a 'Projektmanager (m/w/d)' at a medium-sized IT company in Munich, and one for a 'Pflegefachkraft' at a hospital in Vienna. The ads include standard sections: Ihr Profil, Wir bieten, Aufgaben, Bewerbung. Teacher pre-teaches three key reading strategies in Vietnamese L1 support note on the handout: (1) Skimming for job type and location, (2) Scanning for required qualifications, (3) Close reading for benefits and conditions. Learners first skim both ads (2 minutes), then complete a T-chart comparison worksheet with categories: Anforderungen (Requirements), Aufgaben (Tasks), Vorteile (Benefits). Learners work individually, then compare answers with a partner. Teacher conducts whole-class feedback, focusing on vocabulary items learners found unclear and common misreadings caused by false cognates or German-specific abbreviations (m/w/d, VB, PKW-Führerschein).
materials: Two job advertisement handouts (authentic-style, B1 adapted)
Vocabulary glossary strip at bottom of handout with 8 difficult terms translated into Vietnamese

activities.title: Sprachbausteine: Anforderungen beschreiben mit Modalverben und Konjunktiv II
activities.description: Using sentences extracted directly from the two job ads, teacher draws learners' attention to how requirements are expressed in German job advertisements: (1) Modal verbs in present tense: 'Sie müssen teamfähig sein', 'Sie sollten Erfahrung haben', (2) Konjunktiv II for polite/ideal requirements: 'Idealerweise hätten Sie bereits Berufserfahrung', 'Wir würden uns über Ihre Bewerbung freuen'. Teacher writes a contrastive table on the board: Vietnamese equivalent structures are briefly noted (e.g., cần phải / nên có) to build conceptual bridges. Learners then complete a gap-fill exercise using 6 sentences from job ads where they choose the correct modal verb or Konjunktiv II form. Answers checked as a class.

sessions.title: Das Vorstellungsgespräch – Hören, Sprechen und Schreiben

activities.title: Ein Vorstellungsgespräch hören
activities.description: Learners listen to a scripted B1-level audio recording (approximately 3.5 minutes) of a job interview between a HR manager and an applicant for an office management position at a German company. The audio features standard job interview questions and answers using natural but clear spoken German. Listening is done in two rounds: Round 1 (global understanding): Learners listen and answer 3 true/false/not mentioned questions about the candidate's background. Round 2 (detailed understanding): Learners listen again and fill in a structured note-taking grid with columns for: Frage (Question), Antwort des Bewerbers (Applicant's answer), Schlüsselwörter (Key words heard). Teacher pauses audio after each question-answer pair in Round 2. Vietnamese learners are reminded that German interview speech may include indirect politeness markers and Konjunktiv II forms which differ from direct Vietnamese communication styles – a brief cultural note is given before listening.
materials: Audio file: 'Vorstellungsgespräch_B1.mp3' (teacher-prepared or from DaF textbook)
Listening task worksheet with true/false questions and note-taking grid
Audio player or computer with speakers

activities.title: Rollenspiel: Das Vorstellungsgespräch
activities.description: Learners practise a job interview roleplay in pairs. Each pair receives a role card: one learner is the HR Manager (Personalchef/-in) and one is the Bewerber/-in (applicant). Role cards contain: For the HR Manager – 6 interview questions to ask (e.g. 'Warum bewerben Sie sich bei uns?', 'Was sind Ihre Stärken und Schwächen?', 'Wo sehen Sie sich in fünf Jahren?', 'Welche Erfahrungen haben Sie in diesem Bereich?', 'Was sind Ihre Gehaltsvorstellungen?', 'Haben Sie noch Fragen an uns?'). For the Applicant – a brief fictional CV (Lebenslauf) with name, education, work history, and skills. Learners are given 3 minutes to prepare using a sentence scaffold bank provided on the back of their role card (e.g., 'Ich habe X Jahre Erfahrung in...', 'Meine größte Stärke ist...', 'Ich würde gerne...', 'Ich interessiere mich für diese Stelle, weil...'). Pairs then conduct the roleplay for 5 minutes. Teacher circulates, takes notes on errors for delayed correction. Roles are then swapped. After both rounds, teacher conducts brief whole-class feedback using the board to address 3-4 common grammar or vocabulary errors observed, without identifying individual learners.
materials: Role cards (Personalchef and Bewerber versions, laminated or printed)
Fictional CV for applicant role (A5 handout)
Sentence scaffold bank on role card reverse

activities.title: Ein Motivationsabsatz schreiben
activities.description: Learners write a single motivational paragraph (80–100 words) as part of a cover letter (Bewerbungsschreiben) responding to one of the two job advertisements from Session 1. Teacher first models the writing process using a think-aloud: projecting a sample paragraph and deconstructing its structure – (1) Opening: why you are applying, (2) Middle: 2-3 relevant qualifications/experiences, (3) Closing: expression of interest and availability. A writing frame is provided on the handout with sentence starters for each section. Learners write individually. Teacher monitors and gives brief individual feedback on structure and vocabulary use. Two or three volunteers share their paragraph aloud with the class at the end.
materials: Writing frame handout with sentence starters and word count guide
Dictionary access (learner smartphones permitted for this task)

vocabulary_target: teamfähig (adj.) (able to work in a team)
sich bewerben um + Akk. (to apply for)
lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Konjunktiv II (würden + Infinitiv, hätten, wären, könnten) for polite requests, hypothetical statements, and expressing wishes in professional contexts; revision and extension of modal verbs (müssen, sollen, dürfen, können, mögen, wollen) in job advertisement and interview language
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In DACH countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland), job applications traditionally include a formal Anschreiben, a detailed tabellarischer Lebenslauf, and copies of Zeugnisse (certificates/references). Unlike Vietnam, where personal connections (quan hệ) often play a significant informal role, German hiring processes tend to emphasise formal qualifications and documented experience. A professional photo on the CV (Bewerbungsfoto) is still standard in Germany and Austria, though this practice differs from many other countries. The greeting 'Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren' in written applications and the formal 'Sie' throughout interviews are mandatory – switching to 'du' prematurely is considered unprofessional. In Switzerland, salary negotiation is somewhat more open, while in Germany it is common to provide a Gehaltsvorstellung only when explicitly requested. Punctuality for job interviews is critical: arriving 5–10 minutes early is expected; being late – even by a few minutes – can eliminate a candidate from consideration.

homework.description: Learners complete a full motivational paragraph revision based on in-class teacher feedback, then record themselves answering two standard interview questions (audio recording on smartphone) and complete an online vocabulary practice set.
exercises: Revise and expand the in-class Motivationsabsatz to 120–150 words, incorporating at least 5 vocabulary items from the week's target list and one example of Konjunktiv II. Submit via class messaging app or email.

Record a 60–90 second audio response to the following two interview questions using the sentence scaffolds provided: (1) 'Warum bewerben Sie sich bei uns?' (2) 'Was sind Ihre größten Stärken?' Upload to the class shared folder or send to teacher.

Complete Vocabulary Set 1 on the class Quizlet deck 'B1 Beruf & Karriere – Woche 1' (25 flashcards): complete the Learn mode and achieve at least 80% on the Test mode. Take a screenshot of your score and share in the class group.
Read the short text 'Arbeiten in Deutschland – Was ist anders?' (provided as PDF, 250 words, B1 level) and write 3 sentences in German summarising the most surprising information for you personally.

formative: Observation during Berufe-Raten warm-up: teacher notes range of vocabulary learners can spontaneously produce about professions
T-chart completion accuracy during Stellenanzeige reading task checked against answer key during pair comparison phase
Gap-fill grammar exercise self-checked against board answers; teacher notes common errors for re-teaching
Teacher circulates during roleplay and records recurring pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary errors on notepad for end-of-session feedback
Spot-check 3–4 writing frames during individual writing task to assess structure and grammar use
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (Week 1, to be administered in the final 15 minutes of the next class session): Learners receive a new job advertisement (not previously seen) and complete: (1) 5 comprehension questions in German (3 points each), (2) a gap-fill of 8 sentences using modal verbs and Konjunktiv II (2 points each), (3) write a 80-word motivation paragraph responding to the ad (10 points assessed on vocabulary range, grammatical accuracy, and discourse coherence). Total: 41 points. Passing threshold: 25 points (approximately 60%).

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a bilingual German-Vietnamese vocabulary glossary strip at the bottom of all reading handouts. Offer an extended sentence scaffold bank with 10 additional starters for the speaking roleplay and writing tasks. During listening tasks, allow one additional replay of the audio. For the grammar focus, provide a simplified reference table comparing modal verb meanings in German and Vietnamese equivalents. Pair struggling learners with a slightly stronger partner during pair work, but ensure the struggling learner takes the speaking role first in roleplay to build confidence. Reduce writing task minimum to 60 words. Provide a partially completed T-chart for the Stellenanzeige reading task as a scaffold.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to read one authentic job advertisement found independently online (e.g., from Stepstone.de or jobs.ch) and bring it to the next session for a brief 2-minute presentation explaining why they chose it and what qualifications it requires. During roleplay, remove the sentence scaffold bank and encourage fully spontaneous speech. Ask advanced learners to write a full three-paragraph cover letter (Anschreiben) rather than a single paragraph for homework, following the formal German letter format (Datum, Betreff, Anrede, Hauptteil, Schluss, Grußformel). Provide an extension grammar task on Konjunktiv II in indirect speech ('Er sagte, er hätte Erfahrung in...').

review_from_previous: A2 vocabulary for daily routines and workplaces – reactivated through the Berufe-Raten warm-up
Perfekt tense for describing past work experiences – reactivated in the roleplay (e.g., 'Ich habe drei Jahre bei X gearbeitet')
Modal verbs (können, müssen, sollen, wollen) from A2 – reviewed and extended in the grammar focus activity
Subordinate clauses with 'weil' and 'dass' – practised in speaking and writing tasks ('Ich bewerbe mich, weil...', 'Ich glaube, dass...')
Adjective vocabulary (positive personal qualities) from A2 – recycled and expanded with new B1 items (belastbar, teamfähig, zuverlässig)
