spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 2 will build on this week's Beruf & Karriere foundation by focusing on workplace communication: writing formal emails (formelle E-Mails) to colleagues and supervisors, understanding and using passive voice (Passiv) in professional contexts ('Die Aufgabe wird von mir erledigt'), and discussing workplace problems and solutions. The job advertisement vocabulary and interview language practised this week will be recycled in a Week 2 role-play scenario set inside a German office environment.

learning_objectives: Ich kann das Schul- und Hochschulsystem in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz beschreiben und vergleichen.
Ich kann über eigene Bildungserfahrungen sprechen und diese mit dem DACH-System vergleichen.
Ich kann authentische Texte über Bildungsthemen lesen und wichtige Informationen entnehmen sowie schriftlich zusammenfassen.
prerequisite_knowledge: Grundlegendes Vokabular zu Schule und Lernen (A2-Niveau)
Konjugation von Verben im Präsens, Präteritum und Perfekt
Verwendung von Komparativ und Superlativ für Vergleiche
Grundlegende Satzstruktur mit Nebensätzen (weil, dass, wenn)
Kenntnis geografischer Grundlagen zu Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz aus Woche 1

sessions.title: Das Schulsystem im DACH-Raum – Strukturen und Vergleiche

activities.title: Meine Schulzeit – Erinnerungen teilen
activities.description: Lernende erhalten Kärtchen mit Fragen wie 'Wie lange sind Sie zur Schule gegangen?', 'Welche Fächer mochten Sie am liebsten?' und 'Wann haben Sie die Schule abgeschlossen?'. In Paaren tauschen sie sich 3 Minuten auf Deutsch aus. Anschließend teilen zwei Paare ihre Antworten im Plenum. Die Lehrkraft notiert Schlüsselbegriffe an der Tafel und stellt dabei die Frage: 'Wie könnte das in Deutschland anders sein?'

activities.title: Infografik: Das deutsche Schulsystem
activities.description: Die Lehrkraft präsentiert eine Infografik des deutschen Schulsystems (Grundschule → Hauptschule/Realschule/Gymnasium/Gesamtschule → Berufsausbildung/Abitur → Hochschule). Lernende erhalten die Infografik als Handout. Die Lehrkraft erklärt schrittweise die Schultypen, deren Dauer und die wichtigsten Übergangspunkte. Lernende hören zu und ergänzen eine Lücken-Tabelle (Handout B) mit: Schultyp, Alter der Schüler, Abschluss, Möglichkeit danach. Vietnamese-sprachige Glossar-Karten werden verteilt, um Schlüsselbegriffe wie 'die Grundschule', 'das Abitur', 'die Berufsausbildung' zu verankern.

activities.title: Leseverstehen: Österreich und die Schweiz im Vergleich
activities.description: Lernende erhalten zwei kurze Lesetexte (je ca. 150 Wörter, B1-Niveau) – einen über das österreichische Bildungssystem und einen über das schweizerische. In Zweiergruppen liest jeweils eine Person Text A (Österreich) und die andere Text B (Schweiz). Danach erklären sie sich gegenseitig die wichtigsten Punkte (Jigsaw-Methode). Anschließend füllen sie gemeinsam eine Vergleichstabelle (Handout C) mit drei Spalten: Deutschland / Österreich / Schweiz aus und notieren Gemeinsamkeiten und Unterschiede.
materials: Lesetext A: Das Bildungssystem in Österreich (Handout C1)
Lesetext B: Das Bildungssystem in der Schweiz (Handout C2)

activities.title: Vergleiche ausdrücken – Sprachliche Mittel
activities.description: Die Lehrkraft präsentiert an der Tafel wichtige Satzmuster für Vergleiche: 'Im Gegensatz zu Deutschland hat Österreich...', 'Sowohl...als auch...', 'Während in der Schweiz..., ist in Deutschland...', 'Ähnlich wie in Vietnam...'. Lernende erhalten Handout E mit diesen Strukturen und zwei Beispielsätzen pro Struktur. Kurze Übung: Lernende schreiben in 3 Minuten 2 eigene Vergleichssätze aus ihrer Vergleichstabelle und lesen diese dem Partner vor. Die Lehrkraft gibt sofortiges Feedback zur Grammatik.

sessions.title: Hochschule, Ausbildung und Berufsschule – Wege nach der Schule

activities.title: Bildungsweg-Rätsel
activities.description: Lernende erhalten Kärtchen mit verschiedenen Bildungsbiografien (z.B. 'Anna, 22, macht eine Ausbildung zur Krankenpflegerin an der Berufsschule in Wien'). In Gruppen von 3 ordnen sie die Kärtchen dem richtigen Bildungsweg zu (Berufsausbildung, Fachhochschule, Universität, duales System). Dies aktiviert Vokabular aus Session 1 und führt in neue Begriffe ein. Die Lehrkraft klärt Unklarheiten im Plenum.

activities.title: Hörverstehen: Zwei junge Menschen berichten
activities.description: Lernende hören zwei kurze Audio-Interviews (je ca. 2 Minuten): Interview 1 mit Jonas, der eine duale Ausbildung als IT-Techniker in München macht, und Interview 2 mit Lena, die an der Universität Zürich Wirtschaft studiert. Vor dem Hören aktivieren die Lernenden ihr Vorwissen mit Antizipationsfragen auf Handout G. Beim ersten Hören: globales Verstehen (Was ist der Unterschied zwischen Jonas' und Lenas Weg?). Beim zweiten Hören: Detailverstehen – Lernende beantworten 5 Fragen in Stichworten. Anschließend kurzer Austausch mit dem Partner: 'Welcher Weg gefällt dir mehr und warum?'
materials: Audiodatei: Interviews Jonas & Lena (MP3, 4 min gesamt)
Handout G – Antizipationsfragen und Aufgaben zum Hörverstehen

activities.title: Diskussion und Rollenspiel: Bildungsberatung
activities.description: In Gruppen von 3 Personen übernehmen die Lernenden Rollen: Rolle A – Bildungsberater/in, Rolle B – vietnamesischer Schüler/in, der/die in Deutschland studieren möchte, Rolle C – Beobachter/in mit Feedback-Bogen. Rolle B schildert seinen/ihren Hintergrund (auf Rollenkarte) und fragt nach Möglichkeiten. Rolle A berät auf Basis der Kenntnisse aus den Sessions. Rolle C notiert verwendete Vokabular und Strukturen. Nach 5 Minuten Rollentausch. Die Lehrkraft zirkuliert, gibt Impulse und notiert häufige Fehler für späteres Feedback.

activities.title: Exit Ticket und Fehlerfeedback
activities.description: Die Lehrkraft gibt kurzes Feedback zu häufigen Fehlern aus dem Rollenspiel (ohne Namen zu nennen) und korrigiert 3–4 typische Satzfehler gemeinsam im Plenum. Lernende füllen ein Exit Ticket (Post-it oder Handout I) aus: 'Das habe ich heute gelernt: ___', 'Das ist mir noch unklar: ___'. Lernende kleben Post-its an die Tafel. Die Lehrkraft liest sie durch und gibt eine kurze Vorschau auf die Hausaufgaben und Woche 3.
materials: Post-it-Zettel oder Exit Ticket Handout I

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Vergleichsstrukturen: Komparativ und Superlativ in Vergleichssätzen; Konnektoren für Kontrast und Ähnlichkeit (während, obwohl, sowohl...als auch, im Gegensatz zu + Dativ, ähnlich wie); Relativsätze zur Beschreibung von Institutionen (Das Gymnasium ist eine Schule, die zum Abitur führt.)
lesson_plans.cultural_note: Das Bildungssystem im DACH-Raum ist stark föderalistisch geprägt: In Deutschland liegt die Bildungshoheit bei den 16 Bundesländern, was zu erheblichen Unterschieden zwischen z.B. Bayern (traditionell, selektives dreigliedriges System) und Hamburg (Gesamtschulsystem) führt. Österreich hat eine ähnliche Struktur, nennt das Abitur jedoch 'Matura'. Die Schweiz hat ein besonders dezentrales System mit 26 Kantonen, vier Landessprachen und einem stark ausgebauten dualen Berufsbildungssystem, das weltweit als Vorbild gilt – ca. 70% der Schweizer Jugendlichen absolvieren eine Berufslehre. Für vietnamesische Lernende ist besonders interessant, dass das deutsche duale System sehr verschieden vom zentralisierten vietnamesischen Bildungssystem ist, und dass der Universitätsabschluss in DACH nicht automatisch höher angesehen wird als ein Berufsabschluss.

homework.description: Lernende recherchieren online das Bildungssystem eines DACH-Landes ihrer Wahl und schreiben einen strukturierten Vergleich mit dem vietnamesischen Bildungssystem.
exercises: Schriftlicher Vergleich (150–200 Wörter): 'Das Bildungssystem in [Land] und in Vietnam – Gemeinsamkeiten und Unterschiede'. Mindestens 3 Vergleichsstrukturen aus Handout E verwenden.
Vokabellernkarten: 10 neue Vokabeln aus der Woche auf Karteikarten schreiben (Deutsch – Vietnamesisch – Beispielsatz) und für Spaced-Repetition-Review vorbereiten.
Höraufgabe: DaF-Podcast 'Auf Deutsch' – Episode zum Thema 'Studium in Deutschland' (20 Min.) hören und 3 neue Informationen auf Handout J notieren.
Optional – Erweiterungsaufgabe für Fortgeschrittene: Online-Artikel aus der österreichischen Zeitung 'Der Standard' zum Bildungsthema lesen und eine kurze Stellungnahme (100 Wörter) verfassen.

formative: Beobachtung der Lernenden während des Jigsaw-Lesens: Können sie die Kerninformationen ihrem Partner verständlich weitergeben?
Überprüfung der Vergleichstabelle (Handout D) auf Vollständigkeit und korrekte Verwendung von Fachvokabular
Mündliches Monitoring während des Rollenspiels: Verwendung von Zielstrukturen (Komparativ, Vergleichskonnektoren), Aussprache, Kommunikationsstrategien
Auswertung der Exit Tickets zur Identifikation von Lücken im Verständnis für die nächste Stunde
Kurze Vokabelabfrage zu Beginn der nächsten Woche (5 Minuten, 8 Begriffe zum Schulsystem)
assessment.summative: Ende der Woche 2: Kleines Portfolio-Element – Lernende reichen ihren schriftlichen Vergleich (Hausaufgabe) ein. Bewertungskriterien: inhaltliche Genauigkeit (30%), Verwendung von Zielstrukturen und Komparation (30%), Vokabular aus der Woche (20%), Textorganisation und Kohäsion (20%). Feedback wird schriftlich auf einem Bewertungsraster gegeben und in der nächsten Stunde besprochen.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Zweisprachige Glossar-Karten (Deutsch-Vietnamesisch) für alle Fachbegriffe bereitstellen. Vereinfachte Version der Lesetexte (A2+) als Alternative zu den B1-Texten anbieten. Satzanfänge für das Rollenspiel und den schriftlichen Vergleich auf Hilfskarten vorgeben (z.B. 'In Deutschland gibt es... / In Vietnam hingegen...'). Vorab-Aktivierung des Schemas durch Bilder aus vietnamesischen und deutschen Schulen. Lernende mit Verständnisschwierigkeiten können die Infografik-Beschriftungen auf Vietnamesisch ergänzen. In Gruppenarbeiten werden stärkere Lernende als informelle Mentoren eingeteilt.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Zusatzaufgabe: Kurze Präsentation (2–3 Minuten) über ein spezifisches Merkmal des DACH-Bildungssystems, das sie besonders interessant finden. Authentische Lektüre: Artikel aus dem PISA-Bericht über DACH-Länder lesen und die wichtigsten Schlussfolgerungen zusammenfassen. Schreiben eines Blogbeitrags (250 Wörter) aus der Perspektive eines vietnamesischen Studierenden, der in Deutschland studiert. Recherche und Präsentation: 'Warum gilt das Schweizer Berufsbildungssystem weltweit als Modell?' Fortgeschrittene können auch als Peer-Coaches im Rollenspiel fungieren und Feedback auf dem Beobachtungsbogen geben.

review_from_previous: Woche 1: Geografie und Landeskunde DACH – Nennen der Hauptstädte, Bundesländer und Sprachregionen (kurze 3-Minuten-Aktivierung zu Beginn von Session 1)
Woche 1: Alltagsvokabular und sich vorstellen – Aktivierung durch die Warm-Up-Aktivität 'Meine Schulzeit'
A2-Grammatik: Perfekt und Präteritum – Nutzung beim Erzählen von eigenen Schulerfahrungen
Woche 1: Kulturelle Unterschiede DACH – Verknüpfung mit föderalistischem Bildungssystem
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Woche 3 wird das Thema 'Arbeit und Beruf im DACH-Raum' behandeln. Das duale Ausbildungssystem aus Woche 2 dient als direkte Brücke: Wie führen die verschiedenen Bildungswege in den Arbeitsmarkt? Lernende werden ermutigt, beim Podcast-Hören (Hausaufgabe) auf Berufsbezüge zu achten. Die Vokabeln 'der Beruf', 'die Stelle', 'die Bewerbung' werden als Vorschau kurz eingeführt.

learning_objectives: Can describe their ideal apartment or house in a German-speaking city using relevant vocabulary for rooms, furniture, and location features.
Can understand and write a rental advertisement (Wohnungsanzeige) including key details such as size, rent, and amenities.
Can discuss advantages and disadvantages of urban living in Germany, Austria, or Switzerland using comparative structures and opinion phrases.
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic room and furniture vocabulary (A2 level: Zimmer, Küche, Bad, Sofa, Tisch)
Prepositions of place with accusative and dative (in, auf, neben, zwischen, vor, hinter)
Modal verbs: können, möchten, müssen, dürfen
Simple present and conversational past (Perfekt) tenses
Numbers and prices in German (for rent and apartment size)
Basic adjective endings in nominative and accusative cases

sessions.title: Meine Traumwohnung – Describing Urban Apartments

activities.title: Stadtbilder – Was siehst du?
activities.description: Teacher displays 4–5 images of typical apartments and residential buildings from Berlin, Vienna, and Zurich on the projector. Students work in pairs and spend 3 minutes discussing in German: 'Was siehst du? Wie findest du diese Wohnung/dieses Haus?' Teacher elicits 2–3 responses from the class, writing key vocabulary on the board (e.g., Altbau, Neubau, Hochhaus, Balkon, Innenhof). Special attention is given to cultural contrasts with Vietnamese housing styles to activate schemata.
materials: Projector or printed image cards of DACH city apartments

activities.title: Wohnungsvokabular – Neue Wörter im Kontext
activities.description: Teacher introduces 15 target vocabulary items using a visual vocabulary sheet (Wortschatzblatt) combining images and example sentences. Words are grouped thematically: (1) Building types – Altbau, Neubau, Einfamilienhaus, Hochhaus, Reihenhaus; (2) Apartment features – Balkon, Terrasse, Keller, Dachgeschoss, Erdgeschoss, Aufzug; (3) Location and neighbourhood – Stadtviertel, Innenstadt, Vorort, Nähe, fußläufig erreichbar. Teacher models pronunciation; students repeat chorally and individually. Vietnamese learners are given a bilingual gloss sheet (German–Vietnamese) for self-reference to avoid over-reliance on L1 translation during production tasks. Students then match 10 words to images on the handout individually (2 minutes), then check in pairs.

activities.title: Podcast-Ausschnitt: 'Wohnen in Berlin'
activities.description: Students listen to a 2-minute authentic-style audio clip (teacher-recorded or sourced from DW Deutsch) in which a young woman named Lena describes her apartment in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg. First listening: students identify the overall topic and 2 key facts (global comprehension). Second listening: students complete a gap-fill activity on the handout with 6 missing words from the target vocabulary. After checking answers with a partner, teacher confirms correct answers and clarifies any comprehension issues. Note for Vietnamese learners: pre-teach the compound noun Zweiraumwohnung and explain German apartment sizing convention (Zimmeranzahl) versus square metres, contrasting with Vietnamese practice.

activities.title: Meine Traumwohnung beschreiben
activities.description: Students individually spend 2 minutes noting 4–5 features of their ideal city apartment using the new vocabulary and a sentence frame card provided: 'Meine Traumwohnung liegt in … Sie hat … Zimmer und … Die Miete beträgt ungefähr … Mir ist wichtig, dass …'. Students then describe their dream apartment to their partner (1.5 minutes each). Partner asks at least one follow-up question using: 'Warum ist dir das wichtig?' or 'Hast du eine Präferenz für Altbau oder Neubau?' Teacher circulates, notes errors for delayed correction, and nominates 2 pairs to share with the class.

sessions.title: Wohnungsanzeigen lesen und schreiben

activities.title: Anzeigen lesen – Was wird angeboten?
activities.description: Students receive a handout with three authentic-style rental advertisements (Wohnungsanzeigen) modelled on Immobilienscout24 listings for Munich, Vienna, and Bern. Each ad contains abbreviations commonly used in German housing ads (e.g., 2 ZKB = 2 Zimmer, Küche, Bad; WG = Wohngemeinschaft; NK = Nebenkosten; KM = Kaltmiete; TG = Tiefgarage). Before reading, teacher briefly explains the abbreviation system using a reference list. Students read all three ads and complete a comparison table (Vergleichstabelle) with columns: Stadt, Zimmeranzahl, Größe (m²), Kaltmiete, Besonderheiten. Individual work for 5 minutes, then comparison and discussion with partner. Teacher elicits answers and discusses cultural note on WG culture in Germany, which is very common among students and young professionals, and may contrast with Vietnamese family-oriented housing norms.
materials: Reading handout with three rental advertisements

activities.title: Relativsätze zur Beschreibung – 'Die Wohnung, die …'
activities.description: Teacher introduces relative clauses (Relativsätze) as the grammar focus of this week, showing their practical use in housing descriptions. Using examples taken directly from the rental ads, teacher presents the structure on the board: 'Das ist eine Wohnung, die einen Balkon hat.' / 'Ich suche ein Zimmer, das in der Nähe der U-Bahn liegt.' / 'Das ist ein Haus, dessen Garten sehr groß ist.' Focus is on nominative and accusative relative pronouns (der, die, das / den, die, das) using a colour-coded grammar table. Vietnamese learners are explicitly told that relative clauses in German require verb-final word order, which differs from Vietnamese relative structures. Teacher models 3 examples, then students complete 6 controlled gap-fill sentences on the handout, transforming two simple sentences into one sentence with a relative clause. Pairs check answers together.
materials: Grammar explanation handout with colour-coded table

activities.title: Eigene Wohnungsanzeige schreiben
activities.description: Students write their own rental advertisement (Wohnungsanzeige) for an imaginary apartment they wish to rent out. They must include: (1) at least one relative clause; (2) a minimum of 8 target vocabulary items; (3) standard ad abbreviations where appropriate; (4) price, size, location, and at least two special features. Teacher provides a writing scaffold (Schreibgerüst) with required elements and a model text for reference. Writing time: 10 minutes. Students then exchange their ad with a different partner (not their usual pair) who checks for: correct relative clause structure, vocabulary accuracy, and overall comprehensibility. Peer feedback is given using a simple 3-point checklist on the handout. Teacher collects all ads for formative assessment.

activities.title: Reflexion und Fehlerkorrektur
activities.description: Teacher presents 5 anonymised sentences on the projector taken from student writing during the lesson (errors collected during circulation). Class collaboratively corrects each sentence, focusing on relative clause word order and vocabulary use. Teacher then leads a 2-minute exit ticket: each student writes one sentence on a sticky note or scrap paper: 'Heute habe ich gelernt, dass …' and one question they still have. Teacher collects these to inform the next session. Teacher previews homework and briefly mentions next week's topic (neighbourhood services and asking for directions) to create anticipation.
materials: Sticky notes or scrap paper for exit ticket

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Relativsätze im Nominativ und Akkusativ (Relative clauses in nominative and accusative): formation with relative pronouns der, die, das / den, die, das; verb-final word order in the relative clause; contrast with Vietnamese sentence structure to address learner-specific challenges.
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, renting (Mieten) is far more common than home ownership compared to Vietnam and many other countries – approximately 50–60% of Germans rent their homes. Wohngemeinschaften (WGs) are a widespread and socially accepted housing form, especially in university cities like Berlin, Munich, and Vienna. German rental advertisements follow strict conventions with specific abbreviations (ZKB, NK, KM, WG) that renters must understand. Apartment size is always measured in Zimmeranzahl (number of rooms, not counting kitchen and bathroom) plus square metres. Nebenkosten (utility costs) are billed separately from Kaltmiete (base rent), a system that Vietnamese learners often find surprising. In Swiss cities such as Zurich and Geneva, rental prices are among the highest in the world. The Mieterschutzbund (tenant protection association) is a powerful institution in German-speaking countries, reflecting strong renter rights.

homework.description: Students complete two tasks at home to reinforce vocabulary, grammar, and reading skills from this week's sessions.
exercises: Task 1 – Reading and Vocabulary (15 min): Read the two additional rental advertisements on Handout HW-3A and answer 5 comprehension questions in full German sentences. Underline all relative clauses you find and check that verb-final word order is used.

Task 2 – Writing (15 min): Write a short description (80–100 words) of your current home or an ideal home you would like to have in a German city. Use at least 6 words from the vocabulary target list and include at least 2 relative clauses. Use the sentence frame card from the lesson as support. Bring the written text to the next lesson for peer review.

formative: Observation during pair-speaking activity (Session 1, Activity 4): teacher uses a simple checklist to note correct use of target vocabulary and fluency.
Gap-fill listening comprehension check (Session 1, Activity 3): quick whole-class answer verification reveals comprehension gaps.
Comparison table task (Session 2, Activity 1): teacher circulates and checks reading comprehension of rental ad abbreviations.
Relative clause transformation exercise (Session 2, Activity 2): teacher checks pair answers to identify persistent structural errors.
Peer feedback on written advertisement (Session 2, Activity 3): structured peer checklist provides immediate feedback to writers.
Exit ticket (Session 2, Activity 4): collected by teacher to diagnose remaining difficulties and adjust next lesson accordingly.
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (to be administered at the start of Week 4, first 15 minutes): Students receive an unseen rental advertisement and must (1) answer 3 comprehension questions in German, (2) identify and correct 2 relative clause errors in a short text, and (3) write 3 sentences describing a fictional apartment using target vocabulary. Scoring rubric: vocabulary accuracy (10 pts), relative clause structure (10 pts), reading comprehension (10 pts). Pass mark: 21/30.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a full bilingual German–Vietnamese vocabulary list with example sentences for all 20 target words. During speaking activities, allow use of the sentence frame card at all times without time pressure. For the relative clause exercise, offer a partially completed model sentence before each item. Reduce the writing task to 60 words and allow 3 vocabulary items from L1 to be substituted if unknown German equivalents cannot be recalled. Pair struggling learners with supportive peers rather than other struggling learners during peer correction. Offer an optional 10-minute pre-session vocabulary preview audio (teacher-recorded) to be listened to before class.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to use genitive relative clauses (dessen / deren) in their written advertisement. Ask them to write a comparison of urban versus rural living in Germany using comparative and superlative adjectives (which previews a B1+ grammar point). During the reading activity, provide an authentic unmodified Immobilienscout24 advertisement with full legal and administrative language and ask them to identify and research 3 unfamiliar terms. Encourage them to role-play a phone conversation with a landlord enquiring about an apartment, using polite register (Konjunktiv II: 'Ich würde gerne …', 'Wäre es möglich, …?').

review_from_previous: Week 1 topic: Prepositions of place with dative and accusative – reactivated through describing furniture placement in apartment images
Week 2 topic: Modal verbs (können, müssen, dürfen, möchten) – recycled in discussion of apartment rules (Hausordnung) and tenant rights
A2 carry-over: Adjective endings in nominative and accusative – reviewed implicitly through relative clause formation (e.g., 'ein schöner Balkon, der …')
Numbers and prices – reviewed in context of reading rental advertisements and comparing Kaltmiete across cities
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 4 will build directly on 'Wohnen in der Stadt' by zooming out to the neighbourhood (das Viertel / die Nachbarschaft). Learners will need this week's location vocabulary (Innenstadt, Vorort, fußläufig erreichbar) to describe neighbourhood amenities and give directions. The grammar of relative clauses will be extended to dative case (dem / der) in the context of describing places: 'Das ist der Park, in dem ich jeden Morgen laufe.' The topic of Week 4 will be 'Mein Viertel – Einkaufen, Verkehr und Freizeit.'

learning_objectives: Can describe and compare different media sources (TV, radio, online news, newspapers) using appropriate B1 vocabulary and expressing personal preferences with justification.
Can summarize the main points of a short news article or radio broadcast and retell key information to a partner using reported speech and connectors.
Can express and justify opinions about media reliability and the influence of social media on society, using modal verbs and opinion phrases at B1 level.
prerequisite_knowledge: A2–B1 present tense and simple past tense verb conjugations
Basic Nebensatz structures with 'dass', 'weil', and 'obwohl'
Vocabulary for daily routines and free-time activities (A2 level)
Familiarity with Konjunktiv II for polite requests (modal verbs: können, müssen, dürfen)
Basic adjective declension in nominative and accusative cases
Ability to use connectors: und, aber, oder, denn, deshalb at A2 level

sessions.title: Medienlandschaft – Welche Medien nutzen wir?

activities.title: Medien-Mindmap & Diskussion
activities.description: Teacher draws a central bubble on the board with the word 'Medien'. Learners call out media types they know in German or Vietnamese (teacher provides German equivalents). Learners then work in pairs to answer: 'Welche Medien nutzt du täglich? Warum?' Each pair shares one answer. Teacher collects key vocabulary on the board. This activates prior knowledge and creates a Vietnamese–German bridge for learners unfamiliar with media vocabulary in German.

activities.title: Wortschatz: Medien & Nachrichten – Einführung
activities.description: Teacher presents 15 target vocabulary items using a structured PPT slide with images of Vietnamese and German media outlets (e.g., VnExpress vs. Der Spiegel; VTV vs. ARD). Each word is shown with: (1) a visual, (2) a German example sentence at B1 level, (3) a Vietnamese translation gloss for accessibility. Learners copy words into their vocabulary journal using the 'Wort – Beispielsatz – Übersetzung' format. Special attention is given to compound nouns (e.g., die Nachrichtensendung, der Zeitungsartikel) which are structurally unfamiliar to Vietnamese learners.

activities.title: Medientypen zuordnen – Kategorisierungsaufgabe
activities.description: Learners receive a handout with 12 sentences describing media habits (e.g., 'Ich schaue jeden Abend die Tagesschau.' / 'Sie liest jeden Morgen die Zeitung auf dem Handy.'). They must assign each sentence to a media category: Fernsehen, Radio, Zeitung, Online-Medien, Social Media. Then they underline the key noun or verb that helped them decide. This trains contextual vocabulary recognition. After individual work (4 min), pairs compare answers and discuss disagreements. Teacher reviews with the class.
materials: Answer key (projected on board at end)

activities.title: Kurzinterview: 'Wie informierst du dich?'
activities.description: Teacher plays a 2-minute authentic-style audio recording (teacher-created or from DW Deutsch) of two German speakers (one young adult, one older adult) describing their media habits. Learners complete a structured listening grid: Who? What media? How often? Why? First listening: global understanding (what is the general topic?). Second listening: detail extraction for the grid. Vietnamese learners are supported with a pre-listening glossary of 5 key words on the board. Teacher pauses after each speaker for processing time, which accommodates the slower auditory processing typical in foreign language listening for Vietnamese learners.
materials: Audio file: Interview 'Wie informierst du dich?' (2 min, MP3)

sessions.title: Nachrichten verstehen & Meinungen ausdrücken

activities.title: Zeitungsartikel lesen: 'Fake News in sozialen Medien'
activities.description: Learners receive an adapted B1-level newspaper article (approx. 180 words) about the spread of fake news on social media in Germany. The article uses Präteritum and dass-Sätze which were previewed in previous weeks. Task sequence: (1) Read for global understanding – choose the best headline from three options. (2) Read for detail – answer 4 true/false/not stated questions. (3) Vocabulary in context – match 4 underlined words to their definitions. The text is adapted from a real Spiegel Online article to maintain authenticity while adjusting complexity for B1. Vietnamese learners are reminded to focus on word roots and compound noun analysis strategies taught in Week 3.
materials: Handout: Adapted article 'Fake News in sozialen Medien'
activities.interaction_pattern: individual then pairs for answer check

activities.title: Indirekte Rede & Meinungsausdrücke – Entdeckungsaufgabe
activities.description: Teacher draws learners' attention back to two sentences from the article that use reported speech and opinion phrases: 'Er sagte, dass viele Menschen den Nachrichten nicht mehr vertrauen.' and 'Meiner Meinung nach sind soziale Medien gefährlich.' Teacher elicits the grammar rule through guided questions: 'Was ist das Subjekt? Wo steht das Verb? Was bedeutet 'meiner Meinung nach'?' Learners then receive a mini grammar card with: (1) Indirekte Rede structure with 'dass' + verb-final, (2) 5 opinion phrases (Meiner Meinung nach…, Ich glaube, dass…, Ich finde es wichtig, dass…, Es scheint mir, dass…, Ich bin der Meinung, dass…). Learners practice by transforming 4 direct statements into reported speech in writing. The inductive discovery approach is especially effective for Vietnamese learners who respond well to pattern recognition.
materials: Mini grammar card: Indirekte Rede & Meinungsausdrücke

activities.title: Diskussion: 'Vertrauen wir den Medien?'
activities.description: Learners work in groups of 3. Each group receives a set of 6 statement cards with provocative media-related claims (e.g., 'Soziale Medien verbreiten mehr Lügen als Zeitungen.' / 'Das Fernsehen ist für ältere Menschen wichtiger als für junge Menschen.'). Each learner must respond to at least 2 cards using the opinion phrases from the grammar card. Learner A reads a card, Learner B gives an opinion using one of the 5 phrases, Learner C agrees or disagrees and adds a reason with 'weil' or 'aber'. Roles rotate. Teacher circulates and notes language errors for delayed feedback. This structured output task provides the scaffolding Vietnamese learners need to move from controlled to freer production, addressing typical reluctance to speak without a clear model.
materials: Statement cards set (6 cards per group, laminated)
Teacher observation checklist for formative assessment

activities.title: Reflexion & Feedback-Runde
activities.description: Teacher conducts a brief whole-class feedback session (3 min language focus: teacher shares 2–3 common errors heard during the discussion activity and elicits self-correction from the class without naming individual learners, which is culturally sensitive for Vietnamese learners who may feel embarrassed by public correction). Then learners complete a 'Lernkarte' (exit ticket) with three prompts: (1) Heute habe ich gelernt: ___. (2) Das war schwierig für mich: ___. (3) Ich möchte mehr üben: ___. Teacher collects cards to inform next session's adjustments.

vocabulary_target: sich informieren (to inform oneself / keep up with news)
lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Indirekte Rede mit 'dass'-Sätzen (reported speech with subordinate clauses) and opinion expressions (Meinungsausdrücke) at B1 level: 'Ich glaube, dass…', 'Meiner Meinung nach…', 'Ich bin der Meinung, dass…'. Focus on verb-final word order in dass-Sätze, which contrasts with Vietnamese SVO word order and requires explicit attention for Vietnamese learners.
lesson_plans.cultural_note: In the DACH countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland), public broadcasting plays a culturally significant role. ARD and ZDF (Germany), ORF (Austria), and SRF (Switzerland) are publicly funded and considered highly credible news sources. The 'Tagesschau' (ARD, 8pm) is one of the most-watched news programmes in Germany with over 10 million viewers nightly and is seen as a national institution. Germans tend to be critical consumers of media and the concept of 'Pressefreiheit' (freedom of the press) is highly valued. In recent years, the term 'Lügenpresse' (lying press) emerged as a controversial term used by populist movements, reflecting wider debates about media trust. Vietnamese learners may find it interesting to compare this with media consumption culture in Vietnam, where state television (VTV) plays a similarly central role but within a different political context. Discussing media trust differences can generate meaningful intercultural dialogue.

homework.description: Learners complete a structured home learning task connecting media vocabulary, grammar, and personal reflection. They should write a short text and complete online exercises to consolidate session content before Week 5, Session continuation or Week 6.
exercises: Schreiben (Writing – 80–100 words): Write a short paragraph describing your personal media habits. Use at least 5 target vocabulary words from the week's list and include 2 opinion sentences using 'Ich glaube, dass…' or 'Meiner Meinung nach…'. Title: 'Wie ich mich über Nachrichten informiere'.

Grammatik (Grammar – online platform): Complete the 10-sentence exercise on Quizlet or the course LMS converting direct speech to indirect speech using dass-Sätze. Example: 'Sie sagte: Ich lese jeden Tag die Zeitung.' → 'Sie sagte, dass sie jeden Tag die Zeitung liest.'

Lesen (Reading – optional extension): Read one short news summary on DW Deutsch (www.dw.com/de – 'Langsam gesprochene Nachrichten' section, B1 level) and note 3 new words with their meaning in your vocabulary journal.
Hören (Listening – optional extension): Listen to one episode of 'Deutsch – warum nicht?' (DW podcast, Series 3, B1 level) and note any media-related vocabulary you recognize.

formative: Observation during pair and group discussions: Teacher uses a checklist to note use of target vocabulary, correct dass-Satz structure, and opinion phrases during the 'Vertrauen wir den Medien?' activity.
Exit ticket (Lernkarte) analysis: Teacher reviews learner self-reported difficulties and learning highlights to adjust Week 6 instruction.
Listening grid completion check: Teacher reviews completed Hörverständnis-Raster grids during or after Session 1 to identify comprehension gaps.
Transformation exercise check: Teacher reviews the 4 indirekte Rede transformation sentences written individually during the grammar focus activity.
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (administered at the start of Week 6, approx. 20 minutes): A short written task where learners read a 100-word adapted news text about a current media topic, answer 3 comprehension questions, and write a 60-word response expressing their opinion about the topic using at least 3 target vocabulary items and 2 opinion phrases with dass-Sätze. Assessed using a simple B1-aligned rubric covering: task completion, vocabulary range and accuracy, grammatical correctness of Nebensätze, and coherence.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a sentence frame handout for the speaking discussion activity with partially completed opinion sentences (e.g., 'Ich glaube, dass soziale Medien ___ sind, weil ___.'). Reduce the number of vocabulary items to focus on the 10 highest-frequency words. During listening tasks, allow a third listening if needed and provide a Vietnamese gloss for the 5 most difficult words. For the grammar activity, provide a completed model example before the transformation practice. Pair struggling learners with mid-level peers (not the strongest) for supportive peer scaffolding. Offer the option to write homework in simpler sentences before attempting complex structures.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to use Konjunktiv II in their opinion expressions (e.g., 'Es könnte sein, dass…', 'Man sollte bedenken, dass…'). During the discussion activity, ask them to take notes on their group's opinions and write a 3-sentence summary in reported speech. Provide an optional extension article from Der Spiegel Online or Zeit Online (authentic, unadapted) and ask them to identify 5 new vocabulary items and write one paragraph summarizing the article using their own words. For homework, ask advanced learners to find one Vietnamese news article, identify its equivalent German news topic, and write a comparison sentence.

review_from_previous: Week 1–2: Basic present tense and Nebensatz structures with 'weil' and 'dass' – recycled in the grammar focus activity on indirekte Rede
Week 3: Compound noun analysis strategy (e.g., Zeitungs+artikel, Nachrichten+sendung) – explicitly referenced during vocabulary presentation
Week 4: Adjective vocabulary for describing places/things (e.g., aktuell, wichtig, interessant) – reactivated in discussion card responses
Week 2–3: Connectors (deshalb, aber, weil, obwohl) – encouraged and scaffolded during the speaking discussion task
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 6 will build on media language by introducing the topic of 'Reisen & Tourismus', where learners will use similar opinion expression structures and Nebensätze to describe and recommend travel destinations. The skill of summarizing information from a text (practiced in Week 5 with news articles) will be transferred to summarizing travel reviews and blog posts. Vocabulary for describing experiences and making comparisons (Komparativ and Superlativ) will bridge the grammar focus from Week 5 into Week 6.

learning_objectives: Can understand and use key vocabulary related to politics and society (e.g., die Demokratie, die Wahl, das Grundgesetz) in context
Can express and justify simple opinions about political and social issues using modal verbs and connectors such as 'weil', 'deshalb', 'obwohl'
Can read and extract main ideas from short authentic texts such as newspaper headlines or simplified political statements about German/DACH society
prerequisite_knowledge: Solid grasp of A2–B1 grammar: modal verbs (müssen, können, dürfen, sollen), subordinate clauses with 'weil' and 'dass'
Ability to express simple opinions using 'Ich denke, dass...', 'Meiner Meinung nach...'
Basic vocabulary for social topics: Familie, Arbeit, Schule, Umwelt from previous weeks
Reading comprehension of moderately complex texts (approx. 150–200 words) at A2–B1 level
Familiarity with German sentence structure including verb-second rule and subordinate clause word order

sessions.title: Einstieg in die Politik: Wortschatz und erste Meinungen

activities.title: Bildimpuls: Was ist Politik?
activities.description: Teacher projects 6 images related to German/DACH political and social life (e.g., Bundestag building, election poster, protest march, recycling bins, a courtroom, a school). In pairs, learners discuss in Vietnamese and then switch to German: 'Was siehst du? Was hat das mit Politik oder Gesellschaft zu tun?' Teacher elicits 3–5 German words learners already know. Write responses on the board as a mind map. This activates prior knowledge and creates curiosity about the topic.

activities.title: Schlüsselwörter: Politik & Gesellschaft
activities.description: Teacher introduces 16 target vocabulary items using a structured handout with word, article, plural, example sentence, and a Vietnamese gloss for difficult items. Words are grouped into three semantic clusters: (1) Politische Institutionen (der Bundestag, die Regierung, das Grundgesetz, der Bürgermeister, die Partei), (2) Politische Prozesse (die Wahl, abstimmen, das Gesetz, die Demokratie, die Opposition), (3) Gesellschaftliche Themen (die Gleichberechtigung, die Integration, die Umweltpolitik, der Protest, die Meinungsfreiheit, die Steuern). Teacher models pronunciation. Learners repeat chorally, then individually. Brief attention given to noun genders — teacher highlights a memory tip: many abstract nouns ending in -ung, -heit, -keit are feminine.
materials: Audio pronunciation model (teacher or audio file)

activities.title: Wortschatz-Bingo und Matching-Spiel
activities.description: Phase 1 (5 min): Learners receive a bingo card with 9 of the 16 target words. Teacher reads definitions in German (e.g., 'Das ist das wichtigste Gesetz in Deutschland'). Learners mark the word. First to complete a row calls 'Bingo!' and reads back the words with their articles. Phase 2 (5 min): In pairs, learners complete a matching exercise on the handout — matching German words to Vietnamese translations and to short example sentences. Pairs check answers with another pair (group of 4).

activities.title: Meinungen äußern: Konjunktionen und Redemittel
activities.description: Teacher presents a short dialogue on the board between two fictional German students discussing voting age (Sollte das Wahlalter auf 16 Jahre gesenkt werden?). The dialogue is annotated to highlight: (1) Opinion phrases: 'Ich bin der Meinung, dass...', 'Ich finde, dass...', 'Meiner Ansicht nach...', (2) Concession with 'obwohl' (obwohl-clause sends verb to end), (3) Cause with 'weil' and 'deshalb'. Teacher draws a contrast table on the board showing subordinating conjunctions (weil, obwohl, dass → verb at end) vs. coordinating adverb (deshalb → verb second position). Vietnamese learners often struggle with verb-final order — teacher explicitly contrasts with Vietnamese SOV tendency and German standard V2. Two example transformations are worked through together as a class.

activities.title: Sätze bauen: Meinungen zur Politik
activities.description: Learners individually complete 5 sentence-completion exercises on the handout, inserting the correct conjunction and completing the clause. Example: 'Ich wähle die Grünen, ________ mir Umweltpolitik wichtig ist.' (weil) and 'Die Regierung hat neue Gesetze gemacht; ________ sind viele Bürger unzufrieden.' (deshalb). Learners then compare with a partner. Teacher conducts whole-class feedback, asking individual learners to read answers aloud and corrects word order errors explicitly.

sessions.title: Lesen, Diskutieren und Sprechen: Gesellschaftliche Themen

activities.title: Zeitungsartikel: Ein Thema, zwei Meinungen
activities.description: Learners receive a simplified, authentic-style dual-opinion article (approx. 180 words total, adapted from real German press at B1 level) on a relevant social issue — 'Soll das Wahlalter in Deutschland auf 16 Jahre gesenkt werden?' The article contains one 'Pro' paragraph (90 words) and one 'Contra' paragraph (90 words). Task sequence: (1) Pre-reading (2 min): Learners predict content from the headline alone — teacher asks 'Was denkt ihr? Ja oder Nein?' as a quick show of hands. (2) First reading (4 min): Learners read silently and underline words they don't know. Teacher circulates. (3) Comprehension tasks (5 min): True/False/Not mentioned exercise (6 statements) + one open question: 'Welches Argument findest du am stärksten? Warum?'. Learners work individually then compare with partner. Whole-class feedback focuses on text evidence.

activities.title: Meinungskarten vorbereiten
activities.description: Each learner receives one 'Meinungskarte' — a small card with a political/social statement they must agree or disagree with and justify. Statements are differentiated: simpler cards use high-frequency vocabulary (e.g., 'Schüler sollen Schuluniformen tragen.'), more complex cards address political themes (e.g., 'Die Regierung soll mehr Geld für Integration ausgeben.'). Learners have 4 minutes to write 3–4 bullet points supporting their position using the target grammar and vocabulary from Session 1. Teacher circulates, offering scaffolding phrases on the board: 'Ich bin dafür/dagegen, weil...', 'Obwohl ... , denke ich, dass...', 'Ein wichtiges Argument ist, dass...'
materials: Meinungskarten (differentiated set A and set B)

activities.title: Fishbowl-Diskussion: Pro und Contra
activities.description: Two rounds of structured discussion using a modified fishbowl format adapted for a language class. Round 1 (8 min): 4 learners sit in the inner circle; 2 argue 'Pro', 2 argue 'Contra' on their Meinungskarte topic. Remaining learners observe and tick a 'Beobachtungsbogen' (observation sheet) noting: (a) Was a target vocabulary word used? (b) Was 'weil' or 'obwohl' used correctly? (c) Did the speaker give a reason? This promotes active listening and peer assessment. Round 2 (6 min): New group of 4 takes the inner circle with new statements. Teacher moderates, noting language errors for later feedback. After both rounds, teacher gives brief feedback on common errors noticed (3–4 points), focusing on word order after 'weil/obwohl' and article use with key nouns. Positive examples from learners are highlighted.

activities.title: Exit Ticket: Drei Sätze zur Politik
activities.description: In the final 5 minutes, each learner independently writes exactly 3 sentences on a slip of paper: (1) One sentence stating a political opinion using 'Ich bin der Meinung, dass...', (2) One sentence using 'weil' or 'deshalb' to give a reason, (3) One sentence using a new vocabulary word from today's lesson in context. Learners hand the slip to the teacher as they leave. Teacher reviews slips between sessions (or uses them as formative assessment data). This technique is familiar from pedagogical research and gives teacher immediate insight into learning gaps. Alternatively, if digital tools are available, learners submit via a shared Google Form.
materials: Exit ticket slips (pre-cut paper) or Google Form link on board

activities.title: Lernziele-Reflexion
activities.description: Teacher briefly revisits the three learning objectives displayed on the board (or slide) from the start of the week. Learners use a simple traffic-light self-assessment (green = confident, yellow = partly confident, red = need more practice) to rate themselves against each objective on a small card they keep in their course folder. Teacher collects data verbally with a show of hands for each objective. This informs next week's review activities and helps the teacher plan differentiated support.

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Expressing opinions with subordinating conjunctions 'weil' and 'obwohl' (verb-final word order) versus coordinating adverb 'deshalb' (verb-second word order); opinion phrases at B1 level: 'Ich bin der Meinung, dass...', 'Meiner Ansicht nach...', 'Ich finde es wichtig, dass...'
lesson_plans.cultural_note: The German Basic Law (Grundgesetz), established in 1949 after World War II, is central to German political identity and daily civic life. Key values enshrined in it — Meinungsfreiheit (freedom of speech), Gleichberechtigung (gender equality, Article 3), and Demokratie — are frequently referenced in public discourse. In Austria and Switzerland, the political systems differ: Austria has the Nationalrat, and Switzerland is famous for its direct democracy (Volksabstimmung / Volksinitiative), where citizens vote directly on specific laws and constitutional changes. This contrasts sharply with Vietnam's one-party system and may be a point of genuine cultural interest and discussion for Vietnamese learners — teachers should approach this comparison with sensitivity and openness rather than judgment. The minimum voting age in Germany is 18 for federal elections, though some federal states allow 16-year-olds to vote in state (Landtag) and local elections, making this a topical and age-relevant debate.

homework.description: Learners complete a structured writing task and a vocabulary review exercise to consolidate the week's learning and prepare for next week's topic on Media and Communication.
exercises: Writing task (150 words): Write a short opinion text ('Meinungstext') on one of two provided social issues: (a) 'Soll das Mindestalter für das Wahlrecht in Deutschland auf 16 Jahre gesenkt werden?' or (b) 'Soll der öffentliche Nahverkehr in deutschen Städten kostenlos sein?' Use at least 3 target vocabulary words from this week, at least one 'weil'-clause, and at least one 'obwohl'-clause. A structured template is provided on the back of the handout for struggling learners.

Vocabulary revision: Complete the Quizlet set for Week 7 vocabulary (link/QR code provided on handout) — do at least 2 rounds of 'Learn' mode and one round of 'Test' mode. Screenshot your test result and bring it or send it to the teacher.

Reading extension (optional, for advanced learners): Read the short adapted Deutsche Welle article on the handout ('Wie funktioniert die Demokratie in Deutschland?', approx. 220 words) and answer 4 comprehension questions in full German sentences.

formative: Vocabulary Bingo (Session 1): Teacher observes engagement and listens for correct article use when learners read back words
Grammar controlled practice (Session 1): Written sentence-completion exercise reviewed in class — teacher notes recurring word-order errors for targeted feedback
Fishbowl discussion observation (Session 2): Teacher uses a simple checklist to note use of target vocabulary, correct subordinate clause word order, and discourse management strategies
Peer observation (Beobachtungsbogen) during Fishbowl: Learners note vocabulary and grammar usage of peers, developing metalinguistic awareness
Exit ticket (Session 2): Three-sentence written production checked for grammar accuracy and vocabulary use — gives teacher immediate formative data on individual learner progress
assessment.summative: End-of-week mini-assessment (to be administered at the start of Week 8, first 15 minutes): A combined 20-item quiz comprising (1) 8 vocabulary matching items (German word → Vietnamese meaning), (2) 6 grammar transformation sentences (rewrite using 'weil', 'obwohl', or 'deshalb' as indicated), and (3) 6 True/False comprehension items based on a new, unseen short text (approx. 100 words) on a DACH political topic. Scored out of 20; 14/20 indicates satisfactory B1-level mastery for this topic.

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a bilingual vocabulary glossary (German–Vietnamese) for all 16 target words to reduce cognitive load during activities. Supply a sentence-starter scaffold card during the Fishbowl discussion and writing tasks listing opinion phrases and connectors. For the reading text, provide a simplified version with shorter sentences and a side glossary. During pair work, strategically pair struggling learners with slightly stronger peers (not the strongest) to encourage supportive interaction. For homework writing, provide a paragraph frame template: 'Ich bin der Meinung, dass ___. Ein Argument dafür ist, dass ___. Obwohl ___, denke ich, dass ___.'
differentiation.advanced_learners: Challenge advanced learners to use additional B1+ structures in discussions and writing: passive voice (Das Gesetz wird vom Bundestag beschlossen.), Konjunktiv II for hypothetical statements (Wenn ich Politiker wäre, würde ich...), and more nuanced opinion language (Es lässt sich argumentieren, dass...). Provide the optional Deutsche Welle reading extension as homework. During Fishbowl, assign advanced learners the role of 'moderator' in Round 2, requiring them to summarise other speakers' points in German. Advanced learners can also research one real German political party (e.g., CDU, SPD, Grüne, FDP) and prepare a 2-minute oral summary for next week's class.

review_from_previous: Week 4 grammar: Modal verbs (müssen, dürfen, können, sollen) — revisited this week in political context: 'Bürger müssen Steuern zahlen.', 'Man darf seine Meinung frei äußern.'
Week 5 topic: Arbeit & Wirtschaft — vocabulary overlap with this week (die Steuern, die Gleichberechtigung am Arbeitsplatz, Mindestlohn) provides semantic bridging
Week 6 grammar: Relative clauses and complex sentence structure — extended this week with subordinating conjunctions 'weil' and 'obwohl' to build longer, more complex sentences appropriate for B1
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 8 topic will be 'Medien & Kommunikation' (Media and Communication). This week's political vocabulary and opinion-expressing structures lay the groundwork: learners will discuss how media shapes political opinion (Wie beeinflussen Medien unsere politischen Ansichten?), introducing new vocabulary around Zeitung, soziale Medien, Fake News, and Berichterstattung. The persuasive writing skills practiced this week will directly transfer to evaluating media texts and writing a short media commentary next week.

learning_objectives: Can describe past travel experiences using Perfekt and Präteritum, including cultural differences encountered abroad
Can express opinions and make comparisons about travel destinations and intercultural situations using comparative structures and modal particles
Can write a coherent travel blog entry (150–200 words) describing a personal intercultural experience with appropriate connectors and descriptive vocabulary
prerequisite_knowledge: Perfekt formation with haben and sein (A2–B1)
Präteritum of modal verbs and sein/haben/werden (A2)
Basic travel vocabulary: Flughafen, Hotel, Koffer, buchen, reisen (A2)
Comparative and superlative adjective forms (A2–B1)
Weil- and dass-clauses with verb-final word order (A2–B1)
Basic opinion expressions: Ich finde, Ich denke, Meiner Meinung nach (A2)

sessions.title: Reiseerfahrungen – Ankunft und Kulturschock

activities.title: Bilderreise – Wohin würdest du reisen?
activities.description: Teacher displays 8 vivid images of iconic travel destinations including Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and Southeast Asia (e.g., Berlin street, Vienna café, Swiss Alps, Hanoi Old Quarter). Learners work in pairs for 3 minutes: each partner picks one destination photo and explains in 2–3 sentences why they would or would not want to visit. Sentence starters are provided on screen: 'Ich würde gern nach … reisen, weil…' / 'Diesen Ort finde ich … weil…'. Pairs then share one interesting answer with the class. Teacher elicits travel vocabulary on the board as a living word cloud.
materials: Slideshow with 8 destination photos (DACH + Vietnam contrast)
Sentence starter prompt card (printed or on screen)

activities.title: Wortfeld Reisen & Kultur – Semantische Felder aufbauen
activities.description: Teacher distributes a vocabulary card set (30 cards) grouped into four semantic fields: 1) Reisevorbereitung (der Reisepass, das Visum, die Unterkunft, der Reiseführer, buchen, packen), 2) Unterwegs (der Anschluss, die Verspätung, umsteigen, der Zoll, die Einreise), 3) Kulturelle Unterschiede (der Kulturschock, die Gepflogenheit, die Sitte, der Brauch, befremdlich, vertraut, sich anpassen), 4) Erfahrungen beschreiben (beeindrucken, überraschen, enttäuschen, faszinieren, sich wohlfühlen, fremd vorkommen). Learners in groups of 3 sort the cards into the four fields, then check against an answer key. Teacher highlights the 10 priority words for the week and drills pronunciation with focus on Vietnamese learner challenges: word-final consonant clusters (Reisepass, Gepflogenheit), compound nouns stress patterns.
materials: Printed vocabulary card sets (one set per group of 3)
Target vocabulary poster for classroom wall

activities.title: Podcast-Ausschnitt: 'Mein erster Kulturschock in Vietnam'
activities.description: Learners listen to an authentic-style audio recording (2 min 30 sec) of a German speaker, Lena, describing her first week in Hanoi: unfamiliar food customs, different concepts of personal space, noise levels, and hospitality surprises. The audio uses natural B1-level speech with occasional pauses. Task 1 (first listen, global): Learners answer 3 true/false/not mentioned questions on a worksheet. Task 2 (second listen, selective): Learners complete a gapped summary paragraph using words from the vocabulary set introduced earlier. Post-listening: Teacher asks 2 comprehension check questions and one opinion question: 'Was findet Lena am schwierigsten? Kannst du das verstehen?' This bridges listening to speaking and activates schema for Vietnamese learners who can relate their own perspective.
materials: Audio file: 'Lenas Kulturschock in Vietnam' (teacher-produced MP3)
Worksheet with T/F/NM questions and gapped summary
Transcript available for post-activity teacher reference

activities.title: Präteritum vs. Perfekt bei Reiseberichten – Kontextanalyse
activities.description: Using 6 sentences extracted from the audio transcript, teacher guides learners through a guided discovery task. Sentences are displayed showing both Perfekt and Präteritum in context. Learners in pairs answer guided questions on a mini-worksheet: 'Welche Zeitform steht in welchem Satz? Wann benutzen wir Perfekt im Gespräch? Wann benutzen wir Präteritum beim Schreiben?' Teacher consolidates with a clear B1 rule summary on the board: Perfekt = spoken narrative, Präteritum = written narrative + sein/haben/modals in both contexts. Special attention to Vietnamese learner challenge: German tense distinction does NOT map to Vietnamese aspect markers; teacher explicitly notes this contrast. Quick choral drill: teacher calls out infinitives, class responds with correct Perfekt form (sein/haben + Partizip II).
materials: Grammar summary card (Perfekt vs. Präteritum, keep for portfolio)

sessions.title: Interkulturelle Begegnungen – Vergleichen, Erzählen, Schreiben

activities.title: Tandem-Erzählung: 'Meine beste / seltsamste Reiseerfahrung'
activities.description: Learners work in pairs (A/B roles). Each learner receives a role card. Person A: tells a 2-minute story about a real or imagined travel experience using at least 5 vocabulary words from Session 1 and at least one Perfekt and one Präteritum sentence. Person B listens and notes down 2 interesting details, then asks 2 follow-up questions from a provided question bank (e.g., 'Wie hast du dich dabei gefühlt?', 'Was war das Seltsamste?', 'Hättest du es anders gemacht?'). Roles then switch. Teacher circulates, taking brief notes on grammar errors for a delayed group feedback slot. After both turns, each pair writes one sentence about their partner's story on a sticky note posted on the 'Reise-Pinnwand' at the front. Teacher conducts a 2-minute gallery walk reading the notes aloud.
materials: Sticky notes and Reise-Pinnwand (poster paper on wall)

activities.title: Reiseblog lesen: 'Drei Wochen in der Schweiz – was mich überraschte'
activities.description: Learners read a 220-word authentic-style travel blog entry written by a Vietnamese exchange student studying in Bern. The text uses B1 vocabulary, Perfekt narrative, comparative structures, and intercultural observations (Swiss punctuality, Abendbrot culture, recycling rules, greetings). Task 1 (skim): Learners read for 90 seconds and identify the 3 main cultural differences mentioned. Task 2 (scan): Learners find and underline all comparative structures (größer als, genauso … wie, anders als) and all Perfekt verbs. Task 3 (critical response): Learners answer one discussion question in writing (2–3 sentences): 'Was hättest du in dieser Situation gefühlt? Kennst du ähnliche Erfahrungen aus Vietnam oder anderen Ländern?' This question is specifically designed to leverage Vietnamese learners' intercultural capital and build cross-cultural reflection skills.
materials: Printed blog text: 'Drei Wochen in der Schweiz'
Task worksheet with skimming, scanning, and reflection prompts

activities.title: Reiseblog schreiben – Geführtes Schreiben mit Scaffolding
activities.description: Learners write their own short travel blog entry (130–160 words) describing a real or imagined intercultural experience. The task uses a structured scaffold: a paragraph frame on the worksheet with sentence starters and required elements checklist (✓ greeting/introduction, ✓ description of place using 3 adjectives, ✓ cultural observation with weil-clause, ✓ personal reaction using fühlen/überraschen/beeindrucken, ✓ comparison with Vietnam, ✓ conclusion/recommendation). Vietnamese learner note: teacher explicitly reminds learners that German blog writing requires a clear topic sentence per paragraph—different from Vietnamese narrative styles that often build context before the main point. Learners write for 10 minutes, then swap with a partner who uses a peer-edit checklist (grammar, vocabulary range, connectors). Teacher collects for written feedback.
materials: Writing scaffold worksheet with paragraph frame and checklist
Model blog entry (the Swiss blog from reading task as mentor text)

activities.title: Exit Ticket: 3-2-1 Reflexion
activities.description: Each learner completes a structured 3-2-1 exit ticket on a half-sheet: 3 new vocabulary words they learned today and will use again, 2 things they found interesting or surprising about German/DACH travel culture, 1 grammar question they still have about Perfekt vs. Präteritum or comparative structures. Teacher collects tickets, reads grammar questions before next session to address persistent gaps, and uses vocabulary selections to gauge retention for spaced repetition planning. Tickets can be stored in learner portfolios.

lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Perfekt vs. Präteritum in travel narratives (spoken vs. written register distinction); Komparativ und Superlativ for intercultural comparisons (größer als, genauso … wie, anders als, am interessantesten); Modal particles doch, eigentlich, ja for nuancing opinions in intercultural contexts
lesson_plans.cultural_note: DACH cultural specifics relevant to this week: (1) Germany: Punctuality (Pünktlichkeit) is a deeply ingrained social value—being late is considered disrespectful; Vietnamese learners often note contrast with flexible time culture in Vietnam. (2) Austria: Coffee house (Kaffeehaus) culture in Vienna is UNESCO-listed intangible heritage—a social institution for hours-long conversation, not just drinking coffee; very different from Vietnamese café culture. (3) Switzerland: Strict recycling and noise regulations (Ruhezeiten: no loud noise after 10pm, no laundry on Sundays in some cantons)—can be surprising for newcomers. General DACH: Direct communication style (saying 'no' clearly) vs. Vietnamese indirect communication preference—a common source of intercultural misunderstanding worth explicit classroom discussion.

homework.description: Learners complete and expand their travel blog entry written in class, bringing it to 180–200 words. They also complete a structured vocabulary review exercise and watch a short video.
exercises: Expand the in-class blog entry to 180–200 words, incorporating at least 8 vocabulary words from this week's target list and at least 2 comparative structures. Use the paragraph frame scaffold if needed.
Complete vocabulary exercise sheet: 10 gap-fill sentences using this week's target vocabulary in context (sentences themed around travel and intercultural situations in DACH countries).

Watch the 4-minute YouTube clip 'Kulturschock Deutschland – Was ist anders?' (teacher-provided link or QR code) and note down 3 cultural differences mentioned. Write 2 sentences comparing one of them to Vietnamese culture.
Spaced repetition review: Using Quizlet set 'B1 Woche 13 – Reisen & Kultur' (teacher-prepared), complete one study session of at least 10 minutes using the Learn mode.

formative: Teacher observation checklist during pair speaking activity (Session 2, Activity 1): noting correct Perfekt/Präteritum usage, vocabulary range, and ability to maintain conversation for 2 minutes
Exit ticket 3-2-1 analysis: vocabulary retention check and identification of persistent grammar questions for next session remediation
Peer-edit feedback quality during writing task: teacher monitors whether learners can identify grammar and vocabulary issues in peers' texts
Listening task worksheet (Session 1, Activity 3): T/F/NM answers and gapped summary scored informally to gauge comprehension level
Vocabulary card sorting task: teacher circulates to identify learners who struggle with semantic categorisation for immediate micro-support
assessment.summative: End-of-week written assessment (completed as homework, submitted next session): A 180–200 word travel blog entry describing a real or imagined intercultural experience in a German-speaking country. Assessed using a B1-adapted rubric across 4 criteria: (1) Task achievement and content (intercultural observation included, appropriate length) – 25 points; (2) Vocabulary range and accuracy (min. 8 target words used correctly) – 25 points; (3) Grammar accuracy (Perfekt/Präteritum use, comparative structures, subordinate clauses) – 25 points; (4) Coherence and cohesion (connectors, paragraph structure, register appropriate for blog) – 25 points. Total: 100 points. Pass threshold: 60 points (B1 standard).

differentiation.struggling_learners: Provide a fully pre-labelled vocabulary card set so sorting is confirmation rather than discovery. Offer a more detailed writing scaffold with sentence-level starters for each required element (not just paragraph-level). During speaking activities, allow struggling learners to use their vocabulary reference card openly. For listening, provide a simplified transcript with key vocabulary glossed in Vietnamese for first listen only. Pair struggling learners with a supportive peer rather than the teacher to reduce anxiety. Provide a simplified grammar summary card with only Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip II) rules and a model conjugation table, deferring Präteritum focus to grammar consolidation. After class: offer a 10-minute optional grammar clinic on Perfekt formation.
differentiation.advanced_learners: Extend writing task to 250 words with the requirement to include a second perspective (e.g., what a local German speaker might think of the Vietnamese student's reaction). Add a challenge card during reading task: rewrite two sentences using Konjunktiv II to speculate (e.g., 'Wenn ich in der Schweiz wäre, würde ich …'). During speaking, remove the question bank card and require spontaneous follow-up questions. Assign additional homework: find an authentic German travel blog post online (e.g., on reiseblog.de or similar), summarise it in 5 bullet points in German, and identify 3 intercultural observations. Provide access to a B2 vocabulary extension list of 10 additional nuanced terms (e.g., die Ambivalenz, das Vorurteil, die Stereotypisierung, die Assimilation).

review_from_previous: Week 10–11 grammar: Konjunktiv II for hypothetical situations (Wenn ich Zeit hätte…) – reactivated in travel wishlist context
Week 8 vocabulary: Wohnen und Alltag – recycled via comparison of daily routines in Germany vs. Vietnam
Week 6 grammar: Weil- and obwohl-clauses – required for expressing reasons and concessions in travel narratives
Week 4 vocabulary: Adjektivdeklination – recycled in descriptive writing about travel destinations
Week 12 topic: Arbeit und Beruf – bridged via 'Dienstreisen' (business travel) warm-up connection
spaced_repetition.preview_next_week: Week 14 will focus on 'Medien & digitale Kommunikation'. This week's blog-writing skill directly prepares learners for Week 14's digital text types (social media posts, online reviews, emails). The vocabulary of expressing opinions and reactions (beeindrucken, überraschen, faszinieren) will recur in the context of media consumption and digital experiences. The intercultural reflection lens will be extended to examine how digital communication norms differ between German-speaking and Vietnamese contexts.

learning_objectives: Can discuss and articulate aspects of cultural identity, including national, regional, and personal identity, using complex sentence structures and nuanced vocabulary in German.
Can read and critically analyse authentic texts (newspaper articles, essays) about cultural identity in German-speaking countries and express opinions with supporting arguments.
Can write a structured argumentative essay (250–300 words) discussing the challenges and opportunities of multicultural identity, using appropriate discourse markers and cohesive devices.
prerequisite_knowledge: Solid command of B1 grammar: subordinate clauses, modal verbs, Konjunktiv II for hypothetical statements
Familiarity with basic vocabulary related to society, family, and everyday life
Ability to express and justify simple opinions using phrases such as 'Ich finde, dass…', 'Meiner Meinung nach…'
Basic knowledge of German-speaking countries (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) and their geographic diversity
Reading comprehension of B1-level texts with occasional unknown vocabulary

sessions.title: Was bin ich? – Annäherung an kulturelle Identität

activities.title: Identitätskarte – Wer bin ich?
activities.description: Each learner receives a blank 'Identitätskarte' (identity card template). They write 5–8 words or short phrases that describe their identity (e.g. nationality, profession, hobbies, values, family role). In pairs, learners share and compare their cards. The teacher facilitates a brief open-class discussion: 'Welche Aspekte eurer Identität sind durch Kultur geprägt?' This activates prior knowledge and connects learners personally to the topic. Teacher writes key terms from the discussion on the board as a living word cloud. Vietnamese learners are encouraged to reflect on Vietnamese cultural identity markers and how they might translate or relate to German contexts.
materials: Blank Identitätskarte handout (A5 card with outline)

activities.title: Wortfeld: Kulturelle Identität
activities.description: Teacher introduces 15 target vocabulary items using a structured vocabulary map projected on screen. Words are grouped into thematic clusters: (1) Identity terms – die Identität, die Zugehörigkeit, die Herkunft, das Erbe, die Wurzeln; (2) Cultural concepts – die Leitkultur, die Multikulturalität, die Integration, die Assimilation, die Akkulturation; (3) Adjectives – geprägt, verwurzelt, entwurzelt, vielfältig, fremd. For each word, teacher provides: pronunciation, part of speech, example sentence in context, and a Vietnamese cultural equivalent or contrast where appropriate (e.g. 'die Herkunft' parallels the Vietnamese concept of 'quê hương'). Learners complete a gapped vocabulary map handout, filling in definitions, collocations, and example sentences. Peer-check in pairs.

activities.title: Textarbeit: 'Was macht unsere Identität aus?'
activities.description: Learners read an adapted authentic text (approx. 350 words) excerpted from a German magazine article discussing what shapes cultural identity – language, customs, values, and lived experience. The text is structured in three paragraphs: (1) definition and components of cultural identity, (2) the role of migration and globalisation in shaping hybrid identities, (3) the concept of 'Heimat' in the DACH context. Task sequence: (a) Pre-reading – learners predict content from headline and three images shown on screen (2 min); (b) Global reading – learners read once and identify the main idea of each paragraph (3 min); (c) Detailed reading – learners answer 5 comprehension questions requiring inference and interpretation, not just retrieval (5 min); (d) Vocabulary in context – learners identify 3 target vocabulary items in the text and explain meaning from context (3 min). Vietnamese learner note: The concept of 'Heimat' is discussed in contrast with the Vietnamese concept of 'quê hương' to build intercultural competence.

activities.title: Relativsätze mit Präpositionen – Identität beschreiben
activities.description: Teacher draws learners' attention to two example sentences from the reading text that use prepositional relative clauses (Relativsätze mit Präpositionen), e.g. 'Die Kultur, in der ich aufgewachsen bin, prägt meine Identität.' and 'Das Land, aus dem meine Familie stammt, ist Teil meiner Identität.' Teacher explains the structure on the board: preposition + relative pronoun (dative/accusative). Learners complete 6 gap-fill sentences by choosing the correct preposition and relative pronoun. Then learners write 3 original sentences about their own cultural identity using this structure. Partners check each other's sentences for agreement and preposition choice. Teacher monitors and gives corrective feedback.

sessions.title: Identität im Diskurs – Argumentieren und Schreiben

activities.title: Podcast-Ausschnitt: 'Zwischen zwei Kulturen'
activities.description: Learners listen to an authentic or semi-authentic podcast excerpt (approx. 3–4 minutes) in which a young German-Vietnamese person (second generation immigrant) talks about navigating dual cultural identity in Germany. The audio is played twice. Task 1 (Global – first listening): Learners note answers to three questions: Who is speaking? What is the main topic? What is the speaker's overall attitude? Task 2 (Detailed – second listening): Learners complete a structured note-taking grid with four categories: (a) challenges of dual identity, (b) positive aspects, (c) family expectations, (d) the role of language. Post-listening discussion in small groups: 'Kannst du dich mit diesem Erlebnis identifizieren? Welche Gemeinsamkeiten gibt es zwischen vietnamesischer und deutsch-vietnamesischer Identitätserfahrung?' This activity is specifically chosen to maximise relevance for Vietnamese adult learners and build empathy and personal connection to the topic.

activities.title: Podiumsdiskussion: Leitkultur – Chance oder Bedrohung?
activities.description: Class is divided into three groups of approximately equal size. Each group is assigned a position: (A) Pro Leitkultur – a common cultural framework strengthens social cohesion; (B) Contra Leitkultur – imposing a dominant culture threatens minority identities; (C) Moderatoren – they prepare 4–5 discussion questions and moderate the debate. Groups have 5 minutes to prepare arguments using a provided argument framework card (Argumentationskarte) with sentence starters: 'Einerseits … andererseits …', 'Man könnte argumentieren, dass …', 'Ein überzeugender Punkt ist …', 'Dagegen spricht jedoch …'. The debate runs for 8 minutes with moderators guiding the discussion. Teacher monitors for language accuracy, notes common errors for delayed feedback. After the debate, the whole class reflects: 'Welche Argumente waren am überzeugendsten und warum?' Teacher provides delayed oral feedback on grammar and vocabulary use observed during the debate.

activities.title: Erörterung vorbereiten: 'Kulturelle Vielfalt – Bereicherung oder Herausforderung?'
activities.description: Learners are guided through the planning phase of a B2-level argumentative essay (Erörterung). Teacher models essay structure on the board: Einleitung (hook + thesis statement), Hauptteil (2–3 argument paragraphs, each with: Argument – Beispiel/Belege – Schlussfolgerung), Schluss (summary + personal position + outlook). Learners individually complete a structured planning template: they write a thesis statement, list 3 main arguments with evidence or examples from the session's discussions and readings, and note appropriate discourse markers (Darüber hinaus, Zwar … aber …, Insgesamt lässt sich sagen …). Learners share plans in pairs and give constructive peer feedback using a checklist: (1) Is the thesis clear? (2) Are arguments logical and supported? (3) Are discourse markers varied? The essay itself is assigned as homework to ensure adequate writing time.

activities.title: Exit Ticket: Drei Dinge, die ich gelernt habe
activities.description: In the final 6 minutes, each learner completes a structured exit ticket on a sticky note or digital form: (1) 'Ein neues Wort, das ich heute gelernt habe:' (2) 'Eine Grammatikstruktur, die ich heute geübt habe:' (3) 'Eine Frage, die ich noch habe:'. Learners stick notes on the board or submit digitally. Teacher quickly reviews responses to identify gaps for the next session or homework follow-up. This also reinforces metacognitive awareness and encourages self-monitoring of learning – particularly effective for adult Vietnamese learners who respond well to structured self-reflection.
materials: Sticky notes or digital exit ticket form (e.g. Google Form)

vocabulary_target: geprägt sein von (to be shaped by)
lesson_plans.grammar_focus: Relativsätze mit Präpositionen (Prepositional Relative Clauses) – e.g. 'Die Kultur, in der ich aufgewachsen bin, …' / 'Das Land, aus dem ich stamme, …'. Learners practise forming relative clauses with two-way prepositions and prepositions governing dative and accusative, focusing on correct relative pronoun agreement in gender, number, and case. This structure is essential for nuanced discussion of cultural identity at B2 level.
lesson_plans.cultural_note: The concept of 'Heimat' is central to German-speaking cultural identity and has no direct English or Vietnamese equivalent. It combines notions of home, belonging, landscape, and emotional rootedness. In Germany, the term has complex historical connotations (including misuse during the Nazi era) and is experiencing a renaissance in contemporary debates about migration, national identity, and globalisation. The Austrian federal state ministry 'Bundesministerium für Heimat' reflects its ongoing political resonance. In Switzerland, the multilingual national identity (German, French, Italian, Romansh) provides an excellent model of a pluricultural identity within one nation. For Vietnamese learners, a meaningful parallel is the concept of 'quê hương' (homeland/native village), which similarly carries deep emotional and ancestral significance. Comparing these concepts builds intercultural competence and helps learners internalise the German vocabulary through culturally meaningful anchors.

homework.description: Learners write a full argumentative essay (Erörterung) of 250–300 words on the topic: 'Kulturelle Vielfalt in Deutschland – Bereicherung oder Herausforderung? Nehmen Sie Stellung.' Learners should use: (1) the essay structure practised in class (Einleitung, Hauptteil, Schluss), (2) at least 8 target vocabulary items from the week's list, (3) at least 3 discourse markers for argumentation, (4) at least 2 prepositional relative clauses. Essays should be submitted before the next lesson for teacher feedback (written or via annotated digital document).
exercises: Write a 250–300 word argumentative essay: 'Kulturelle Vielfalt in Deutschland – Bereicherung oder Herausforderung?'
Review and self-correct using the peer feedback checklist from class
Look up one additional authentic source (German newspaper article) on cultural identity and note 3 new vocabulary items with definitions
Prepare to briefly summarise your essay argument in 2–3 spoken sentences for the next class warm-up

formative: Observation of pair and group discussion quality during Identitätskarte and Podiumsdiskussion activities – teacher uses a simple observation checklist tracking: vocabulary use, grammar accuracy (especially prepositional relative clauses), fluency, and argumentation quality
Vocabulary map gap-fill exercise – peer-corrected in class; teacher reviews for patterns of error
